assumption: w16b holds the same low byte as w16 throughout (the routine sets w16b = w16 and w16b+1 = w16+1 - >RINGBYTES, and RINGBYTES = 80*28*8 = $4600, whole pages -- the source comment says so). Saving is per character copied; ~160 chars/call is possible, so this is ~6000 cycles/call at the top end. Byte cost is +24.
original:
@cp:    ldy #7
:       lda (w16),y
        sta (w16b),y
        dey
        bpl :-
        lda w16
        clc
        adc #8
        sta w16
        bcc :+
        inc w16+1
:       lda w16b
        clc
        adc #8
        sta w16b
        bcc :+
        inc w16b+1
:       dex
        bne @cp
proposal:
@cp:    ldaz w16                    ; lda (w16)   -- line 0 needs no index
        staz w16b                   ; sta (w16b)
        ldy #1
        lda (w16),y
        sta (w16b),y
        iny
        lda (w16),y
        sta (w16b),y
        iny
        lda (w16),y
        sta (w16b),y
        iny
        lda (w16),y
        sta (w16b),y
        iny
        lda (w16),y
        sta (w16b),y
        iny
        lda (w16),y
        sta (w16b),y
        iny
        lda (w16),y                 ; y = 7
        sta (w16b),y
        lda w16                     ; w16b tracks w16 in the low byte: one add serves both
        clc
        adc #8
        sta w16
        sta w16b
        bcc :+
        inc w16+1
        inc w16b+1
:       dex
        bne @cp
argument:
Two independent changes, both inside the character loop.

(a) Unroll the 8-byte copy. Present cost: ldy #7 (2) + 8 x [lda (w16),y 5 + sta (w16b),y 6 + dey 2] = 104 + 7 taken bpl (21) + 1 fallthrough (2) = 129. Unrolled: line 0 uses the 65C02 non-indexed forms, lda (w16) 5 + sta (w16b) 5 = 10; ldy #1 (2); seven [lda (w16),y 5 + sta (w16b),y 6] = 77 with six iny between (12) = 101. Saving 28. Ordering: the copy now runs 0..7 instead of 7..0, which only matters if source and destination overlap -- they cannot, w16b is a whole $4600 below w16. Page crossing on lda (w16),y is unchanged between the two versions (same base, same offsets), and sta (zp),y is 6 regardless. Y is left at 7 instead of $FF; nothing after the loop (the pointer adds, dex/bne, and @done's four pla/sta) reads Y, and @cp reloads it on every pass. X is untouched.

(b) Merge the two pointer advances. w16b+1 = w16+1 - $46 and w16b = w16 are established before @cp and both are stepped by the same 8 every pass, so the low bytes are equal for the life of the loop and the carry out of 'adc #8' is the same for both. One lda/clc/adc feeds two stores: 3+2+2+3+3+3 = 16 cycles against 13+13 = 26 (no-carry path), 22 against 34 on the carry path. Saving 10 (12 on a carry). The two inc's on the carry path preserve the pairing. Flags: the block ends with dex/bne, which set their own N,Z; the inc's N,Z are dead, exactly as before.

Total 38 cycles per character, 160 -> 122. Bytes 34 -> 58, i.e. +24.

*** ANONYMOUS LABELS -- FLAG *** this block currently contains three ':' lines (the loop head, and the two carry targets); the rewrite leaves one. I checked engine.s: the only ':-' reference between here and the end of the routine is the loop's own 'bpl :-', which goes away, and the next backward reference in the file ('bne :--' at line 2447 in @advance) counts back to two labels inside its own block. The preceding 'bcs :+ / sta tmp4 / :' pair is a forward reference resolved before @cp. So the change is safe as the file stands today, but it must be re-checked if it is applied on top of other edits.

assumption: Y and A are dead at the loop exit (they are: the next instruction is `lda w16`, and Y is reloaded by `ldy #7` at @cp on the next pass), and 32 extra bytes are affordable in the LOGIC bank.
original:
@cp:    ldy #7
:       lda (w16),y
        sta (w16b),y
        dey
        bpl :-
proposal:
@cp:    ldy #7
        lda (w16),y
        sta (w16b),y
        dey
        lda (w16),y
        sta (w16b),y
        dey
        lda (w16),y
        sta (w16b),y
        dey
        lda (w16),y
        sta (w16b),y
        dey
        lda (w16),y
        sta (w16b),y
        dey
        lda (w16),y
        sta (w16b),y
        dey
        lda (w16),y
        sta (w16b),y
        dey
        lda (w16),y
        sta (w16b),y
argument: The trip count is a compile-time constant 8 (`ldy #7` down to 0 via `bpl`), so the loop control is pure overhead. Original: `ldy #7` 2, then 8 bodies of `lda (w16),y` 5 + `sta (w16b),y` 6 + `dey` 2 = 104, plus 7 taken `bpl` at 3 and one not-taken at 2 = 2 + 104 + 21 + 2 = 129 cycles. Unrolled: 2 + 8*(5+6) + 7*2 = 2 + 88 + 14 = 104 cycles. Saving 25 cycles per char copied, at a cost of 32 bytes (9 bytes becomes 41). No page-cross penalty differs between the two: w16 is set from MIRR_LO and stepped by 8 from a char boundary, so its low byte is a multiple of 8 and 248+7 = 255 never crosses; the loads are 5 cycles in both forms. Correctness: the final `dey` is dropped, so the loop exits with Y = 0 instead of $FF and with Z=1/N=0 instead of Z=0/N=1. Both are dead - the next instruction is `lda w16`, which overwrites A and the flags, and Y is reloaded by `ldy #7` when control returns to @cp from `dex / bne @cp`. A also holds byte 0 in both versions. WARNING on anonymous labels: this deletes the `:` line in front of `lda (w16),y` together with the `bpl :-` that references it. I checked the rest of mirror_run (engine.s 2190-2227): the only `:-` in the routine is that `bpl`, and every other reference is a forward `:+` that resolves to a `:` placed after this point, so nothing is retargeted. Still, re-check the assembly listing after the edit. If 32 bytes is too much, a 2x unroll (`lda/sta/dey/lda/sta/dey/bpl :-`, 4 trips) costs only 8 extra bytes and still saves 14 cycles.

assumption: @fslow/@fsc is worth 17 extra bytes in drawrect (segment CODE, main RAM). The unrolled form must keep a bare ':' label line where the loop's ':' was, or every anonymous-label reference in drawrect that counts past it is retargeted.
original:
@fsc:   lda tp
        ldy #7
:       sta (sp),y
        dey
        bpl :-
        spnext
        dec tmp2
        bne @fsc
proposal:
@fsc:   lda tp
        ldy #7
        sta (sp),y
        dey
        sta (sp),y
        dey
        sta (sp),y
        dey
        sta (sp),y
        dey
        sta (sp),y
        dey
        sta (sp),y
        dey
        sta (sp),y
        staz sp                     ; line 0 non-indexed
:                                   ; KEPT, unreferenced, so the anonymous-label
                                    ; count through drawrect is unchanged
        spnext
        dec tmp2
        bne @fsc
argument: The @f7 block six lines above is exactly this fill, already unrolled (FIL1 7 + 6x FILN + staz sp); @fslow re-rolls it. Loop cost: lda tp 3 + ldy #7 2 + 8 iterations of sta (sp),y 6 / dey 2 / bpl 3 (taken 7 times, 2 on the last, since dey from 0 gives $FF and clears the branch) = 3+2+64+23 = 92. Unrolled cost: lda tp 3 + ldy #7 2 + sta (sp),y 6 + 6x(dey 2 + sta (sp),y 6) = 48 + staz sp 5 = 64. Saving 28 cycles per char row. Correctness: the store order is y=7 down to y=1 then (sp) non-indexed for y=0, identical to the loop's 7..0; staz sp is 'sta (sp)' (65C02, 5 cycles) and is what @f7 already uses for line 0. Y ends at 1 instead of $FF -- Y is reloaded by the next FIL1/ldy on every path out of here and spnext does not read Y, but that is the one register difference, so it is an assumption. Flags: the loop left N=1/Z=0 from the final dey; the unrolled form leaves the flags of 'ldy #7' untouched by the stores (sta sets no flags), so flags differ -- the next instruction is spnext, whose first act is 'lda sp', so no flag is consumed. Bytes: +17. Cheaper compromise if the space matters: unroll by two only (sta/dey/sta/dey/bpl :-, 4 iterations) for 80 cycles, i.e. 12 saved for +3 bytes.

assumption: @fjmp must not be a branch/jump target from anywhere else (i.e. the patched jmp is never re-executed without being re-patched), and A must be dead at @g2/@g4/@g6 -- @g2 immediately does `ldy #2 / lda (sp),y`, so that holds for the one target visible in the window.
original:
asl
        tax
        lda @ftab,x
        sta @fjmp+1
        lda @ftab+1,x
        sta @fjmp+2
@fjmp:  jmp @g2                     ; operand patched: @g2/@g4/@g6
@ftab:  .word @g2, @g4, @g6
proposal:
asl
        tax
        jmpx @ftab                  ; jmp (@ftab,x)
@ftab:  .word @g2, @g4, @g6
argument: This is an NMOS-era self-modifying dispatch; the 65C02 has jmp (abs,x) and the codebase already wraps it as the `jmpx` macro (used by SPRFULL/SPRHALF). Cycle count, original: asl A 2, tax 2, lda abs,x 4, sta abs 4, lda abs,x 4, sta abs 4, jmp abs 3 = 23. Proposed: asl A 2, tax 2, jmp (abs,x) 6 = 10. Saving 13 cycles. Bytes: 1+1+3+3+3+3+3 = 17 vs 1+1+3 = 5, saving 12. Correctness: X is identical in both (asl A then tax gives 0/2/4, exactly the byte offset into the .word table that both the patch and jmp (abs,x) index with). @ftab is unchanged and still needed. Flags: the original leaves flags from `sta` (i.e. from `lda @ftab+1,x`, the target high byte); the proposal leaves flags from `tax`. Both targets begin with `ldy #n`, which reloads N/Z, so flags are dead across the jump. A differs (target high byte vs index*2) and is likewise overwritten at the target. No anonymous labels are added or removed -- @fjmp is a cheap-local named label, and the only references to it are the two patch stores that disappear with it.

assumption: Space in the LOW2 segment for +7 bytes per TOBANK trampoline (13 of them, +91 bytes total). pagelogic itself must stay, because TOMAIN still jmps to it.
original:
pagelogic:
        pha
        lda #BANK_LVL
        sta ROMSEL_CPY
        sta ROMSEL
        pla
        rts
.macro TOBANK n
.ident(.concat("t_", n)):
        jsr pagelogic
        jmp .ident(n)
.endmacro
proposal:
.macro TOBANK n
.ident(.concat("t_", n)):
        pha
        lda #BANK_LVL
        sta ROMSEL_CPY
        sta ROMSEL
        pla
        jmp .ident(n)
.endmacro
argument: TOBANK pays jsr pagelogic 6 + pha 3 + lda # 2 + sta abs 4 + sta abs 4 + pla 4 + rts 6 + jmp 3 = 32 cycles of pure ceremony before the target runs. Inlining the five-instruction switch into the trampoline drops the jsr (6) and the rts (6) and keeps the jmp: 3+2+4+4+4+3 = 20. Saving 12 cycles per t_ entry. Correctness: identical instruction sequence, so A is preserved across the pha/pla exactly as before; X, Y and C are never touched by any of these instructions (pha/pla do not affect flags on the 65C02, and neither does sta); the jsr/rts pair that is removed also preserved nothing else. ROMSEL_CPY is written before ROMSEL in both. No anonymous labels involved. TOMAIN is already optimal -- its 'jmp pagelogic' is a tail jump, so inlining there would buy only the jmp's 3 cycles for the same +7 bytes and is not worth it. Cost: 13 TOBANK instantiations x 7 bytes = 91 bytes in LOW2 ($0206..$03FF).

assumption: Applies to the mirror=1 instantiation of SPRLINE2 only. X still holds the source byte at the point of use (nothing between tax and the two ora's touches it), and IDENT is page aligned ($0600 from the TABLES segment at $0400) so IDENT+$80,x with the x<$80 codes the mirror path ever looks up never crosses a page: 4 cycles, not 5.
original:
tax
        lda MASKTAB+$80,x
        beq opaque
        sta tmp4
.if mirror
        lda IDENT+$80,x
        sta tmp3
.else
        stx tmp3
.endif
        ...
        lda (sp),y
        and tmp4
        ora tmp3
        sta (sp),y
        iny
        lda (sp),y
        and tmp4
        ora tmp3
        sta (sp),y
proposal:
tax
        lda MASKTAB+$80,x
        beq opaque
        sta tmp4
.if .not mirror
        stx tmp3
.endif
        ...
        lda (sp),y
        and tmp4
.if mirror
        ora IDENT+$80,x
.else
        ora tmp3
.endif
        sta (sp),y
        iny
        lda (sp),y
        and tmp4
.if mirror
        ora IDENT+$80,x
.else
        ora tmp3
.endif
        sta (sp),y
argument: Mirror path only. Original: lda IDENT+$80,x (4) + sta tmp3 (3) + ora tmp3 (3) + ora tmp3 (3) = 13 cycles, 9 bytes. Proposal folds the table read into each use: ora IDENT+$80,x (4) twice = 8 cycles, 6 bytes. Saving 5 cycles, 3 bytes per masked byte drawn by a mirrored half-res sprite. Correctness: X is set by the tax three instructions earlier and is not written again anywhere on this path (lda/and/ora/sta/iny only), so IDENT+$80,x reads exactly the byte that was stashed in tmp3. Page cross: MASKTAB=$0400, SWAPTAB=$0500, IDENT=$0600 (TABLES loads at $0400), and engine.s line 2799 states only codes < $80 are ever looked up in the +$80 halves, so IDENT+$80+x stays inside $0680..$06FF - no +1 penalty. Flags: the value left in A at 'skip' is identical ((sp),y AND tmp4 OR IDENT[x]) in both versions, and the flags are those of the final ora in both, so the fall-through to 'skip' is unchanged. tmp3 is left unwritten, but no path out of SPRLINE2 sets it either (both/opaque/skip do not), so no caller can be relying on it. Deliberately NOT applied to the .else branch: replacing stx tmp3 with ora IDENT,x would save only 1 cycle and is not semantically identical - build_tables zeroes IDENT+$41, IDENT+$44 and IDENT+$82, so IDENT[x] != x for three codes.

assumption: low(w16) == low(w16b) throughout the @cp loop. This holds by construction: the setup immediately above the loop is `lda w16 / sta w16b / lda w16+1 / sec / sbc #>RINGBYTES / sta w16b+1` -- the low byte is copied verbatim, and the source comment says so ('RINGBYTES is whole pages, so the low byte holds'). Both pointers then advance by the same +8 every iteration, so the low bytes stay equal and the carries out of the two low-byte adds are always identical.
original:
sta w16
        bcc :+
        inc w16+1
:       lda w16b
        clc
        adc #8
        sta w16b
        bcc :+
        inc w16b+1
:       dex
        bne @cp
proposal:
sta w16
        sta w16b                    ; w16b tracks w16 exactly in the low byte
        bcc :+
        inc w16+1
        inc w16b+1
:
:       dex
        bne @cp
argument: The loop maintains two pointers that differ by a constant whole number of pages, so the second 16-bit add is pure duplication. The new low byte, already in A from the `adc #8`, is stored to both pointers (`sta w16` 3 + `sta w16b` 3), and the single carry test serves both high bytes. Common case (no carry out of the low add): old = sta 3 + bcc taken 3 + lda w16b 3 + clc 2 + adc 2 + sta 3 + bcc taken 3 = 19; new = sta 3 + sta 3 + bcc taken 3 = 9, so 10 cycles saved per char copied. Carry case: old = 3 + bcc not taken 2 + inc zp 5 + 3 + 2 + 2 + 3 + 2 + 5 = 27; new = 3 + 3 + 2 + 5 + 5 = 18, 9 saved. The loop runs up to 160 times per mirror_run call, so this is worth up to ~1600 cycles a call. Bytes: 11 removed (lda zp 2, clc 1, adc# 2, sta zp 2, bcc 2, inc zp 2) against 4 added (sta zp 2, inc zp 2) = 7 saved. Correctness: `sta` sets no flags, so the carry from `adc #8` survives to the `bcc`; `inc w16+1` sets N/Z but nothing between there and `dex` reads them, and `dex` sets its own flags for the `bne`. ANONYMOUS LABELS: the rewrite naturally removes one `:` line, which would silently retarget any `:+`/`:-` that counts past this point, so the proposal deliberately keeps two consecutive `:` label lines (legal in ca65, both resolve to the same address) to hold the file's anonymous-label count exactly as it was. Do not collapse them into one.

assumption: CHARPER's trailing `jmp next` is macro-generated, so realising this needs a macro variant (extra parameter, or CHARPER 0 written out inline at @p0). No register or scratch assumption.
original:
@p0:    CHARPER 0, @advsp
@advsp: lda sp
        clc
        adc tmp
        sta sp
        bcc :++
        lda sp+1
        inca
proposal:
@p0:    CHARPER_F 0            ; same as CHARPER 0 but WITHOUT the trailing `jmp next`
@advsp: lda sp
        clc
        adc tmp
        sta sp
        bcc :++
        lda sp+1
        inca
argument: CHARPER ends with `jmp next`. At the @p0 site next = @advsp, and @advsp is literally the next address in the listing (nothing sits between `@p0: CHARPER 0, @advsp` and `@advsp: lda sp`). So the emitted jmp transfers control to the instruction that would have been reached by falling through: 3 cycles and 3 bytes for nothing. Deleting it is control-flow identical. Flags: jmp sets none, fall-through sets none, so @advsp sees exactly the flags CHARPER's final `sta (sp),y` left in both cases (sta sets none, so really the flags from the preceding `lda (tp),y`). No anonymous labels are involved. The other three CHARPER sites (@p3->@b23, @p2->@b15, @p1->@b7) genuinely need their jmp and are untouched. I looked for a bigger win -- making the hot `jmp @advsp` after `@b7: CHARCPY 0, @t0` a fall-through by moving @t0/@t1/@p0..@p3 -- but @b15 is fallen into from the block above it (@b23), so the @b* chain cannot be broken from inside this window; verdict on that part is none.

assumption: None for correctness. The trade is cycles for bytes: +30 bytes across the two loops. If space is tighter than that, a 2x unroll gives 96 cycles for +12 bytes instead.
original:
ldy #31
:       lda (w16),y
        sta (ptr),y
        dey
        bpl :-
        add16i w16, 32
        add16i ptr, 640
        ldy #31
:       lda (w16),y
        sta (ptr),y
        dey
        bpl :-
proposal:
ldy #31
:       lda (w16),y
        sta (ptr),y
        dey
        lda (w16),y
        sta (ptr),y
        dey
        lda (w16),y
        sta (ptr),y
        dey
        lda (w16),y
        sta (ptr),y
        dey
        bpl :-
        add16i w16, 32
        add16i ptr, 640
        ldy #31
:       lda (w16),y
        sta (ptr),y
        dey
        lda (w16),y
        sta (ptr),y
        dey
        lda (w16),y
        sta (ptr),y
        dey
        lda (w16),y
        sta (ptr),y
        dey
        bpl :-
argument: Each copy moves a fixed 32 bytes and spends 5 of its 16 cycles per byte on loop overhead (`dey` 2 + `bpl` 3). Unrolling 4x amortises the branch over four bytes: body = 4*(lda (zp),y 5 + sta (zp),y 6 + dey 2) + bpl 3 = 55 per four bytes against 64, i.e. 9 saved per group, 8 groups = 72 per loop, 144 for the two loops. 32 divides exactly by 4, so Y runs 31..28, 27..24, ... 3..0 and ends at $FF with the eighth `bpl` not taken, exactly as before -- no partial group and no change to the terminating condition. Flags: `bpl` still reads the `dey` immediately before it, which is what the original tested. Registers: only A and Y, same as before, and Y's exit value ($FF) is identical. Anonymous labels: unchanged, one `:` per loop, and each `bpl :-` still resolves to its own loop head. The two `add16i` calls between the loops are untouched. Note that `add16i w16, 32` could also be shortened to lda/clc/adc #32/sta/bcc/inc (13 cycles common, 17 worst, against a flat 18), but that inserts a fresh anonymous label between the two loops, so I have left it out of the proposal.

assumption: A is free at routine entry (the existing loop already clobbers it with lda q1 every iteration) and q1's only readers during the loop are the rol/lda being replaced. q1's entry value is the initial remainder, so it must be loaded once up front.
original:
ldx #16
@l:     asl t16
        rol t16+1
        rol q1
        lda q1
        cmp #10
        bcc :+
        sbc #10
        sta q1
        inc t16
:       dex
        bne @l
        rts
proposal:
ldx #16
        lda q1                  ; remainder lives in A for the whole loop
@l:     asl t16
        rol t16+1
        rol a                   ; was rol q1 / lda q1
        cmp #10
        bcc :+
        sbc #10                 ; was sbc #10 / sta q1
        inc t16
:       dex
        bne @l
        sta q1
        rts
argument: The running remainder never needs to be in memory inside the loop: rol q1 (5) + lda q1 (3) = 8 cy becomes rol a (2), and on the subtract path sta q1 (3) disappears too. inc t16 does not touch A, so the remainder survives it. Per iteration: 28->22 cy when the remainder is <10, 37->28 when it is not; x16 iterations minus 6 cy of lda/sta ceremony gives roughly 90-138 cy saved per call (~114 typical). Exit state is unchanged: A = final remainder = q1 in both versions, and the last flag-setting instruction is still dex (sta sets no flags), so Z=1/N=0 at the rts exactly as before. The single anonymous label is preserved in place. Byte count: -3 in the body, -2 for the dropped sta, +4 for the new lda/sta = -1.

assumption: Depends on three instructions just past the window, which I checked in engine.s: the loop tail is `sty w16 / inx / bra @div` and it ends `@dd: stx barq / rts`. Also assumes the remainder left in w16 is dead -- it is: the three callers (main.s:111, menu.s:189, engine.s:2587) never read w16 afterwards, and the only consumer of the modulus, mirror_seek at engine.s:2474, recomputes it as ringS - mulrowlo,barq. Y must be free (it is only the loop's own scratch here). ringS < RINGCHARS = 2240 after the fold above, so the high byte is 0..8 and X cannot run past 27.
original:
:       ; q = S / 80
        lda ringS
        sta w16
        lda ringS+1
        sta w16+1
        ldx #0
@div:   lda w16
        sec
        sbc #ROWCHARS
        tay
        lda w16+1
        sbc #0
        bcc @dd
        sta w16+1
        sty w16
        inx
        bra @div
@dd:    stx barq
        rts
proposal:
:       ; q = S / 80
        lda ringS                   ; running value: low in A, high in Y
        ldy ringS+1
        ldx #$FF                    ; quotient, pre-decremented
@div:   inx
        sec
        sbc #ROWCHARS
        bcs @div                    ; no borrow: high byte unchanged, value still >= 0
        dey
        bpl @div                    ; borrow absorbed by the high byte
@dd:    stx barq                    ; high byte went negative: X is the quotient
        rts
argument: Same repeated-subtraction division, with the 16-bit running value held in A (low) and Y (high) instead of round-tripping through w16 every step. Per successful subtraction the old body is lda w16 (3) + sec (2) + sbc #80 (2) + tay (2) + lda w16+1 (3) + sbc #0 (2) + bcc not taken (2) + sta w16+1 (3) + sty w16 (3) + inx (2) + bra (3) = 27 cycles; the new body is inx (2) + sec (2) + sbc #80 (2) + bcs taken (3) = 9 when the low byte does not borrow, and 13 when it does and the high byte absorbs it (add dey 2 and bpl taken 3, minus the 1 cycle the untaken bcs saves). Borrows fall every 256/80 ~ 3.2 steps, so the average is about 10 cycles against 27: roughly 17-18 cycles per quotient step. calc_ring runs once a frame with q = ringS/80 in 0..27, so the whole loop drops from 27q+17 to about 10q+12 -- around 250 cycles at a typical q = 14 and about 480 at q = 27. Correctness: X starts at $FF and is bumped before each attempt, so after the k-th `inx` X = k-1 and the value in A/Y is S - k*80; the loop leaves when that goes negative, at which point q = k-1 = X, which is what `stx barq` stores -- the same quotient the old code accumulated. `sec` is kept inside the loop because the borrow path leaves C = 0 (hoisting it would need a `clc`-style fixup and a `bra`, which costs more than it saves on the borrow arm). Negativity is detected by `dey` going 0 -> $FF and setting N: a low-byte borrow with Y >= 1 leaves a non-negative value and re-enters the loop, a borrow with Y = 0 is the terminating case. S = 0 terminates immediately with barq = 0; S = 80 gives 1; S = 300 gives 3 (checked by hand, including the Y = 1 -> 0 borrow on the first step). The anonymous `:` at the head is untouched -- the three `bcc :+`/`bne :+` branches in the fold above still resolve to it -- and no `:` line is added or removed anywhere. A and Y are dead at `@dd`, which only stores X and returns.

assumption: C = 0 on every entry to @advsp. Verified against the whole of drawrect: both dispatchers (`jmpx @jt-2` at line 546 and `jmpx @ft-2` at line 699) are reached either via `beq :+` with C cleared by the preceding `asl/asl` (rc_n <= 4, so 8*rc_n <= 32 never carries -- the source already comments on this) or via `bcc :+` after `cmp #>RINGEND`, which only branches with C = 0. Nothing on the paths from there to @advsp (CHARCPY / CHARPER / FIL1 / FILN and the `jmp @advsp` at 605 and 741) touches C: they are only lda/sta/ldy/iny/dey/bmi/jmp.
original:
@p0:    CHARPER 0, @advsp
@advsp: lda sp
        clc
        adc tmp
        sta sp
        bcc :++
        lda sp+1
        inca
        ringup
        sta sp+1
:
@runend:
        lda cnt
        sec
        sbc rc_n
        sta cnt
        beq @rowdone
        stz rc_subc
proposal:
@p0:    CHARPER 0, @advsp
@advsp: lda sp
        adc tmp                     ; C is already clear at every entry to @advsp
        sta sp
        bcc :++
        lda sp+1
        inca
        ringup
        sta sp+1
:
@runend:
        lda cnt
        sec
        sbc rc_n
        sta cnt
        beq @rowdone
        stz rc_subc
argument: The only change is deleting `clc` (2 cycles, 1 byte) from the per-run screen-pointer advance. `lda sp` does not disturb C, so `adc tmp` sees the carry that was live at the dispatch, which is 0 on all four routes into the unrolled blocks (see assumption). Everything downstream is unchanged: `sta sp` sets no flags, `bcc :++` still jumps past ringup's own anonymous label, and the anonymous-label count in the file is untouched (no `:` line added or removed). `sec` at @runend must stay -- @runend is also entered by `jmp @runend` from @slow (652) and @fslow (752), and the fall-through from @advsp can arrive with C = 1 out of ringup's `sbc`, so the carry there is genuinely unknown. This is the hottest window in the batch (once per run of <= 4 chars, for every char row of every rect), so 2 cycles is small but free.

assumption: No code preceding the SPRFULL expansions has an unresolved forward `:+` that currently binds to the `:` being deleted. Checked: SPRFULL/SPRLINE bodies use .local names everywhere else, the `solid:`/`name:`/`et:` prologue contains no anonymous labels, and the k=0 arm of SPRLINE is expanded exactly once per SPRFULL (as l0), so the only reference to this `:` is the `bcc :+` immediately above it.
original:
beq done                    ; 0: both pixels transparent, no store
        bpl masked                  ; (N from the load: cmp would set it from the subtraction)
        cmp #$C0
        bcc :+                      ; bit 7+6: this and the next 7 bytes all opaque
        jmp solid
:
        bra opaque
proposal:
beq done                    ; 0: both pixels transparent, no store
        bpl masked                  ; (N from the load: cmp would set it from the subtraction)
        cmp #$C0
        bcc opaque                  ; bit7 alone: single opaque byte
        jmp solid                   ; bit 7+6: this and the next 7 bytes all opaque
argument: LOUD FLAG (rule 3): this deletes one anonymous label. The `:` on its own line and the `bcc :+` that targets it both disappear, so the count of `:` in engine.s drops by one at this point in each of the three SPRFULL expansions. Everything that follows inside SPRLINE's k!=0 arm and the rest of drawsprite uses forward `:+` references that bind to labels defined after them, and there is no `:-` anywhere between line 1140 and line 1500, so nothing is silently retargeted; but it must be re-assembled and checked. Instruction by instruction: `cmp #$C0` is unchanged and still sets C from the unsigned compare (A is known >= $80 here because `beq done`/`bpl masked` have already filtered $00 and bit7-clear). Original: C clear (A in $80..$BF, the single-opaque-byte case) takes `bcc :+` = 3 cycles, lands on `bra opaque` = 3 more, total 6. New: `bcc opaque` taken = 3, total 3. Saving 3 cycles on the single-opaque path. C set (A >= $C0, run case): original `bcc` not taken 2 + `jmp solid` 3 = 5; new identical 5, no change. Branch range: from the byte after `bcc opaque`, `opaque` is 16 bytes forward in the unmirrored build (jmp solid 3, cmp #$41 2, beq blank 2, tax 1, lda MASKTAB,x 3, and (sp) 2, ora IDENT,x 3) and 18 in the mirrored build (extra `bra skip` 2) -- comfortably inside +127, and ca65 would raise a range error rather than mis-assemble if that ever changed. Flags: `bra` sets no flags and `bcc` sets no flags, so the state arriving at `opaque` (A = the source byte, N/Z from the original load, C from the cmp) is identical; `opaque` either falls into `staz sp` (unmirrored) or does `tax`/`lda SWAPTAB,x` (mirrored), neither of which reads C. Registers: unchanged, nothing new is clobbered. Bytes: cmp2+bcc2+jmp3+bra2 = 9 becomes cmp2+bcc2+jmp3 = 7.

assumption: @g4 and @g6 are the only entry points into this unrolled copy other than the top; no code branches to the `iny` itself. No register or scratch assumption (the rewrite only deletes instructions).
original:
lda (sp),y
        sta (ptr),y
        iny
@g4:    ldy #4
        lda (sp),y
        sta (ptr),y
        iny
@g6:    ldy #6
        lda (sp),y
        sta (ptr),y
proposal:
lda (sp),y
        sta (ptr),y
@g4:    ldy #4
        lda (sp),y
        sta (ptr),y
@g6:    ldy #6
        lda (sp),y
        sta (ptr),y
argument: Each 2-byte group ends `iny` and the next group starts `ldy #<even>`. On the fall-through path the iny writes Y=4 and the immediately following ldy #4 overwrites it with the same value; on the entry path (jump to @g4) the ldy is what sets Y. So the trailing iny has no reachable use of its result. Flags: iny sets N,Z from Y; ldy #imm immediately re-sets N,Z from the immediate, and nothing reads flags between the two instructions, so the deletion is flag-transparent. Cost: iny is 2 cycles / 1 byte; two of them are visible in this window (before @g4 and before @g6) = 4 cycles, 2 bytes. The same dead iny almost certainly precedes @g2 as well, for 2 more cycles outside the window. The only thing to check before applying is that no branch targets the iny rather than the label -- it does not, the label is on the ldy.

assumption: Y is dead after the inner loop (spnext clobbers only A and the flags; @runend reads cnt/rc_n). No anonymous label is added or removed.
original:
@fsc:   lda tp
        ldy #7
:       sta (sp),y
        dey
        bpl :-
        spnext
proposal:
@fsc:   lda tp
        ldy #7
:       sta (sp),y
        dey
        bne :-
        staz sp                     ; line 0 non-indexed, as the fast path already does
        spnext
argument: The loop as written runs eight iterations (Y = 7..0) and needs `bpl` to include Y = 0, so it pays a ninth branch evaluation when Y wraps to $FF: 2 (ldy) + 8*(6+2) + 7*3 + 2 = 89 cycles per char. Peeling Y = 0 out lets the loop terminate on `bne` after seven iterations and store line 0 with the 65C02's non-indexed `sta (zp)`: 2 + 7*(6+2) + 6*3 + 2 + 5 = 83, i.e. -6 cycles per char cell, at a cost of +2 bytes. This is exactly the trick the fast fill path already uses - @f7's block ends `staz sp ; line 0 non-indexed` - so `staz sp` (sta (sp), 5 cycles) is known-good here and sp is known to be the live pointer. Correctness: A is unchanged by sta/dey/bne so the fill value survives to the peeled store; the loop still writes all eight bytes 7..0 in descending order. Flags/registers at the end differ (Y = 0 with Z set rather than $FF with N set) but spnext's first instruction is `lda sp`, which overwrites both, and spnext never reads Y. Label count is unchanged: no `:` is added, so spnext's internal `bcc :++` still counts the same labels.

assumption: Costs 12 bytes to save 56 cycles. Two things must hold, both checked: (a) nothing after the call relies on gravity leaving X = 0 -- both call sites (logic.s:1123 in player_dead and 1256 at @grav) go straight to `jsr vy_step`, which starts `mov16 dpx, vy` and never reads X; (b) ANONYMOUS LABEL COUNT CHANGES -- the loop's `:` disappears, so any `:-` textually after gravity that currently binds to it retargets. In practice vy_step's own `beq :+ / : sta dpx+1` immediately below re-establishes a label, but this must be checked before applying. t16 is zero page (logic.s:280, t16 = $D1), so `ror t16` is 5 cycles.
original:
neg16 t16                   ; sec / lda #0 / sbc t16 / sta t16 / lda #0 / sbc t16+1 / sta t16+1
        ldx #5
:       asr16 t16                   ; lda t16+1 / cmp #$80 / ror t16+1 / ror t16
        dex
        bne :-
        add16 vy, t16
        rts
proposal:
sec
        lda #0
        sbc t16
        sta t16
        lda #0
        sbc t16+1                   ; A = high byte of -t16, not yet stored
        .repeat 5
        cmp #$80                    ; C = sign of the current high byte
        ror a                       ; arithmetic shift of the high byte, in A
        ror t16                     ; and of the low byte, in place
        .endrepeat
        sta t16+1
        add16 vy, t16
        rts
argument: Two changes, both value-identical. (1) The high byte never needs to leave A. neg16's last two instructions are `sbc t16+1 / sta t16+1`, and asr16's first is `lda t16+1` -- the store and the reload cancel if the shift chain keeps the high byte in the accumulator. (2) asr16 is `lda var+1 / cmp #$80 / ror var+1 / ror var`: cmp #$80 sets C to the sign bit, `ror var+1` rotates that sign back into bit 7 (the arithmetic part) and pushes var+1's old bit 0 into C, and `ror var` pulls it into var's bit 7. With the high byte already in A, `cmp #$80 / ror a / ror t16` does exactly the same: cmp sets C from A's bit 7, `ror a` produces the new high byte in A and leaves C = A's old bit 0, and `ror t16` consumes it identically. Each iteration then re-reads its input straight out of A, which is already the current high byte, so the per-iteration `lda t16+1` is gone as well; one `sta t16+1` at the end writes the final value, which is all the original loop's five stores accomplish between them. Cycles: original neg16 2+2+3+3+2+3+3 = 18, loop ldx 2 + 4 x (15+2+3) + (15+2+2) = 101, total 119. New: 2+2+3+3+2+3 = 15, plus 5 x (cmp 2 + ror a 2 + ror t16 5) = 45, plus sta 3 = 63. 119 - 63 = 56 cycles. Bytes: 13 + 13 = 26 becomes 11 + 25 + 2 = 38, i.e. 12 bytes spent. Flags: the original leaves N,Z from `bne :-`'s dex; the new code leaves N,Z from `sta t16+1` (none) so effectively from the last `ror t16`. Neither matters -- the next instruction is add16's `clc`, which resets C, and A is reloaded by `lda vy`. Registers: X is no longer touched (see assumption); A ends as the final high byte in both versions.

assumption: Part 1 also rewrites logic.s:2916 ('lsr', immediately above the window) as 'and #$FE'; X is the bar column and the original lsr proves it is halved before scaling. Part 2 relies on the copy being exactly 32 bytes (ldy #31, an even count), which it is.
original:
txa
        lsr                         ; char = x/2      [line 2916, just above the window]
        stza ptr+1
        asl
        rol ptr+1
        asl
        rol ptr+1
        asl
        rol ptr+1
        clc
        adc #<BARADDR
        ...
        ldy #31
:       lda (w16),y
        sta (ptr),y
        dey
        bpl :-
proposal:
txa
        and #$FE                    ; drop bit 0 instead of shifting it out
        stza ptr+1
        asl
        rol ptr+1
        asl
        rol ptr+1
        clc
        adc #<BARADDR
        ...
        ldy #31
:       lda (w16),y
        sta (ptr),y
        dey
        lda (w16),y
        sta (ptr),y
        dey
        bpl :-
argument: Part 1 - the address scale. (x >> 1) << 3 is the same number as (x & $FE) << 2, so one of the three 16-bit shift steps is pure waste. Removing lsr (2) and one asl / rol ptr+1 pair (2 + 5) and adding and #$FE (2) saves 7 cycles and 2 bytes. The 16-bit result is bit-identical: ptr+1 is zeroed first and the value (at most 79*8 = 632) is the same either way; the bit lsr threw into C was never used (stza does not touch C and the following asl overwrites it), and the final rol ptr+1 still sets the flags the following clc then discards. Part 2 - the glyph copy. The loop is 32 iterations of lda (w16),y (5) + sta (ptr),y (6) + dey (2) + bpl (3 taken, 2 on the last) = 511 cycles. Unrolling two-up gives 16 iterations of 5+6+2+5+6+2+3 = 463 cycles, saving 48 for 5 extra bytes. Y counts 31 down to 0, an even 32 bytes, so the pairing is exact and the loop still falls out when dey takes Y to $FF with N set. No anonymous label is added or removed - the ':' stays on the first lda and bpl :- still counts back to it, and the branch is well inside range. Combined: 55 cycles for 3 extra bytes. The two parts are independent; take part 1 alone for 7 cycles and 2 bytes saved if the code growth is unwanted. The identical second copy loop below the window admits the same unroll for another 48.

assumption: BARADDR is an assembly-time constant (engine.s:107, BARADDR = RINGBASE + RINGBYTES) and BARROWS*640 = 1280 = exactly 5 pages (BARROWS = 2). w16b is dead across the fill: the span loop that follows writes both bytes of it ('adc #<BARADDR / sta w16b' and 'adc #>BARADDR / sta w16b+1') before any use. X and Y are dead after the fill (the span loop does 'ldy #1' first and never reads X).
original:
lda #<BARADDR
        sta w16b
        lda #>BARADDR
        sta w16b+1
        lda #$C0
        ldx #>(BARROWS*640)         ; 1280 bytes = 5 pages
        ldy #0
@bf:    sta (w16b),y
        iny
        bne @bf
        inc w16b+1
        dex
        bne @bf
        lda #<BARBUF
        sta w16
        lda #>BARBUF
        sta w16+1
proposal:
lda #$C0                    ; BARADDR is a constant, so the fill needs no pointer:
        ldx #0                      ; five abs,x stores cover the 5 pages in one pass
@bf:    sta BARADDR+$000,x
        sta BARADDR+$100,x
        sta BARADDR+$200,x
        sta BARADDR+$300,x
        sta BARADDR+$400,x
        inx
        bne @bf
        lda #<BARBUF
        sta w16
        lda #>BARBUF
        sta w16+1
argument: The fill builds a zero-page pointer to a constant address and then pays 6 cycles per byte for 'sta (w16b),y' when 'sta abs,x' costs 5. Original: setup (lda#/sta/lda#/sta/lda#/ldx#/ldy# = 16) + 5 pages of 256*(6+2+3) = 2815 each + 4*(inc 5 + dex 2 + bne 3) + a final 9 = about 14140 cycles. Proposal: setup 4 + 256 iterations of (5*5 + inx 2 + bne 3) = 30, last bne 2, = 7683. Saving about 6457 cycles per call. The address range covered is identical - BARADDR+$000+X through BARADDR+$4FF+X over X = 0..255 is exactly BARADDR..BARADDR+1279 - and it does not require BARADDR to be page aligned, just as the original does not. sta abs,x is always 5 cycles (stores never take the page-cross penalty), so the count is exact. A is untouched by the stores and by inx, so one 'lda #$C0' still serves all five. Exit state matches: X = 0 either way, and the old code's Y = 0 is re-established by the 'ldy #1' at @bs. Bytes: 24 -> 22, because the four instructions that built w16b disappear. This routine runs twice per level, so the absolute win is modest, but it is the largest per-execution saving in the batch.

assumption: Nothing inside the loop reads w16 (only w16+1 is touched, by the carry fixup), and w16 must be committed before falling into @wrap, which the added `sta w16` does. A is already dead across the loop (the original clobbers it every iteration). Anonymous-label count is UNCHANGED: still two `:` in the region, and `:+`/`:--` still resolve to the same instructions, so any outside branch counting into this region is unaffected.
original:
@advance:
        tay
:       lda w16
        clc
        adc #ROWCHARS
        sta w16
        bcc :+
        inc w16+1
:       dey
        bne :--
        ; fall through
@wrap:  lda w16+1
proposal:
@advance:
        tay
        lda w16
:       clc
        adc #ROWCHARS
        bcc :+
        inc w16+1
:       dey
        bne :--
        sta w16
        ; fall through
@wrap:  lda w16+1
argument: Loop-invariant hoist of the low-byte load/store. Original body: lda w16 3 + clc 2 + adc 2 + sta w16 3 + bcc(taken) 3 + dey 2 + bne 3 = 18 cycles per row with no carry (22 with: bcc not taken 2 + inc zp 5). Rewritten body: clc 2 + adc 2 + bcc 3 + dey 2 + bne 3 = 12 (16 with carry). Saving is 6 cycles per iteration, i.e. 6*(rows-1) per call once the one-off lda/sta outside the loop are accounted for. Correctness: A carries the running low byte; the only other instruction in the loop, `inc w16+1`, does not touch A, and it does not touch C either -- and C is reset by the `clc` at the top regardless. `bcc :+` still reads the carry out of the `adc` that immediately precedes it. Flags on entry to @wrap: original arrived with Z=1 from the falling-through `bne`; the new `sta w16` sets no flags, so @wrap still sees Z=1 -- and @wrap starts `lda w16+1` anyway. Direct jumps to @wrap from elsewhere are unaffected because `sta w16` is placed before the @wrap label. Note (outside the window, so not proposed): calc_ring uses `mulrowhi,x` tables; if a mulrowlo/mulrowhi pair indexed by row count exists and is paged in here, @advance could become a constant-time 16-bit add and the loop would disappear entirely. That rests on facts not visible in this window.

assumption: None beyond the window. The loop falls through to @wrap, whose first instruction is `lda w16+1`, so A is dead on exit either way; `sta w16` sets no flags, so the Z-from-dex state on fall-through is preserved.
original:
@advance:
        tay
:       lda w16
        clc
        adc #ROWCHARS
        sta w16
        bcc :+
        inc w16+1
:       dey
        bne :--
proposal:
@advance:
        tay
        lda w16
:       clc
        adc #ROWCHARS
        bcc :+
        inc w16+1
:       dey
        bne :--
        sta w16
argument: The loop reloads and restores w16's low byte on every pass even though nothing between the iterations reads it. Hoisting `lda w16` above the loop and sinking `sta w16` below it keeps the running low byte in A. Per iteration: original `lda w16`(3) + `clc`(2) + `adc #ROWCHARS`(2) + `sta w16`(3) + `bcc :+`(3 taken) + `dey`(2) + `bne :--`(3) = 18; new `clc`(2) + `adc`(2) + `bcc`(3) + `dey`(2) + `bne`(3) = 12. Saves 6 per iteration; on the carry pass it is 22 vs 16, also 6. Net per call is 6n-6 (the hoisted lda and sunk sta each cost 3 once), so break-even at n=1 and a clear win for the multi-row sections build_sections actually passes. Correctness: `clc` stays inside the loop because each `adc` can leave carry set; `inc w16+1` and `dey` do not touch A, so the accumulator survives the round trip. Anonymous labels: the count is unchanged at 2 - the first `:` simply moves from before `lda w16` to before `clc`, so `bcc :+` still resolves to the label before `dey` and `bne :--` still resolves to the loop top. Bytes are unchanged (one `lda w16` removed from the loop, one `sta w16` added after it).

assumption: RINGEND = $7B00 so 256 - >RINGEND = $85, a legal immediate. A is dead after the test: the fast path goes `jmpx @jt-2` into CHARCPY, which starts `ldy #8*c` / `lda (tp),y` (or `ldaz tp`), and the slow path @slow starts `lda rc_n`.
original:
ldy rc_wrap
        beq :+
        adc sp
        lda sp+1
        adc #0
        cmp #>RINGEND
        bcc :+
        jmp @slow
:       jmpx @jt-2
proposal:
ldy rc_wrap
        beq :+
        adc sp
        lda sp+1
        adc #(256 - >RINGEND)
        bcc :+
        jmp @slow
:       jmpx @jt-2
argument: Same fold as engine_695. Entering the test A = 8*rc_n and C = 0 (the comment is right: rc_n <= 4, so the three asl's shift out zeros; `ldy`/`beq` do not touch C). `adc sp` leaves C = the carry out of the low byte. The old pair then computed A = sp+1 + C (2 cycles) and compared it against $7B (2 cycles), using only the resulting C. Replacing both with `adc #$85` computes sp+1 + C + $85, whose carry out is set exactly when sp+1 + C >= $7B -- the identical predicate -- in 2 cycles instead of 4. sp+1 is in $35..$7B, so sp+1+C+$85 <= $101; the only way the add carries is the threshold being met, which is what we want, and a value of exactly $7B still carries as `cmp` would have set C on equality. N/Z differ from the old `cmp` but neither is read: the only consumer is `bcc`. A's value differs but A is dead on both successors. `bcs @slow` is NOT available here as a further saving: @slow sits past the four CHARCPY and four CHARPER blocks (the existing @t0..@t3 trampolines exist precisely because that region is out of branch range). The `:` label is preserved -- `beq :+` after `ldy rc_wrap` still points at it -- so no anonymous-label renumbering. The min-of-two above (`lda #4 / sec / sbc rc_subc / cmp cnt / bcc :+ / lda cnt`) is already minimal at 7 cycles for 4-rc_subc; the `lda rc_subc / eor #3 / inc a` alternative is the same 7 cycles and one byte longer.

assumption: A is dead at ':' (jmpx uses X only) and at @slow (which starts 'lda rc_n'); D is clear, as everywhere in this code.
original:
adc #0
        cmp #>RINGEND
        bcc :+
        jmp @slow
:       jmpx @jt-2
proposal:
adc #(256 - (>RINGEND))     ; = adc #$85 ; C set iff sp+1+C >= >RINGEND
        bcc :+
        jmp @slow
:       jmpx @jt-2
argument: Context (line 537, just above the window) is 'lda sp+1', reached with C = the carry out of 'adc sp'. The pair 'adc #0 / cmp #>RINGEND' only ever feeds the following bcc, so only the carry out matters. 'adc #0' gives A = sp+1 + C; 'cmp #$7B' then sets C = (sp+1+C >= $7B). A single 'adc #(256-$7B)' = 'adc #$85' gives A = sp+1 + C + $85 with carry out set exactly when sp+1 + C >= $7B, so the branch condition is identical. No wrap hazard: RINGEND = $7B00 so sp+1 <= $7A and sp+1+C+$85 <= $100. Cost: adc #imm (2) + cmp #imm (2) = 4 becomes adc #imm (2), saving 2 cycles and 2 bytes. Flags: only C is consumed (bcc); N/V/Z differ but nothing reads them - the fall-through is 'jmpx @jt-2' (X only) and @slow begins 'lda rc_n'. The 'beq :+' at line 535 that also targets this ':' never runs this code. Anonymous labels: none added or removed - the ':' before jmpx stays. The 'bcc :+ / jmp @slow' pair cannot be folded into 'bcs @slow': @slow is at engine.s:633, past the four unrolled CHARCPY/CHARPER blocks, hundreds of bytes out of branch range.

assumption: Proposal covers the whole po_star prologue (logic.s 1801-1822), i.e. four instructions past the end of the 16-instruction window; spx/spy do not alias px/py.
original:
lda O_XL,y
        sec
        sbc px
        sta rx
        lda O_XH,y
        sbc px+1
        sta rx+1
        lda O_YL,y
        sec
        sbc py
        sta ry
        lda O_YH,y
        sbc py+1
        sta ry+1
        lda O_XL,y
        sta spx
        lda O_XH,y
        sta spx+1
        lda O_YL,y
        sta spy
        lda O_YH,y
        sta spy+1
proposal:
lda O_XL,y
        sta spx
        sec
        sbc px
        sta rx
        lda O_XH,y
        sta spx+1
        sbc px+1
        sta rx+1
        lda O_YL,y
        sta spy
        sec
        sbc py
        sta ry
        lda O_YH,y
        sta spy+1
        sbc py+1
        sta ry+1
argument: The prologue loads each of O_XL/O_XH/O_YL/O_YH twice: once as the minuend of the rx/ry subtraction and again, unchanged, to copy into spx/spy. O_* are absolute tables (LV_OBJST-based, 149-byte stride), so each load is `lda abs,y` = 4 cycles, 3 bytes (+1 cycle when the index crosses a page). Storing the freshly loaded value to spx/spy before subtracting removes four of the eight loads: -16 cycles, -12 bytes (more if any of the four dropped loads crossed a page). Correctness: `sta` sets no flags, so interposing `sta spx` between `lda O_XL,y` and `sec/sbc px` changes nothing, and - critically - interposing `sta spx+1` between `lda O_XH,y` and `sbc px+1` does not disturb the borrow carried out of the low-byte `sbc`, which is the only flag the high byte depends on. The store order within each pair is irrelevant because spx and rx are distinct locations. The instruction that ends the block changes from `sta spy+1` to `sta ry+1`; both leave flags untouched and the next instruction is `jmp ob_star`, so no flag is consumed. A, X and Y are unchanged in kind: Y is still the object index, A ends holding ry+1's value instead of spy+1's and is dead either way.

assumption: None within the routine. The rewrite reaches six lines above the window (to the 'lda O_XL,y' at the po_star entry) -- all four loads it removes have their first copy there.
original:
po_star:
        lda O_XL,y
        sec
        sbc px
        sta rx
        lda O_XH,y
        sbc px+1
        sta rx+1
        lda O_YL,y
        sec
        sbc py
        sta ry
        lda O_YH,y
        sbc py+1
        sta ry+1
        lda O_XL,y                  ; spx/spy = where it draws
        sta spx
        lda O_XH,y
        sta spx+1
        lda O_YL,y
        sta spy
        lda O_YH,y
        sta spy+1
        jmp ob_star
proposal:
po_star:
        lda O_XL,y
        sta spx                     ; spx/spy = where it draws
        sec
        sbc px
        sta rx
        lda O_XH,y
        sta spx+1
        sbc px+1
        sta rx+1
        lda O_YL,y
        sta spy
        sec
        sbc py
        sta ry
        lda O_YH,y
        sta spy+1
        sbc py+1
        sta ry+1
        jmp ob_star
argument: Every one of O_XL,y O_XH,y O_YL,y O_YH,y is loaded twice: once to form rx/ry and once again, unchanged, to form spx/spy. Nothing writes the object table in between (there is no jsr and no indexed store in the window), and Y is not altered, so the second load always returns the same byte. Moving 'sta spx' etc. to immediately after each load makes the second load dead. Four abs,y loads removed at 4 cycles each = 16 cycles, 3 bytes each = 12 bytes. Correctness: sta sets no flags and does not touch the carry, so inserting it between 'lda O_XH,y' and 'sbc px+1' preserves the borrow chain from the low-byte sbc -- this is the only delicate point and it is safe. The two 'sec' instructions stay where they are, ahead of each low-byte subtraction. A at the jmp is ry+1's value in the rewrite versus O_YH,y in the original: ob_star is entered by jmp with the object index in Y and re-derives what it needs, but if it read A on entry it would already be reading a different value than the sbc chain produced two lines earlier, so A is not live here.

assumption: Y is dead at every destination reached from the jmpx/@fslow: @f31/@f23/@f15/@f7 all begin with FIL1 k = `ldy #k`, and @fslow (engine.s:742) does `lda rc_n / sta tmp2 / lda tp / ldy #7`. Saving applies only on the rc_wrap != 0 path.
original:
asl
        sta tmp
        lda rc_wrap
        beq :+
        lda tmp
        adc sp
        lda sp+1
        adc #0
        cmp #>RINGEND
        bcc :+
        jmp @fslow
:       lda tp
        jmpx @ft-2
proposal:
asl
        sta tmp
        ldy rc_wrap                 ; test without destroying A (= 8*rc_n)
        beq :+
        adc sp                      ; C is clear: the asl's above shifted out zeros (rc_n <= 4)
        lda sp+1
        adc #0
        cmp #>RINGEND
        bcc :+
        jmp @fslow
:       lda tp
        jmpx @ft-2
argument: This is the @solid twin of the copy path at engine.s:528-542, which already carries exactly this encoding (`sta tmp / ldy rc_wrap / beq :+ / adc sp`). The reload `lda tmp` exists only because `lda rc_wrap` clobbered A; `ldy rc_wrap` sets N,Z from rc_wrap identically (3 cy, 2 bytes, zp) and leaves A = 8*rc_n, so `lda tmp` (3 cy, 2 bytes) disappears. Carry: rc_n <= 4, so the three asl's (A = n -> 2n -> 4n -> 8n, max 32) all shift out a 0 and leave C=0; `sta`, `ldy` and `beq` do not touch C, so `adc sp` still adds with no carry in, exactly as before. X is untouched (it still holds 2*rc_n for the `jmpx @ft-2` dispatch). Y is the only new casualty and every dispatch target reloads it. Anonymous labels: there is exactly one `:` in the window (before `lda tp`), targeted by both `beq :+` and `bcc :+`; the count is unchanged. Cost: 3 cycles and 2 bytes, but only when rc_wrap != 0 (a row that can straddle the ring end); the rc_wrap == 0 path is byte-for-byte the same cost as before.

assumption: Y is dead here (confirmed: the @f* fill blocks and @fslow both load Y themselves, @advsp/@runend never read Y, and @run reloads X/Y-independent state). Carry must be clear entering `adc sp`, which it is: the last `asl` shifted out a zero because rc_n <= 4, and ldy does not touch C.
original:
sta rc_n
        asl
        tax
        asl
        asl
        sta tmp
        lda rc_wrap
        beq :+
        lda tmp
        adc sp
        lda sp+1
        adc #0
proposal:
sta rc_n
        asl
        tax
        asl
        asl
        sta tmp
        ldy rc_wrap
        beq :+
        adc sp
        lda sp+1
        adc #0
argument: After `sta tmp` the accumulator still holds 8*rc_n, the exact value the code then reloads with `lda tmp`. It is reloaded only because `lda rc_wrap` was used to test the wrap flag. Testing it with `ldy rc_wrap` (3 cycles) sets Z from rc_wrap exactly as `lda` did, so the `beq :+` is unchanged, but leaves A intact so the `lda tmp` (3 cycles, 2 bytes) can be deleted. Net -3 cycles, -2 bytes on both the wrap and no-wrap paths. `sta tmp` must stay: @advsp reads tmp to advance sp by 8*rc_n. Carry: ldy affects only N and Z, so the C=0 left by the final `asl` still reaches `adc sp` - the same reasoning the existing comment on the copy path relies on. X (= 2*rc_n for `jmpx @ft-2`) is untouched by ldy. This is not speculative: the non-solid twin of this very sequence, ~40 lines earlier in drawrect, is already written exactly this way (`sta tmp` / `ldy rc_wrap` / `beq :+` / `adc sp`), so the @solid path is simply the un-updated copy.

assumption: The instruction immediately above the window is `adc #0` (engine.s:694) and RINGEND = $7B00, so >RINGEND = $7B and 256-$7B = $85 is a legal immediate. A is dead at `:` (both successors reload it: @fslow starts `lda rc_n`, the @fNN blocks start `ldy #k`/`sta`). The `bcs @fslow` form needs @fslow within +127 bytes: I count 115 bytes of code between the branch and @fslow (2 lda tp + 3 jmp(abs,x) + 8 table + 25+25+25+24 fill blocks + 3 jmp @advsp), so it fits, and ca65 would error loudly rather than mis-assemble if that count is off.
original:
adc #0
        cmp #>RINGEND
        bcc :+
        jmp @fslow
:       lda tp
        jmpx @ft-2
proposal:
adc #(256 - >RINGEND)
        bcs @fslow
:       lda tp
        jmpx @ft-2
argument: Two independent local edits. (1) `adc #0` (2) + `cmp #>RINGEND` (2) fold into one `adc #(256->RINGEND)` (2). The carry in is the carry out of the preceding `adc sp`, so the accumulator holds sp+1+c; adding $85 = 256-$7B sets C exactly when sp+1+c >= $7B, which is the condition `cmp #>RINGEND` produced, and equality still carries just as CMP set C on equality. sp's high byte lives in $35..$7B, so sp+1+c+$85 <= $101 and the only thing that can make it carry is the threshold being met. The value left in A is now garbage where the old code left the true high byte, but A is dead at that point: the very next instruction on the fast path is `lda tp`, which reloads the fill value before any FIL1 stores it, and the slow path @fslow opens with `lda rc_n`. N and Z from the new adc are not read either -- the only consumer is the branch, which reads C. (2) `bcc :+ / jmp @fslow` inverts to `bcs @fslow`: the common no-wrap path then pays 2 cycles for a not-taken branch instead of 3 for a taken one, and the rare path pays 3 instead of 2+3. Net on the common path 2 + 1 = 3 cycles and 2 + 3 = 5 bytes. The `:` line must stay: it is still the target of the `beq :+` that follows `lda rc_wrap` two instructions earlier, so the ca65 anonymous-label count is unchanged. The fill chain itself has no cheaper form: `sta (sp),y` is 6 cycles and `dey` 2, there is no 65C02 store that writes a byte through a zero-page pointer at a variable offset for less, and the trailing `staz sp` already uses the 5-cycle `sta (zp)` form for offset 0. The apparently redundant `ldy #23` where @f31 falls into @f23 (Y is already 24 there) is not removable either: @f23 is a live jump-table entry and needs its own Y load.

assumption: None. Nothing after the window reads flags or A; @second stays defined so any other reference to it is unaffected. No anonymous labels involved.
original:
lda rc_y
        and #1
        bne @second
        bra @nextrow
@second:
        jsr @drawrow
proposal:
lda rc_y
        and #1
        beq @nextrow
@second:
        jsr @drawrow
argument: Classic branch-over-branch. @second is the next instruction, so invert the test and delete the bra. Even rows: beq taken 3 cy instead of bne-not-taken 2 + bra 3 = 5 (saves 2). Odd rows: beq not taken 2 instead of bne taken 3 (saves 1). 2 bytes saved. Flags/A identical at both targets (both paths previously arrived with the and #1 flags or the bra's, and nothing consumes them).

assumption: @nextrow is within branch range. It is: reading engine.s, @nextrow sits about 9 bytes past the `bra @nextrow` (only `@second: jsr @drawrow / inc rc_y / dec rc_h / beq @done` intervene). ca65 errors at assembly time if a branch does not reach, so this is self-checking.
original:
lda rc_y
        and #1
        bne @second
        bra @nextrow
@second:
        jsr @drawrow
proposal:
lda rc_y
        and #1
        beq @nextrow
@second:
        jsr @drawrow
argument: The gather loop above (lda (ptr),y / tax / lda LV_PAGE0,x / sta GATHERL,y / lda LV_PAGE0+$100,x / sta GATHERH,y / dey / bpl) is already minimal: the tax is forced by the table index, both GATHER stores are abs,y at 5 cycles because GATHER is not in zero page, and dey/bpl is the cheapest counted loop. setbank BANK_TILES (lda #n / sta $F4 / sta $FE30 = 2+3+4 = 9) is a required bank change. The one slack is the parity test. `bne @second` branches forward over exactly one instruction, `bra @nextrow`; inverting the sense lets @second fall through. Correctness: `and #1` sets Z from bit 0 of rc_y, so beq is taken precisely when bne was not taken - the two arms are swapped, not altered, and A is the same ($00 or $01) on both. No anonymous labels are involved (both targets are cheap-locals), so rule 3 does not bite; @second simply becomes an unreferenced label, which ca65 accepts. Cycles: odd rc_y was lda 3 + and 2 + bne taken 3 = 8, now 3+2+2 = 7 (saves 1). Even rc_y was 3+2+2+bra 3 = 10, now 3+2+beq taken 3 = 8 (saves 2). Bytes: the 2-byte bra disappears. Two cycles is the worst-case-path figure; the average over the two parities is 1.5.

assumption: @g6 is reached only by fall-through from the @g4 block or by the patched @fjmp; nothing else branches between the last `sta (ptr),y` of the @g4 block and `@g6`.
original:
sta (ptr),y
        iny
        lda (sp),y
        sta (ptr),y
        iny
@g6:    ldy #6
        lda (sp),y
        sta (ptr),y
proposal:
sta (ptr),y
        iny
        lda (sp),y
        sta (ptr),y
@g6:    ldy #6
        lda (sp),y
        sta (ptr),y
argument: The unrolled copy enters at @g2/@g4/@g6 through the patched `@fjmp`, and each entry point begins with an absolute `ldy #n`. The final `iny` of the @g4 block leaves Y = 4+2 = 6, and the very next instruction executed on the fall-through path is `@g6: ldy #6`, which reloads the identical value. The `iny` is therefore dead: Y is not read between it and the `ldy`, and its N/Z flags are not read either (the `ldy #6` overwrites them, and nothing branches in between). Removing it saves 2 cycles and 1 byte on every pass that falls through from @g4 into @g6, i.e. every char copied when wfine is 2 or 4. The same dead `iny` exists at the end of the @g2 block immediately before `@g4: ldy #4` (engine.s line ~1956, just above this window) and can be removed for another 2 cycles on the wfine=2 path. No anonymous label is added or removed, so no `:+`/`:-` retargeting. `@g4`/`@g6` must keep their `ldy #n` because they are jump targets from @ftab, so the cheap direction is to drop the `iny`, not the `ldy`. Note the rest of the window is already tight: the two `#8` pointer advances are 13 cycles each and `clc` cannot be dropped from the `ptr` one, because on the rare spnext path that takes the `sp+1` fixup the carry is left set by `ringup`'s `sbc`.

assumption: Y is dead on entry to @rowdone and across the `bcc` (true: @rowdone is the tail of the internal @drawrow, which has already clobbered Y in every CHARCPY/CHARPER/@sc path, and its caller resumes at `inc rc_y` without reading Y). mirror_run takes A = low, Y = high, X = count, so only the three registers need to be correct at the `jsr`, not the order they are set in.
original:
dec tmp2
        bne @sc
        jmp @runend
@rowdone:
        lda rc_sp+1
        cmp #(>RINGEND - 5)
        bcc :+
        lda rc_sp
        ldy rc_sp+1
        ldx rc_w
        jsr mirror_run
:
proposal:
dec tmp2
        bne @sc
        bra @runend
@rowdone:
        ldy rc_sp+1
        cpy #(>RINGEND - 5)
        bcc :+
        lda rc_sp
        ldx rc_w
        jsr mirror_run
:
argument: Two edits. (1) The guard loads rc_sp+1 into A only to compare it, then reloads the very same byte into Y three instructions later. `ldy rc_sp+1` (3) + `cpy #imm` (2) costs the identical 5 cycles as `lda rc_sp+1` (3) + `cmp #imm` (2) and sets C identically -- CPY is an unsigned compare on Y exactly as CMP is on A, and only C is consumed by the `bcc`. On the taken path the later `ldy rc_sp+1` (3 cycles, 2 bytes) then disappears outright. So: 0 cycles on the common path, 3 cycles and 2 bytes on the mirror path. Nothing between the new `ldy` and the `jsr` disturbs Y (`cpy`, `bcc`, `lda zp`, `ldx zp`), and mirror_run still receives A = rc_sp, Y = rc_sp+1, X = rc_w. The N/Z difference (from Y rather than A) is not read. (2) `jmp @runend` becomes `bra @runend`: I count 70 bytes back from the end of the branch to the @runend label (20 for the @runend block, 4 for @slow's two instructions, 9+11+20+4 for @sc's body, spnext and the loop tail, plus the 2-byte branch), well inside the -128 reach, so it saves 1 byte at the same 3 cycles. The +640 ring step that follows is already minimal: `ringup` needs A to hold the high byte, so the `cmp`/`adc` fold used in engine_520 does not apply.

assumption: t16 is dead after `add16 py, t16`. Verified: the next reference to t16 anywhere in logic.s after line 1441 is line 1506, and that is a write (`sta t16`), not a read. Saving is 20 cycles when q1 is 0 or 1 (the flat-ground case, by far the common one) and 16 when q1 is negative.
proposal:
@hmoved:
        ; if a <= 1: py += a ; alt = 0 else alt = a   (a may be -1: step up a slope)
        lda q1
        bmi @stepn
        cmp #2
        bcs @alt
        clc                         ; 0 or 1: high byte of the addend is 0
        adc py
        sta py
        bcc :+
        inc py+1
:       stza alt
        bra @hnext
@stepn: clc                         ; negative: high byte of the addend is $FF
        adc py
        sta py
        lda py+1
        adc #$FF
        sta py+1
        stza alt
        bra @hnext
@alt:   sta alt
@hnext:
argument: The sign of q1 is already decided by the branches above @step -- `bmi @step` reaches it only for negative q1, and falling past `bcs @alt` reaches it only for q1 = 0 or 1 -- so `sx16 t16` recomputes at run time a fact the control flow has just established, then `add16 py, t16` reloads py's low byte that a direct `adc py` could have used straight out of A. Splitting the two arms removes both. Positive arm: lda 3 + bmi nt 2 + cmp 2 + bcs nt 2 + clc 2 + adc py 3 + sta py 3 + bcc taken 3 + stza alt 3 + bra 3 = 26, against the original 3+2+2+2 + sx16 (sta 3, and#$80 2, beq taken 3, sta 3 = 11) + add16 (clc 2, lda 3, adc 3, sta 3, lda 3, adc 3, sta 3 = 20) + 3 + 3 = 46: 20 saved. Negative arm: 3 + bmi taken 3 + clc 2 + adc py 3 + sta py 3 + lda py+1 3 + adc #$FF 2 + sta py+1 3 + 3 + 3 = 28 against 44: 16 saved. Correctness of the negative arm: `adc #$FF` adds the sign-extension byte together with the carry out of the low add, which is exactly what `adc t16+1` did with t16+1 = $FF (py = $0100, a = -1: low 0+$FF = $FF C=0, high $01+$FF+0 = $00, giving $00FF -- correct). Positive arm: `bcc :+ / inc py+1` is the zero-extension `adc #0` written the cheap way. Registers: A only, X and Y untouched, same as before. Flags into @hnext do not matter -- @hnext opens with `lda dpx+1`. ANONYMOUS LABELS: the count is deliberately preserved -- the one `:` that lived inside the sx16 expansion is removed and exactly one new `:` appears in the positive arm, so nothing that counts `:+`/`:-` past this region is retargeted. Bytes: 28 against 27, one byte more.

assumption: Nothing reads dpx or dpx+1 between the macros and the sign-extend that follows (it is straight-line code), and D=0 as everywhere else in this file.
original:
mov16 dpx, vx
        add16i dpx, 128             ; leaves the high byte in A
        sta dpx
        and #$80
        beq :+
        lda #$FF
:       sta dpx+1
proposal:
lda vx
        clc
        adc #128
        lda vx+1
        adc #0                      ; A = high byte of vx + 128
        sta dpx
        and #$80
        beq :+
        lda #$FF
:       sta dpx+1
argument: Expanded, the original is: lda vx / sta dpx / lda vx+1 / sta dpx+1 (mov16, 12 cy) then clc / lda dpx / adc #128 / sta dpx / lda dpx+1 / adc #0 / sta dpx+1 (add16i, 18 cy) then sta dpx (3 cy) = 33 cycles, 23 bytes. Every one of add16i's stores is dead: dpx is immediately overwritten by the following sta dpx with the high byte, and dpx+1 is immediately overwritten by the sign-extend. So the whole thing only needs the high byte of vx+128 in A. The proposal computes exactly that in place: lda vx (3) / clc (2) / adc #128 (2) - carry out is all that survives of the low byte - / lda vx+1 (3) / adc #0 (2) / sta dpx (3) = 15 cycles, 11 bytes. Saving 18 cycles, 12 bytes. Correctness: the value stored to dpx is bit-identical (high byte of the 16-bit sum vx+128), and the following and #$80 / beq / lda #$FF / sta dpx+1 is untouched, so dpx+1 gets the same sign extension. Flags entering and #$80 come from a load/adc of the same value in both versions. No anonymous label is added or removed (the single ':' of the sign-extend stays). Note: replacing clc / adc #128 with cmp #$80 saves a further 2 cycles and 1 byte - cmp #$80 sets C exactly when vx >= $80, which is exactly the carry out of vx + $80 - but the clc form above is the conservative one.

assumption: None. tmp3 is zero page (engine.s .zeropage block), so lsr tmp3 is 5 cycles.
original:
@dur:   stza tmp3
        asl
        rol tmp3
        asl
        rol tmp3
        asl
        rol tmp3
        asl
        rol tmp3
        asl
        rol tmp3
        asl
        rol tmp3
        sec
        sbc #2
        bcs :+
        dec tmp3
:       rts
proposal:
@dur:   sta tmp3                    ; n*64 == (n*256)>>2: start from hi=n, lo=0 and
        lda #0                      ; shift right twice instead of left six times
        lsr tmp3
        ror
        lsr tmp3
        ror
        sec
        sbc #2
        bcs :+
        dec tmp3
:       rts
argument: The original builds A*64 as six left shifts of the 16-bit pair tmp3:A, paying 'rol tmp3' (5 cycles) six times. Shifting the other way needs only two steps: put n in the high byte and 0 in the low byte, then halve twice. Trace with n = %abcdefgh: after 'sta tmp3 / lda #0', tmp3=n, A=0. lsr tmp3 -> tmp3 = %0abcdefg, C = h; ror -> A = %h0000000, C = 0. lsr tmp3 -> tmp3 = %00abcdef, C = g; ror -> A = %gh000000. So tmp3 = n>>2 and A = (n&3)<<6, which is exactly the high and low bytes of n*64. Cost: 3+2+5+2+5+2 = 19 against stz tmp3 3 + 6x(asl 2 + rol tmp3 5) = 45. Saving 26 cycles. Bytes: 2+2+2+1+2+1 = 10 against 2+6x3 = 20, saving 10. Correctness: the entry contract (A = lines, exit A/tmp3 = lines*64-2) is unchanged, and the '-2' tail including the 'bcs :+ / dec tmp3' borrow propagation is left byte-for-byte alone, so the exit flags (from sbc, or from dec tmp3 on the borrow path) are identical. No anonymous label is added or removed -- the ':' after 'bcs' is untouched. 'ror' with no operand is the accumulator form, the same implied addressing the original already uses for 'asl'. Note the six left shifts also left a stale carry that 'sec' overrode; the new form does the same.

assumption: A is dead at the `:` merge. Verified: the loop head is `@k: lda keytab,x`, which reloads A on every iteration, and the fall-out path is `lda KEYSCAN / sta keys`. KEYSCAN lives in the TABLES segment (engine.s line 279, after `.segment "TABLES"` at 219), so it is absolute, not zero page.
original:
lda KEYSCAN
        ora keybits,x
        sta KEYSCAN
proposal:
lda keybits,x
        tsb KEYSCAN
argument: The three instructions are a read-modify-write OR of keybits,x into KEYSCAN. 65C02 `tsb` is exactly that: M := M OR A. Cycles: original lda abs 4 + ora abs,x 4 + sta abs 4 = 12; new lda abs,x 4 + tsb abs 6 = 10, saving 2. Bytes: 3+3+3 = 9 down to 3+3 = 6, saving 3. Note keybits is a small table at engine.s:3097 and the indexed load is present in both forms, so any page-cross penalty is identical. Flags: the original leaves N,Z from the ORA result; tsb sets Z from (A AND M) before the store and leaves N,V alone. Nothing between here and the next flag-setter reads them -- the very next instruction is `inx`, which sets N,Z itself, and the branch `bne @k` after `cpx #11` is driven by the cpx. Registers: X is unchanged by both forms; A ends as keybits,x rather than the merged mask, which is safe because @k reloads A first thing and the post-loop code does `lda KEYSCAN` explicitly. This path only runs when a key is down (bpl not taken), so the saving is per key-press per scan slot, not per iteration.

assumption: qy must not be read between the copy and the add (it is not -- the two macros are adjacent), and qy/qy+1 must not alias py/py+1 (distinct zero-page symbols).
original:
mov16 qy, py
        add16i qy, 12
proposal:
clc
        lda py
        adc #12
        sta qy
        lda py+1
        adc #0
        sta qy+1
argument: mov16 qy,py expands to lda py / sta qy / lda py+1 / sta qy+1 = 3+3+3+3 = 12 cycles, 8 bytes. add16i qy,12 expands to clc / lda qy / adc #12 / sta qy / lda qy+1 / adc #0 / sta qy+1 = 2+3+2+3+3+2+3 = 18 cycles, 13 bytes. Total 30 cycles / 21 bytes. The add's two loads read exactly the values the copy just wrote, so reading py/py+1 directly is value-identical: the proposal is 2+3+2+3+3+2+3 = 18 cycles, 13 bytes. Saving 12 cycles / 8 bytes. Flags: the original's last flag-setting instruction is `adc #0` operating on (qy+1 == py+1) with the carry out of the low add; the proposal's is `adc #0` on py+1 with the same carry, so N/Z/C/V and the final A are bit-identical. The intermediate state qy == py is never observed -- `jsr gettileattr` is the next instruction after the add. No anonymous labels involved. Separately, in this same window `mov16i vy, -1280` expands to lda #$00 / sta vy / lda #$FB / sta vy+1; the first pair can be `stz vy` (3cy/2 bytes vs 5cy/4 bytes, a further 2 cycles / 2 bytes) because the Z=1 that lda #$00 sets is immediately overwritten by lda #$FB.

assumption: X must be dead after the loop. Visible evidence: the next three instructions are stza stars / stza bent / ldy nobj, none of which reads X (stza with one argument expands to plain stz). What is not visible is whether anything further down expects X == 128 rather than $FF.
original:
ldx #0
        lda #$FF
:       sta LV_GRID,x
        inx
        cpx #128
        bne :-
proposal:
ldx #127
        lda #$FF
:       sta LV_GRID,x
        dex
        bpl :-
argument: The loop fills 128 bytes of LV_GRID with a constant, so the order of the stores is immaterial and the counter can run downwards, letting dex's own N flag terminate it and deleting the cpx. Per iteration: original sta abs,x 5 + inx 2 + cpx # 2 + bne taken 3 = 12; proposal sta abs,x 5 + dex 2 + bpl taken 3 = 10. (sta abs,x is 5 cycles regardless of page crossing, so the index direction costs nothing there.) 2 cycles x 128 iterations = 256 cycles saved per execution of the loop, plus 2 bytes for the deleted cpx. Termination: X counts 127..0 storing to LV_GRID+127..LV_GRID+0, and bpl is false exactly when dex produces $FF, i.e. after the store at index 0 -- 128 stores, same as before. Flags on exit differ (original leaves Z=1/C=1/N=0 from cpx #128; proposal leaves N=1/Z=0 from dex) but the next instruction, stz, reads no flags and `ldy nobj` reloads N/Z before any branch. `lda #$FF` still sets N=1/Z=0 last in both versions, and A is unchanged by the loop. The anonymous-label count is unchanged: one ':' in, one ':' out, and the earlier `bne :-` in the window still counts back to its own separate label.

assumption: D=0 (as everywhere in this file). X must be preserved - it is, neither version writes it.
original:
lda ry+1
        inca
        cmp #2
        bcs @no
        lda ry
        eor ry+1                    ; low byte sign must agree with the high byte
        bmi @no
        lda ry
        eor #$80
        cmp RNGTAB+2,x
proposal:
lda ry
        cmp #$80                    ; C = carry out of (ry + $80)
        lda ry+1
        adc #0                      ; high byte of ry + $80
        bne @no                     ; ry outside -128..127
        lda ry
        eor #$80
        cmp RNGTAB+2,x
argument: The two-step test 'high+1 is 0 or 1' plus 'low and high signs agree' is exactly the test 'ry lies in -128..127'. That is one 16-bit add: ry + $80 has a zero high byte iff ry is in $FF80..$FFFF or $0000..$007F, i.e. -128..127 - the identical accept set. Original: lda ry+1 (3) + inca (2) + cmp #2 (2) + bcs (2) + lda ry (3) + eor ry+1 (3) + bmi (2) = 17 cycles, 13 bytes before the eor #$80. Proposal: lda ry (3) + cmp #$80 (2) + lda ry+1 (3) + adc #0 (2) + bne (2) = 12 cycles, 10 bytes. Saving 5 cycles and 3 bytes on the passing path. Carry: cmp #$80 sets C=1 exactly when ry >= $80, which is exactly the carry out of the low-byte addition ry + $80, so the clc/adc pair is not needed; the intervening lda ry+1 does not touch C. Flags on the @no path do not matter - @no is clc / rts and clears C itself, and the original reached it with C either set (bcs) or arbitrary (bmi). A is reloaded (lda ry) before the eor #$80, so the value left in A by the test is irrelevant. X is untouched by both forms, which matters because RNGTAB+2,x and RNGTAB+3,x follow. Note the identical rx test at lines 1832-1839, just above this window, admits exactly the same rewrite for another 5 cycles.

assumption: Two facts sit just outside the window. (1) The matching `pla` is at engine.s:2037 and must become `txa`; X is free there because the @bf page counter has been decremented to 0 and nothing from 2023 to the `rts` at 2062 reads X. (2) Dropping the `dey` leaves Y=1 instead of 0 at line 2040, which is immediately `ldy #2`, so no consumer notices. Saving is per icon span, not per frame.
original:
@bs:    ldy #1
        lda (w16),y                 ; offset high ($FF = end)
        cmp #$FF
        beq @bsdone
        pha
        dey
        lda (w16),y                 ; offset low
        clc
        adc #<BARADDR
        sta w16b
        pla
        adc #>BARADDR
        sta w16b+1
proposal:
@bs:    ldy #1
        lda (w16),y                 ; offset high ($FF = end)
        cmp #$FF
        beq @bsdone
        tax                         ; X is free: the @bf counter ran down to 0
        lda (w16)                   ; offset low, 65C02 (zp): no dey needed
        clc
        adc #<BARADDR
        sta w16b
        txa
        adc #>BARADDR
        sta w16b+1
argument: Two independent local savings. First, the high byte is parked across a 16-bit add: pha(3) + pla(4) = 7 becomes tax(2) + txa(2) = 4, for 3 cycles at the same 2 bytes. Neither tax nor txa touches C, and C is the one flag that must survive from `adc #<BARADDR` to `adc #>BARADDR` -- pha/pla did not touch it either, so the carry chain is intact. `txa` sets N,Z from X just as `pla` set them from the pulled byte (same byte), and the consumer `adc #>BARADDR` overwrites them anyway. Second, `dey / lda (w16),y` (2+5 = 7 cycles, 1+2 = 3 bytes) becomes `lda (w16)` (5 cycles, 2 bytes) using the 65C02 (zp) mode -- the same mode the ldaz macro emits elsewhere -- saving 2 cycles and 1 byte, at the cost of leaving Y=1 rather than 0. Total 5 cycles and 1 byte per span header. Anonymous labels in the window are untouched. The @bf fill loop above (6+2+3 per byte through `sta (w16b),y`) has no local improvement: `sta abs,y` would be 5 cycles but the address is not constant, and self-modifying the operand is a redesign.

assumption: A cheap-local label (@nc below) unused in bar_digit - the routine currently has no @ labels at all. It must be a named label, not `:`, or the following loop's `bpl :-` would retarget onto it.
original:
add16i w16, 32              ; clc / lda w16 / adc #32 / sta w16
                                    ; lda w16+1 / adc #0 / sta w16+1
        add16i ptr, 640
        ldy #31
proposal:
lda w16
        clc
        adc #32
        sta w16
        bcc @nc
        inc w16+1
@nc:    add16i ptr, 640
        ldy #31
argument: add16i w16, 32 costs 18 cycles / 13 bytes because it always executes the high-byte lda/adc/sta. Since the immediate's high byte is zero, the high byte only ever needs `inc`, so the branch-over form costs 3+2+2+3+3 = 13 cycles when the low byte does not carry and 3+2+2+3+2+5 = 17 when it does, in 11 bytes. w16 here is SPR_DIGITS + 64*digit, so a carry needs a low byte >= 224 - at most one digit value in eight; 5 cycles saved on essentially every call, never a loss. Correctness: `inc w16+1` is exactly `adc #0` with C=1 for a zero high immediate. Flags are not consumed - the next thing is the second add16i, which starts with its own `clc` - and A ends holding the low byte rather than the high byte, also dead. add16i ptr, 640 is left alone: its high immediate is 2, so the high byte genuinely needs an adc and the macro form is already minimal. The 32-byte copy loop itself is at the floor (lda (w16),y 5 + sta (ptr),y 6 + dey 2 + bpl 3) and cannot use the peel-Y=0 trick, because the source load `lda (w16)` non-indexed would still have to be paired with a `sta (ptr)` and both pointers would need separate handling - the saving would be 1 cycle for 4 bytes and is not taken here.

assumption: @run is referenced only by the single 'bra @run' shown (verified in logic.s). dpx+1 as written by add16i is dead - the sign-extend that follows overwrites it. Decimal mode is clear, as the existing add16i already assumes.
original:
beq @right
        sub16 vx, t16
        lda #1
        sta facing
        bra @run
@right: add16 vx, t16
        stz facing
@run:   lda #1
        sta running
        bra @hmove
@norun: stza running
@hmove:
        ; steps = (vx + 128) >> 8 ; dir = sign
        mov16 dpx, vx
        add16i dpx, 128             ; leaves the high byte in A
        sta dpx
        and #$80
        beq :+
        lda #$FF
:       sta dpx+1
proposal:
beq @right
        sub16 vx, t16
        lda #1
        sta facing
        sta running                 ; A is still 1
        bra @hmove
@right: add16 vx, t16
        stz facing
        lda #1
        sta running
@hmove:
        ; steps = (vx + 128) >> 8 ; dir = sign
        lda vx
        cmp #$80                    ; C = carry out of vx_lo + 128
        lda vx+1
        adc #0                      ; A = high byte of vx + 128 = the step count
        sta dpx
        and #$80
        beq :+
        lda #$FF
:       sta dpx+1
argument: Two changes. (1) Only the high byte of vx+128 is ever wanted, so materialising the whole 16-bit sum in dpx is waste. mov16 dpx,vx is 12 cycles, add16i dpx,128 is 18 (clc 2, lda 3, adc 2, sta 3, lda 3, adc 2, sta 3), plus the 'sta dpx' that copies the high byte back down over the low byte = 33. The replacement needs no 16-bit store at all: 'cmp #$80' sets C exactly when vx_lo + 128 carries (vx_lo >= 128), so 'lda vx+1 / adc #0' is the high byte of the sum, and 'sta dpx' lands it where the old code left it. 3+2+3+2+3 = 13, saving 20 cycles and 13 bytes.
