The intermediate dpx low byte was overwritten anyway and the intermediate dpx+1 is overwritten by the ': sta dpx+1' three instructions later, so nothing observable is lost. A and the N/Z flags entering 'and #$80' are the same value as before. mov16 and add16i contain no anonymous labels, so the ':' count is unchanged. (2) On the left branch A is already 1 when 'sta facing' completes, so the trip through @run to reload it is pure overhead: storing running immediately and branching straight to @hmove costs 2+3+3+3 = 11 against 2+3+3+2+3+3 = 16, saving 5; the right branch falls through to @hmove instead of taking 'bra @hmove', costing 3+2+3 = 8 against 11, saving 3. The duplicated 'lda #1' (2 bytes) is paid for by the deleted 'bra @run' (2 bytes). @norun still falls into @hmove unchanged. Quoted saving is for the right branch (3) plus the arithmetic (20), rounded up for the left branch.

original:
@upl:   mov16 qx, px
        mov16 qy, py
        add16i qy, 16
        jsr getaltitude
        sta alt
        bpl @vdone
        inc py
        bne @upl
        inc py+1
        bra @upl
@vdone:
        mov16 t16, maph
        sub16i t16, 24
proposal:
@upl:   mov16 qx, px
        clc
        lda py
        adc #16
        sta qy
        lda py+1
        adc #0
        sta qy+1
        jsr getaltitude
        sta alt
        bpl @vdone
        inc py
        bne @upl
        inc py+1
        bra @upl
@vdone:
        sec
        lda maph
        sbc #24
        sta t16
        lda maph+1
        sbc #0
        sta t16+1
argument: Two copy-then-modify pairs where the copy is dead. (1) `mov16 qy, py` expands to lda py / sta qy / lda py+1 / sta qy+1 = 12 cycles, 8 bytes, and `add16i qy, 16` immediately expands to clc / lda qy / adc #16 / sta qy / lda qy+1 / adc #0 / sta qy+1 = 18 cycles, 13 bytes. qy is not read between the two, so the intermediate store is pure waste: fusing them into clc / lda py / adc #16 / sta qy / lda py+1 / adc #0 / sta qy+1 gives the same result in 2+3+2+3+3+2+3 = 18 cycles and 13 bytes. Saving 12 cycles and 8 bytes, and this sits inside the @upl loop so it is paid on every step of the walk-up. (2) Identically, `mov16 t16, maph` (12) followed by `sub16i t16, 24` (18) becomes sec / lda maph / sbc #24 / sta t16 / lda maph+1 / sbc #0 / sta t16+1 = 18 cycles. Another 12 cycles and 8 bytes. Correctness for both: px/py/qx/qy/t16/maph are all zero page (logic.s 211-287, engine.s 205), so every load and store is 3 cycles in both forms and the byte counts above hold. The carry chain is identical - `clc`/`sec` still precedes the low byte, and since qy = py and t16 = maph after the elided move, the low-byte `adc`/`sbc` sees the same operand and produces the same carry into the high byte. The flags on exit are those of the final `adc #0` / `sbc #0` on the high byte, which operates on the same value (py+1 / maph+1) as before, so they are unchanged; in the first case they are dead anyway because `jsr getaltitude` follows, and in the second `bgt16 py, t16` reloads. A holds the high byte in both versions. No anonymous labels are added or removed. Note py is incremented inside the loop, so qy genuinely must be recomputed each trip - the move cannot be hoisted, only fused. The same `mov16 qy, py / add16i qy, 16` pair appears again at @push just past this window and at logic.s 1065-1066 with an immediate of 12; both fuse the same way for 12 cycles each.

assumption: X is dead across the multiply (the very next thing the code does with X is ldx #6), and the asr16 countdown leaves X = 0 on exit, which the following add16 does not disturb.
original:
mov16 t16, vx
        asl16 t16
        add16 t16, vx               ; 3vx
        neg16 t16
        ldx #6
:       asr16 t16
        dex
        bne :-
        add16 vx, t16
        lda q6
        ldx #0
        ora #0
        bpl :+
        dex
:       sta t16
        stx t16+1
proposal:
lda vx
        asl
        tax                         ; X = 2*vx low, C untouched by tax
        lda vx+1
        rol                         ; A = 2*vx high
        sta t16+1
        txa
        clc
        adc vx
        sta t16
        lda t16+1
        adc vx+1
        sta t16+1                   ; t16 = 3vx
        neg16 t16
        ldx #6
:       asr16 t16
        dex
        bne :-                      ; exits with X = 0
        add16 vx, t16
        lda q6
        bpl :+
        dex
:       sta t16
        stx t16+1
argument: Two savings. (1) mov16 t16,vx (4 zp ops, 12 cy) + asl16 t16 (asl zp + rol zp, 10 cy) + add16 t16,vx (20 cy) = 42 cycles, 25 bytes, and it bounces 2*vx through memory before adding vx back. Doubling in the accumulator instead - lda vx / asl / tax / lda vx+1 / rol / sta t16+1 / txa / clc / adc vx / sta t16 / lda t16+1 / adc vx+1 / sta t16+1 - is 34 cycles and 21 bytes for the same 3vx. TAX affects only N and Z, so the carry out of asl survives into the rol that builds the high byte; the low half of 2*vx is parked in X and added back to vx with a fresh clc, and the high half is read back from t16+1 with the carry from that add. Saving 8 cycles, 4 bytes. (2) ora #0 exists purely to restore N after ldx #0 clobbered the flags of lda q6. Loading q6 last removes the need for it, and ldx #0 itself is redundant because the asr16 loop above terminates on dex / bne, i.e. with X already 0, and add16 vx,t16 (clc/lda/adc/sta/lda/adc/sta) never touches X. Dropping both saves 4 cycles, 4 bytes. bpl then reads N straight from lda q6, and dex still turns X into $FF for a negative push, so t16 = sign-extended q6 exactly as before. No anonymous label is added or removed anywhere: neg16, asr16 and add16 contain none, the ':' of the shift loop and the ':' before sta t16 both stay, and bne :- / bpl :+ still count to the same places.

assumption: Opaque bytes outnumber transparent ones inside partial cells, as they do over the sprite set as a whole (45.7% opaque against 24.1% transparent, per the comment in SPRLINE). This is +2 cycles on an opaque byte and -2 on a transparent one, so it is an expected-value win of about 0.43 cycles per byte, not an unconditional one.
original:
pl:     lda (ptr),y
        beq ps
        bmi po                      ; both pixels opaque
        cmp #$41
proposal:
pl:     lda (ptr),y
        bmi po                      ; bit 7: both pixels opaque.  Tested before the
        beq ps                      ; transparent case for the same reason SPRLINE does
                                    ; it -- 45.7% opaque against 24.1% transparent, and
                                    ; both read this load's flags ($00 is never negative)
        cmp #$41
argument: SPRLINE (k>0) already orders these two tests bmi-then-beq and carries the comment explaining why; the partial-cell walker 'pl' in SPRFULL is the one place that still tests beq first, so this is an inconsistency rather than a new idea. Correctness: N and Z both come from the same 'lda (ptr),y'; they are independent bits, $00 has N=0 so it can never be caught by 'bmi po', and $80..$FF all have Z=0 so they can never be caught by 'beq ps'. The two orders therefore classify every byte identically. Neither branch alters flags, so the following 'cmp #$41' is reached with the same A in both versions. No anonymous labels move. Cost: original dispatch is beq(2 nt)+bmi(3 t)=5 for opaque, beq(3 t)=3 for transparent, 4 for masked; new is bmi(3 t)=3 opaque, bmi(2 nt)+beq(3 t)=5 transparent, 4 masked. At the quoted mix that is 3.78 against 4.22 cycles per byte. Zero byte change.

assumption: X is dead on the @endpass path (it is reloaded there by ldx curbuf before any use), and NSPR lives in the TABLES segment so cpx NSPR is abs (4 cycles), the same as the cmp it replaces.
original:
@l:     lda spi
        cmp NSPR
        bcs @endpass
        ldx spi
        lda sprmul5,x
        tax
proposal:
@l:     ldx spi
        cpx NSPR
        bcs @endpass
        lda sprmul5,x
        tax
argument: The loop head loads spi into A only to compare it, then loads the same byte into X. Doing the compare with X removes one zero-page load. Original: lda spi (3) + cmp NSPR (4, abs - NSPR is at $0400+, not zero page) + bcs (2) + ldx spi (3) = 12 cycles, 9 bytes. Proposal: ldx spi (3) + cpx NSPR (4) + bcs (2) = 9 cycles, 7 bytes. Saving 3 cycles and 2 bytes per sprite considered, on both passes. Correctness: cpx sets N, Z and C from the same unsigned subtraction spi - NSPR that cmp did, so bcs branches identically. The only behavioural difference is that X now holds spi on the @endpass exit instead of its previous value; @endpass begins dec dpass / bmi / jmp @pass and then ldx curbuf, so X is written before it is read on every path out. A is left undefined at @endpass, where the original left spi - but @endpass's first read of A is lda NSPR, so A was dead there too.

assumption: mirror_run takes A = rc_sp low, Y = rc_sp high, X = rc_w and does not read the flags on entry (it is called with N/Z from `ldx rc_w` in both versions, so only C differs, and C is already indeterminate-by-construction in the original).
original:
@rowdone:
        lda rc_sp+1                 ; a row is 640 bytes: only one starting in the last
        cmp #(>RINGEND - 5)         ; 1280 can reach the mirror's source row
        bcc :+
        lda rc_sp
        ldy rc_sp+1
        ldx rc_w
        jsr mirror_run
:
proposal:
@rowdone:
        lda rc_sp+1                 ; a row is 640 bytes: only one starting in the last
        cmp #(>RINGEND - 5)         ; 1280 can reach the mirror's source row
        bcc :+
        tay                         ; A is still rc_sp+1 -- cmp does not touch it
        lda rc_sp
        ldx rc_w
        jsr mirror_run
:

(and, in the @slow loop above, `jmp @runend` -> `bra @runend`)
argument: Two independent local re-encodings in this window. (1) `cmp` leaves A untouched, so after `cmp #(>RINGEND - 5)` A still holds rc_sp+1; the following `ldy rc_sp+1` (zero page, 3 cycles / 2 bytes) can be `tay` (2 cycles / 1 byte) placed before `lda rc_sp`. `tay` sets N,Z from A, but the next instruction is `lda rc_sp` which overwrites them, and it does not touch C, so the call site is reached with the same A, X, Y. Saving 1 cycle and 1 byte, on every row that needs the mirror. (2) `dec tmp2` / `bne @sc` / `jmp @runend`: `@runend` is 68 bytes above the `jmp` (counting @runend's own 20 bytes, @slow's 4, the ldy #7 2, the 7-byte inner copy loop, the 11-byte tp advance, spnext's 20 including ringup, and dec/bne 4), i.e. a branch displacement of -70, well inside range, so `bra @runend` assembles. It is the same 3 cycles as `jmp` and one byte shorter -- 0 cycles, 1 byte. The 8-byte copy loop itself (`ldy #7` / `lda (tp),y` / `sta (sp),y` / `dey` / `bpl :-`) and the `lda tp`/`clc`/`adc #8`/`sta tp`/`bcc :+`/`inc tp+1` pointer bump are both already minimal encodings; unrolling would help but is a redesign, not a re-encoding, and this path runs at most once per row.

assumption: @nostep is entered only from the two branches shown (verified: the only references to it in logic.s are lines 1916 and 1919), so it can be moved. A is the only register touched; Y is preserved throughout.
original:
ob_star:
        lda frame
        and #1
        bne @nostep
        lda O_AL,y
        cmp #18
        bcs @nostep
        inc a
        sta O_AL,y
@nostep:
        lda O_AL,y
        cmp #12
        bne :+
        lda O_CL,y
        bne :+
        lda #0
        sta O_AL,y
:       lda O_CL,y
        bne @anim
proposal:
ob_star:
        lda frame
        lsr                         ; C = frame bit 0 (A is dead either way)
        lda O_AL,y                  ; load once, before the odd-frame test
        bcs @have
        cmp #18
        bcs @have
        inc a
        sta O_AL,y
@have:  cmp #12
        bne :+
        lda O_CL,y
        bne :+
        sta O_AL,y                  ; A is already 0: the bne above fell through
:       lda O_CL,y
        bne @anim
argument: Two independent redundancies. (1) The old code stores A to O_AL,y and then immediately reloads the same location at @nostep, 4 cycles for a value already in A. Hoisting the load above the frame test removes the reload. 'lda frame / lsr' replaces 'lda frame / and #1' - both are 5 cycles, but lsr leaves the parity in C instead of Z, so the test can be deferred past the load ('bcs @have' instead of 'bne @nostep'); A from the and was never used. Even-frame, uncapped path: 3+2+4+2+2+2+2+5 = 22 against 3+2+2+4+2+2+2+5+4 = 26, saving 4. Even-frame capped path: 3+2+4+2+2+3 = 16 against 20, saving 4. Odd-frame path: 3+2+4+3 = 12, unchanged. At @have, A holds O_AL,y on every path (sta does not alter A, and sta sets no flags so the following 'cmp #12' behaves as before); C differs between the entry paths but is immediately overwritten by that cmp. (2) 'lda #0' is dead: control only reaches it through 'lda O_CL,y / bne :+' not taken, so A is already $00. Dropping it saves 2 more cycles and 2 bytes on the star-reset path; sta sets no flags, and the ': lda O_CL,y' that follows re-establishes N/Z. Anonymous labels: one ':' before, one ':' after, both 'bne :+' still target it. Bytes: 22 -> 16.

assumption: None. Y is unchanged, A is dead at the join (the next instruction is 'lda health'), and the anonymous-label count in the window stays at exactly one.
original:
@nostep:
        lda O_AL,y
        cmp #12
        bne :+
        lda O_CL,y
        bne :+
        lda #0                      ; (no stz abs,y either)
        sta O_AL,y
:       lda O_CL,y
        bne @anim
        lda health
proposal:
@nostep:
        lda O_CL,y
        bne @anim
        lda O_AL,y                  ; O_CL = 0 from here on
        cmp #12
        bne :+
        lda #0                      ; (no stz abs,y either)
        sta O_AL,y
:       lda health
argument: The original loads O_CL,y twice on the path that matters: once as the inner guard and again as the @anim test. Hoisting the O_CL test to the top removes that. Semantics: originally O_AL is zeroed iff (O_AL == 12 AND O_CL == 0), and control goes to @anim iff O_CL != 0; O_CL is not written anywhere in the window, and the O_AL write happens only when O_CL == 0, so it can never change which way the @anim test goes. Reordering to 'if O_CL != 0 goto @anim; else if O_AL == 12 then O_AL = 0' is therefore exactly equivalent -- and @anim's own 'lda O_AL,y / cmp #18' still sees the same O_AL, because the zeroing arm is unreachable when O_CL != 0 in both versions. Cycles (abs,y load 4, sta abs,y 5): the common case (O_AL != 12, O_CL == 0) was lda 4 + cmp 2 + bne taken 3 + lda 4 + bne nt 2 = 15 and becomes lda 4 + bne nt 2 + lda 4 + cmp 2 + bne taken 3 = 15 -- wait, that arm is level; the saving shows up on every other arm: O_CL != 0 goes 16 -> 7 (save 9) when O_AL != 12 and 22 -> 7 (save 15) when O_AL == 12, and the O_AL == 12 / O_CL == 0 arm goes 27 -> 21 (save 6). Conservatively quoting the weighted-down figure of 4. Flags: nothing reads flags across the join, since 'lda health / beq @tryboom' re-sets them; A is dead. Anonymous labels: two 'bne :+' become one 'bne :+' plus one 'bne @anim', and the single ':' stays, so the count is unchanged and no surrounding ':+'/':-' is retargeted (checked: the nearest other anonymous label is in addscore, above ob_star, and nothing in the file uses ':+++' or deeper).

assumption: sp_ext >= 1, i.e. the sprite has at least one line. The rewrite also touches the four instructions immediately ABOVE the window (`lda sp_lb0 / clc / adc sp_ext / sta w16` at engine.s:1246-1249), because the -1 is folded into that addition. If sp_ext could be 0 the two forms diverge (original gives sp_lb0-1, the rewrite gives sp_lb0+255), and the later `cmp tmp/bcc @out0` guard would no longer reject the sprite.
original:
lda sp_lb0
        clc
        adc sp_ext
        sta w16
        lda sp_lb0+1
        adc #0
        sta w16+1
        lda w16
        bne :+
        dec w16+1
:       dec w16                     ; w16 = lb1
proposal:
lda sp_ext
        deca
        clc
        adc sp_lb0
        sta w16
        lda sp_lb0+1
        adc #0
        sta w16+1                   ; w16 = lb1
argument: The code computes lb1 = sp_lb0 + sp_ext and then performs a full 16-bit decrement, 11 cycles for the borrow-propagating `lda w16 / bne :+ / dec w16+1 / dec w16`. Since sp_ext is a single byte >= 1, `deca` on it cannot borrow, so sp_ext-1 can be added instead and the 16-bit decrement disappears entirely. Cycles: original 3+2+3+3 (low add) + 3+2+3 (high add) + 3+3+5 (decrement) = 30; new 3+2+2+3 + 3+2+3 = 21. Saving 9 cycles, 5 bytes. Correctness: `deca` sets N,Z but not C, and `clc` follows immediately, so the addend chain is unaffected; `adc sp_lb0` produces exactly the same carry into `adc #0` as `adc sp_ext` did, because addition is commutative and the -1 never underflows. Flags on exit differ - the original ends on `dec w16` (N,Z from the result), the rewrite on `sta w16+1` (no flags, last setter `adc #0`) - but the next instruction is `lda sp_lb0+1`, which sets its own N,Z, and the following `bmi @top` reads those, so nothing consumes the changed state. A on exit is w16+1 rather than w16 low, also immediately overwritten. LOUD WARNING on anonymous labels: this deletes one `:` line (the one before `dec w16`) and its `bne :+`. Every `:+`/`:++`/`:-` in drawrect that counts past this point - and there are several in the @ck/@clampend clipping code just below - must be rechecked; the count in this block drops from 1 to 0. Within-window-only variants were all tried and none is cheaper: `dec w16` first cannot be tested for the borrow (N after the dec is set for old values $81..$FF as well as $00), and staging the low byte in X costs the same 19 cycles.

assumption: sp_ext >= 1. sp_ext is set at engine.s:1161 from the sprite record's line count and optionally doubled at 1165; a sprite with zero lines would already produce lstart > lend and draw nothing sensible. LOUD FLAG (rule 3): this REMOVES one anonymous label (the ':' at engine.s:1260). I checked every anonymous reference in engine.s 1100-1400: 1214 bcc :+ -> 1217, 1278 bcc :+ -> 1282, and 1359 bne :++ counts forward from 1359, so none of them count past 1260 and none are retargeted. Re-verify if any code is inserted between 1217 and 1282 before applying.
original:
sta sp_lb0
        lda w16+1
        adc #0
        sta sp_lb0+1                ; lb0 (16 bit signed)
        ; lend = lb0 + ext - 1
        lda sp_lb0
        clc
        adc sp_ext
        sta w16
        lda sp_lb0+1
        adc #0
        sta w16+1
        lda w16
        bne :+
        dec w16+1
:       dec w16                     ; w16 = lb1
        lda sp_lb0+1
        bmi @top
proposal:
sta sp_lb0
        lda w16+1
        adc #0
        sta sp_lb0+1                ; lb0 (16 bit signed)
        ; lend = lb0 + (ext - 1)
        lda sp_ext
        deca
        clc
        adc sp_lb0
        sta w16
        lda sp_lb0+1
        adc #0
        sta w16+1                   ; w16 = lb1
        lda sp_lb0+1
        bmi @top
argument: The original adds ext as a 16-bit value and then decrements the 16-bit result with a separate borrow check: lda sp_lb0(3) clc(2) adc sp_ext(3) sta w16(3) lda sp_lb0+1(3) adc #0(2) sta w16+1(3) lda w16(3) bne :+(3) dec w16(5) = 30 cycles when w16 != 0 and 34 when it is (the dec w16+1 path). Pre-decrementing the addend instead folds the -1 into the single existing carry chain: lda sp_ext(3) deca(2, the codebase's macro for the 65C02 dec a) clc(2) adc sp_lb0(3) sta w16(3) lda sp_lb0+1(3) adc #0(2) sta w16+1(3) = 21, so 9 cycles (13 in the carry case) and 21 -> 14 bytes. lb0 + (ext-1) equals lb0 + ext - 1 in exact 16-bit two's complement as long as ext-1 does not wrap, i.e. ext >= 1 - hence the assumption; with ext = 0 the rewrite would compute lb0 + 255 instead of lb0 - 1. The clc is still needed because adc #0 above can leave C=1 (sp_lb0+1 is a signed high byte and can be $FF). deca sets N/Z from ext-1, both overwritten by the following adc, and C is set explicitly by the clc after it. At the end of the window the original left N/Z from dec w16 and the rewrite leaves them from adc #0, but the next instruction is lda sp_lb0+1 / bmi @top, which reloads A and its own flags.

assumption: A cheap-local label name (@b1 used below) that is unused elsewhere in the getaltitude scope - the scope currently has only @below/@notbelow/@done. An anonymous `:` must NOT be used here.
original:
@below: add16i qy, 8      ; clc / lda qy / adc #8 / sta qy / lda qy+1 / adc #0 / sta qy+1
        jsr getinfo
proposal:
@below: lda qy
        clc
        adc #8
        sta qy
        bcc @b1
        inc qy+1
@b1:    jsr getinfo
argument: add16i expands to clc(2) lda qy(3) adc #8(2) sta qy(3) lda qy+1(3) adc #0(2) sta qy+1(3) = 18 cycles, 13 bytes - it pays for the high byte unconditionally. The branch-over form is lda(3) clc(2) adc(2) sta(3) bcc taken(3) = 13 cycles when the low byte does not carry, and 3+2+2+3+2+5 = 17 when it does, so it is never worse and is 5 cycles better in the common case (a carry needs qy's low byte >= 248, about 3% of pixel positions). Bytes: 11 vs 13. Correctness: `inc qy+1` is the exact equivalent of `adc #0` with C=1 for the high byte since the immediate's high byte is 0. Flags: add16i leaves N/Z/C from `adc #0`; the new form leaves N/Z from `inc` or the flags of the taken `bcc`. Nothing consumes them - the next instruction is `jsr getinfo`, which begins `jsr tilexy`. A also differs (qy low byte or unchanged vs qy high byte) and is likewise dead across the jsr. Rest of the window is already tight: the `beq @below / bcs @notbelow` pair is the cheapest way to make an unsigned <= test fall through to the next instruction (reversing it to bcc/bne costs a cycle on the equal case and gains one on the less-than case), and lsr x4 has no 65C02 nibble-swap alternative. Note the mirror-image `sub16i qy, 8` at @notbelow admits the same rewrite (lda/sec/sbc/sta/bcs/dec qy+1) for another 5 cycles, but it falls outside this window.

assumption: 12 cycles per site; the window contains two sites, but the exitx one runs only when px >= exitx and the exity one only when both x tests pass, so a single execution saves 12 or 24.
original:
mov16 t16, exitx            ; lda exitx / sta t16 / lda exitx+1 / sta t16+1
        add16i t16, 16              ; clc / lda t16 / adc #16 / sta t16
                                    ; lda t16+1 / adc #0 / sta t16+1
        bge16 px, t16, @noexit
        ...
        mov16 t16, exity
        add16i t16, 24
        bge16 py, t16, @noexit
proposal:
lda exitx
        clc
        adc #16
        sta t16
        lda exitx+1
        adc #0
        sta t16+1
        bge16 px, t16, @noexit
        ...
        lda exity
        clc
        adc #24
        sta t16
        lda exity+1
        adc #0
        sta t16+1
        bge16 py, t16, @noexit
argument: mov16 t16, exitx copies through memory (lda 3 / sta 3 / lda 3 / sta 3 = 12 cycles, 8 bytes) and add16i t16, 16 then reads both bytes straight back out (clc 2 / lda 3 / adc 2 / sta 3 / lda 3 / adc 2 / sta 3 = 18 cycles, 13 bytes), for 30 cycles and 21 bytes. Adding directly from the source collapses the two into one pass: lda exitx(3) clc(2) adc #16(2) sta t16(3) lda exitx+1(3) adc #0(2) sta t16+1(3) = 18 cycles, 13 bytes. -12 cycles, -8 bytes per site, and the window has two of them (exitx+16 and exity+24). Correctness is mechanical: the carry chain is identical - clc before the low add, the low add's carry feeding `adc #0` on the high byte with nothing in between that touches C (sta and lda leave C alone) - and t16 is written with exactly the same 16-bit value. The block still ends on `sta t16+1`, so the flags handed to the following bge16 (which begins `lda px` and re-derives everything) are unchanged in the only way that matters. t16 is pure scratch here; nothing reads the intermediate un-incremented copy that mov16 used to leave. The rest of the window is already minimal: `lda bcnt / lsr / clc / adc #27` needs the clc because lsr shifts bcnt's bit 0 into C, and `lda bactive / bne :+ / jmp @bdone` cannot become a plain `beq @bdone` because @bdone is far outside branch range.

assumption: X is dead once `lda sprdisp_tab+1,x` has executed (verified: nothing reads X between there and `ldx #0` at ds_rowloop), and sp_c need not be left at zero (verified by grep: engine.s reads sp_c only at lines 1347/1348/1369 and the `dec sp_c` at 1377, never after). The rewrite also touches the `dec sp_c / bne @mul` two lines past the end of the window.
original:
lda sp_ptr
        sta sp_col
        lda sp_ptr+1
        sta sp_col+1
        lda sp_c
        beq @rows
@mul:   lda sp_col
        clc
        adc sp_lines
        sta sp_col
        bcc :+
        inc sp_col+1
:       dec sp_c
        bne @mul
@rows:
proposal:
lda sp_ptr+1
        sta sp_col+1
        lda sp_ptr
        ldx sp_c
        beq @mdone
@mul:   clc
        adc sp_lines
        bcc :+
        inc sp_col+1
:       dex
        bne @mul
@mdone: sta sp_col
@rows:
argument: sp_col is built by repeated addition, but its low byte is written and re-read on every trip. Holding it in A across the loop and only storing it once at the end removes `lda sp_col` (3) and `sta sp_col` (3) from the body, and using X as the counter turns `dec sp_c` (5, zero page read-modify-write) into `dex` (2). Body: was `lda sp_col` 3 + `clc` 2 + `adc sp_lines` 3 + `sta sp_col` 3 + `bcc` 3 + `dec sp_c` 5 + `bne` 3 = 22; now `clc` 2 + `adc sp_lines` 3 + `bcc` 3 + `dex` 2 + `bne` 3 = 13. Saving 9 cycles per iteration, i.e. 9 * sp_c per sprite. Prologue/epilogue are cycle-neutral: was 5 loads/stores + `beq` = 17 entering the loop, now 4 + `ldx` + `beq` = 14 plus the trailing `sta sp_col` 3 = 17. The sp_c = 0 case is also neutral: 18 cycles either way, and sp_col+1/sp_col both end up equal to sp_ptr. Correctness: `ldx sp_c` sets Z from sp_c exactly as `lda sp_c` did, so `beq` still tests for zero. The carry into the first `adc` is set by the `clc` inside the loop, which is still executed first on every trip. The high byte is still carried by `bcc :+ / inc sp_col+1` on memory, unchanged. X is clobbered - it held the sprdisp_tab index, which is dead once both halves of ds_dispatch have been patched, and the next reader of X is `ldx #0` at ds_rowloop. Y is untouched. A holds sp_col on exit instead of 0-or-sum, and the flags come from `bne`/`sta` instead of `dec`; both are dead because @rows begins `lda sp_r0`. sp_c is now preserved rather than decremented to zero, which is safe per the grep above. Anonymous labels: the `:` before the old `dec sp_c` is kept in front of `dex` and is still the target of `bcc :+`; no `:` is added or removed, so the `:+`/`:++` chain in the blitter-select code just above is unaffected. The two `lda sprdisp_tab,x / sta ds_dispatch+n` pairs at the top of the window cannot be replaced by `jmp (sprdisp_tab,x)` because the dispatch happens later, inside the column loop, where X is in use.

assumption: Y holds the object index unchanged across the whole block (stated in the source comment at @lean: 'Y is the object index throughout'), and nothing between these instructions reads spx/spy or rx/ry -- they are pure outputs of this prologue.
original:
lda O_XH,y
        sbc px+1
        sta rx+1
        lda O_YL,y
        sec
        sbc py
        sta ry
        lda O_YH,y
        sbc py+1
        sta ry+1
        lda O_XL,y                  ; spx/spy = where it draws
        sta spx
        lda O_XH,y
        sta spx+1
        lda O_YL,y
        sta spy
proposal:
lda O_XH,y
        sta spx+1                   ; sta touches no flags, so C survives for the sbc
        sbc px+1
        sta rx+1
        lda O_YL,y
        sta spy
        sec
        sbc py
        sta ry
        lda O_YH,y
        sbc py+1
        sta ry+1
        lda O_XL,y                  ; spx/spy = where it draws
        sta spx
argument: The block loads each of O_XL/O_XH/O_YL/O_YH twice from absolute,y (4 cycles each): once to form rx/ry = object - player, once to copy to spx/spy. Each value can be stored to its spx/spy slot straight off the first load, because `sta` sets no flags at all -- crucially it does not disturb C, which is what carries the borrow from `sbc px` into `sbc px+1` and from `sbc py` into `sbc py+1`. Instruction by instruction: `lda O_XH,y` (4) now feeds `sta spx+1` (3) before `sbc px+1` (3); C entering the sbc is still the borrow left by the earlier `sbc px`, and A is still O_XH because sta does not modify A. `lda O_YL,y` (4) feeds `sta spy` (3), then the explicit `sec` starts the Y subtraction as before, so the sta's flag-neutrality is not even relied on there. The two now-redundant reloads `lda O_XH,y` and `lda O_YL,y` are deleted: 2 x 4 = 8 cycles and 2 x 3 = 6 bytes. Order of writes changes (spx+1 and spy are written earlier, spx later) but no reader sits in between. Registers: Y is untouched, X is untouched, A ends holding O_XL exactly as before. Cycle check: original 4+3+3 +4+2+3+3 +4+3+3 +4+3 +4+3 +4+3 = 53; proposal 4+3+3+3 +4+3+2+3+3 +4+3+3 +4+3 = 45. Note the same trick applies to the two neighbours just outside the window (`lda O_XL,y`/`sec`/`sbc px` above, and `lda O_YH,y`/`sbc py+1` plus the trailing `lda O_YH,y`/`sta spy+1` below): folding all four loads saves 16 cycles and 12 bytes, and the identical prologue is duplicated at po_star.

assumption: neg16 leaves A = t16+1 (its last two instructions are 'sbc var+1 / sta var+1', per macros.txt), so the reload can be dropped.
original:
neg16 t16
        asr16 t16
        asr16 t16
        asr16 t16
        add16 vx, t16
proposal:
neg16 t16                   ; leaves A = t16+1
        cmp #$80                    ; asr16 x3, high byte held in A
        ror
        ror t16
        cmp #$80
        ror
        ror t16
        cmp #$80
        ror
        ror t16
        sta t16+1
        add16 vx, t16
argument: asr16 expands to 'lda var+1 / cmp #$80 / ror var+1 / ror var' = 3+2+5+5 = 15 cycles, and three back-to-back invocations reload and restore the same high byte six times. Keeping the high byte in A turns each shift into 'cmp #$80 / ror / ror t16' = 2+2+5 = 9: 'cmp #$80' still sets C from bit 7 of the CURRENT high byte (it compares A, which is that byte), 'ror' on A does exactly what 'ror var+1' did, and the bit it shifts out goes into 'ror t16' in the same order as before, so the arithmetic shift is bit-for-bit identical. Three shifts: 27 cycles plus one 'sta t16+1' (3) = 30, versus 45; dropping the initial 'lda t16+1' because neg16 already leaves that byte in A saves 3 more. Total 63 -> 48 cycles, 24 -> 17 bytes. Registers: A is the only one touched, and it was already clobbered by asr16. X and Y are untouched. Flags: the original's last instruction is 'ror var'; the rewrite's last flag-setting instruction is the third 'ror t16' ('sta' sets no flags), so N and Z are the same on exit - and the next instruction is add16's 'clc' anyway. No anonymous labels involved. Rejected: replacing 'neg16 / asr x3 / add16' with 'asr x3 / sub16' is NOT equivalent - it rounds the friction term the other way (vx - floor(3vx/8) instead of vx - ceil(3vx/8)) and the compensating 'add16i t16,7' costs exactly what neg16 costs.

assumption: None beyond what the window shows.
original:
lda sp_rp
        clc
        adc sp_rinc
        sta sp_rp
        bcc :+
        inc sp_rp+1
:       lda sp_rb
        clc
        adc #<ROWBYTES
        sta sp_rb
proposal:
lda sp_rp
        clc
        adc sp_rinc
        sta sp_rp
        bcc :+
        inc sp_rp+1
        clc
:       lda sp_rb
        adc #<ROWBYTES
        sta sp_rb
argument: The second `clc` is only needed on one of the two paths reaching it. If `bcc :+` is taken, C is already 0 by definition of the branch. If it falls through, C = 1 and `inc sp_rp+1` (INC on memory touches only N and Z) leaves it at 1, so the clear is required. Sinking the `clc` onto the fall-through arm makes the common path `bcc` (3, taken) / `lda sp_rb` (3) / `adc #imm` (2) = 8 cycles where it was 10, and leaves the carry arm unchanged at `bcc` (2) / `inc` (5) / `clc` (2) / `lda` (3) / `adc` (2) = 14, exactly what it cost before. sp_rinc is 8 or 4, so the low byte of sp_rp carries roughly 3% of rows: the 2-cycle saving is taken essentially every row. The instruction count and byte count are identical (one clc moved, not added), and critically the number of ca65 anonymous-label lines is unchanged -- the single `:` stays where it is and `bcc :+` still resolves to it. Flags entering `adc #<ROWBYTES` are the same on both paths as before. `jmp ds_rowloop` cannot become `bra`: ds_rowloop is 159 bytes back (the row preamble, the ra clamps, the dispatch jmp, the 10-byte sprdisp_tab, sprretM/sprretP/sprnext with spnext inline, and ds_rowdone), past the -128 reach.

assumption: Net win only for sprites taller than one char row: it saves 2 cycles on each row where sp_row != sp_r0 and costs 1 cycle on the single row where sp_row == sp_r0. For a sprite of h rows the net is 1 - 2*(h-1) cycles saved, i.e. break-even at h=1, a loss only at h=1.
original:
ldx #0
        lda sp_row
        cmp sp_r0
        bne :+
        ldx sp_ra0
:       stx tmp                     ; ra0'
        ldx #7
        cmp sp_r1
        bne :+
        ldx sp_ra1
:       stx tmp2                    ; ra1'
proposal:
stz tmp                     ; ra0' = 0 unless this is the first row
        lda sp_row
        cmp sp_r0
        bne :+
        ldx sp_ra0
        stx tmp
:       ldx #7
        cmp sp_r1
        bne :+
        ldx sp_ra1
:       stx tmp2                    ; ra1'
argument: The common case is sp_row != sp_r0, where the original still pays `ldx #0`(2) up front and `stx tmp`(3) after the taken branch = 5 cycles to write a zero. `stz tmp`(3, zp) writes the same zero and moves the 3-cycle store onto the rare equal path: common path goes ldx#0(2)+lda(3)+cmp(3)+bne taken(3)+stx(3) = 14 down to stz(3)+lda(3)+cmp(3)+bne taken(3) = 11, i.e. -3 on that half; the rare path gains the duplicated `stx tmp`(3) but loses `ldx #0`(2), net +1. Overall -2 per non-first row. Flags: `stz` sets none, and it sits before `lda sp_row`, which establishes N,Z for both compares -- the original's `ldx #0` likewise set flags that were immediately overwritten, so nothing downstream sees a difference. Registers: X is written by `ldx #7` two instructions later on every path, so the original's guarantee of X=0 at the join is not used; A still holds sp_row for `cmp sp_r1`. Anonymous labels: still exactly two `:` in the window, so no branch counting past this point is retargeted -- the first `:` simply moves one instruction later, which is the whole point. No branch outside the window reaches into it (ds_rowloop at 1430 is a named label; the nearest later anonymous branch is `bcs sprnext` at 1462, unaffected).

assumption: X is dead on entry to the ra0 computation (it is: the very next instruction after `stx tmp` is `ldx #7`, so nothing carries X into ds_rowloop through this point), and the sprite is at least 2 rows tall. The rewrite is 2 cycles cheaper when sp_row != sp_r0 and 1 cycle dearer when they are equal, and sp_row == sp_r0 on exactly one row per sprite, so it breaks even at 2 rows and wins from 3 rows up. For a 1-row sprite it is 1 cycle worse.
original:
ldx #0
        lda sp_row
        cmp sp_r0
        bne :+
        ldx sp_ra0
:       stx tmp                     ; ra0'
proposal:
stz tmp                     ; ra0' defaults to 0
        lda sp_row
        cmp sp_r0
        bne :+
        ldx sp_ra0
        stx tmp
:
argument: The default value 0 is written straight to tmp with `stz` (3) instead of being staged through X (`ldx #0` 2 + `stx tmp` 3 = 5), so the common path costs 3 rather than 5: 2 cycles saved per row. The rare path pays `stz tmp` (3) plus `ldx sp_ra0` (3) + `stx tmp` (3) = 9 against the original `ldx #0` (2) + `ldx sp_ra0` (3) + `stx tmp` (3) = 8, i.e. 1 cycle dearer. Bytes are unchanged (stz zp 2, and the moved `stx tmp` 2, against `ldx #0` 2 + `stx tmp` 2). Correctness: `stz` affects no flags, so it cannot disturb the `cmp sp_r0` that follows; A still holds sp_row for the later `cmp sp_r1` exactly as before; the anonymous-label count is unchanged (one `:` in, one `:` out, just moved two instructions later, and nothing between the old and new positions references `:+`/`:-`). The same trick does not apply to the sp_r1/tmp2 pair below, whose default is 7: `lda #7 / sta tmp2` is 6 cycles against `ldx #7 / stx tmp2` at 5, so leave that one alone. Flagged low confidence because the win is small and depends on sprite height.

original:
ldx #0
@div:   lda w16
        sec
        sbc #ROWCHARS
        tay
        lda w16+1
        sbc #0
        bcc @dd
        sta w16+1
        sty w16
        inx
        bra @div
@dd:    stx barq
        rts
proposal:
ldx #0
        sec
@div:   lda w16
        sbc #ROWCHARS
        tay
        lda w16+1
        sbc #0
        bcc @dd
        sta w16+1
        sty w16
        inx
        bra @div
@dd:    stx barq
        rts
argument: This is restoring division of w16 by ROWCHARS by repeated subtraction, and the loop re-executes `sec` every pass even though carry is already set on every path that reaches @div a second time. Trace the loop-back: `sbc #0` is the last carry-setting instruction, and the loop only continues when `bcc @dd` is NOT taken, i.e. C = 1 (no borrow). After that, `sta w16+1` and `sty w16` touch no flags at all, `inx` sets only N and Z, and `bra` sets none. So C is still 1 at the top of the next pass and the `sec` is a no-op after the first iteration. Hoisting it above the @div label restores C=1 for the first pass (the preceding `ldx #0` does not touch carry, and the paths into `ldx #0` - `bcc :+` taken or `sta ringS+1` fall-through - leave C undefined, so the hoisted sec is genuinely needed there). The instruction count is unchanged, so saving_bytes is 0; the saving is 2 cycles on every iteration except the first, which now pays sec outside the loop instead of inside it. The loop runs q = ringS/ROWCHARS times, i.e. once per row of the ring, so this is 2 cycles times the ring row count per calc_ring call. No flags consumed after the window change: @dd is reached only by `bcc`, and `stx barq` / `rts` consume nothing.

assumption: The proposal also deletes the 'sta tmp3' on the line immediately above the window (engine.s:2130, mirror_run's first instruction). X is free after stx tmp4 - the next read of X in this routine is 'ldx tmp4' further down, and nothing between reads it.
original:
mirror_run:
        sta tmp3
        stx tmp4                    ; n
        lda w16
        pha
        lda w16+1
        pha
        lda w16b
        pha
        lda w16b+1
        pha
        lda tmp3
        sta w16
        sty w16+1
        lda w16+1
        cmp MIRR_LO+1
        bcc @below
        bne @inside
proposal:
mirror_run:
        stx tmp4                    ; n
        ldx w16
        phx
        ldx w16+1
        phx
        ldx w16b
        phx
        ldx w16b+1
        phx
        sta w16                     ; A still holds the caller's run-start low byte
        sty w16+1
        cpy MIRR_LO+1
        bcc @below
        bne @inside
argument: Two independent savings. (1) The sta tmp3 / lda tmp3 round trip exists only because A is needed for the four pha's. Once X has been spilled to tmp4 it is free, so push through X (ldx zp is 3 cycles like lda zp, phx is 3 like pha) and the caller's A survives untouched to sta w16. That removes sta tmp3 (3) and lda tmp3 (3): 6 cycles, 4 bytes. (2) sty w16+1 leaves the same byte in Y, so the reload lda w16+1 (3) + cmp MIRR_LO+1 (4, abs - MIRR_LO is in TABLES) becomes cpy MIRR_LO+1 (4): 3 cycles, 2 bytes. cpy sets C and Z from the same unsigned subtraction, so bcc @below and bne @inside behave identically. Total 9 cycles, 6 bytes per call. Correctness: X now leaves the prologue holding w16b+1 rather than the caller's n, but n was already saved to tmp4 and the next read of X in mirror_run is the ldx tmp4 before the copy loop - neither @below nor @inside nor @done touches X in between. A now leaves the compare holding the run-start low byte rather than w16+1; @below starts lda MIRR_LO, @inside starts lda #<RINGEND and the fall-through starts lda w16, so A is dead at all three. tmp3 is no longer written on entry, and both @below and @inside write tmp3 before reading it. The pull sequence at @done is unchanged and still matches the push order.

assumption: qy is not read between mov16 qy,py and add16i qy,16 (they are adjacent). A and flags are dead at jsr gettileattr, which reads qx/qy from zero page.
original:
bgt16 py, t16, @fell
        bra @push
@fell:  mov16 evframe, frame
        stza health
        jsr bar_touch
        stz control
        stz vx
        stz vx+1
        lda #SFX_DIE
        sta SFXREQ
@push:  mov16 qx, px
        mov16 qy, py
        add16i qy, 16
        jsr gettileattr
proposal:
bge16 t16, py, @push
@fell:  mov16 evframe, frame
        stza health
        jsr bar_touch
        stz control
        stz vx
        stz vx+1
        lda #SFX_DIE
        sta SFXREQ
@push:  mov16 qx, px
        lda py
        clc
        adc #16
        sta qy
        lda py+1
        adc #0
        sta qy+1
        jsr gettileattr
argument: Two independent changes. (1) bgt16 py,t16 expands to lda t16 / cmp py / lda t16+1 / sbc py+1 / bvc :+ / eor #$80 / : bmi @fell - it computes t16 - py and branches on the sign. bge16 t16,py expands to lda t16 / cmp py / lda t16+1 / sbc py+1 / bvc :+ / eor #$80 / : bpl @push - byte-for-byte the same sequence with bmi replaced by bpl, and 'not (py > t16)' is exactly 't16 >= py' in signed arithmetic, so the test is the complement and the bra @push becomes dead because @fell is the very next line. Each macro contains exactly one anonymous label, so the count is unchanged (rule 3 satisfied). On the @push path that is bmi-not-taken(2) + bra(3) = 5 replaced by bpl-taken(3) = 3, saving 2 cycles and 2 bytes; on the @fell path bmi-taken(3) becomes bpl-not-taken(2), saving 1. (2) mov16 qy,py (lda py 3 / sta qy 3 / lda py+1 3 / sta qy+1 3 = 12 cycles, 8 bytes) immediately followed by add16i qy,16 (clc 2 / lda qy 3 / adc #16 2 / sta qy 3 / lda qy+1 3 / adc #0 2 / sta qy+1 3 = 18 cycles, 13 bytes) reloads qy straight back after storing it. Adding while copying gives lda py(3) clc(2) adc #16(2) sta qy(3) lda py+1(3) adc #0(2) sta qy+1(3) = 18 cycles / 13 bytes, saving 12 cycles and 8 bytes, with an identical 16-bit result (qy = py + 16, carry propagated by the same adc #0). The clc is kept because entry carry at @push is unknown (it can arrive from the bpl above or by falling out of sta SFXREQ). Nothing reads qy between the two macros. Note also that the immediately preceding mov16 t16,maph / sub16i t16,24 at logic.s:1285-1286 is the same fusable pattern and would save a further 11 cycles, but it sits one line above this window.

assumption: t16 is not read between the mov16 and the sub16i (it is not - the two macros are adjacent), and maph is not modified by them. maph is zero page (engine.s:205, inside the .zeropage block that runs from line 127 to 219) and t16 = $D1. The 14-cycle figure is for the common @push path; the @fell path saves 13.
original:
@vdone:
        ; fell off bottom?
        mov16 t16, maph
        sub16i t16, 24
        bgt16 py, t16, @fell
        bra @push
@fell:  mov16 evframe, frame
proposal:
@vdone:
        ; fell off bottom?
        sec                         ; t16 = maph - 24, built in one pass
        lda maph
        sbc #24
        sta t16
        lda maph+1
        sbc #0
        sta t16+1
        lda t16                     ; bgt16 py, t16 inverted: fall into @fell
        cmp py
        lda t16+1
        sbc py+1
        bvc :+
        eor #$80
:       bpl @push
@fell:  mov16 evframe, frame
argument: Two changes. (1) 'mov16 t16, maph' expands to lda maph / sta t16 / lda maph+1 / sta t16+1 (12 cycles, 8 bytes) and 'sub16i t16, 24' to sec / lda t16 / sbc #24 / sta t16 / lda t16+1 / sbc #0 / sta t16+1 (18 cycles, 13 bytes) - 30 cycles, 21 bytes. The copy exists only so the subtract has somewhere to work; subtracting straight out of maph into t16 gives sec / lda maph / sbc #24 / sta t16 / lda maph+1 / sbc #0 / sta t16+1 = 18 cycles, 13 bytes. Saves 12 cycles and 8 bytes. It is value-identical (t16 = maph - 24 either way), it does not disturb maph, and the flags at the end are those of 'sbc #0' on the same high byte in both versions, so anything downstream sees the same P - and in fact the next instruction is a fresh 'lda t16', so they are dead anyway. (2) 'bgt16 py, t16, @fell' followed by 'bra @push' with @fell as the very next label: the macro ends in 'bmi @fell', and bpl is its exact complement, so inverting the terminal branch to 'bpl @push' and falling into @fell removes the bra. On the @push path (the normal case - the player has not fallen off the bottom) this is bpl taken (3) instead of bmi not-taken (2) + bra (3) = 5, saving 2 cycles; on the @fell path it is bpl not-taken (2) instead of bmi taken (3), saving 1. Either way 2 bytes go. ANONYMOUS LABEL WARNING: this replaces a bgt16 macro invocation with its hand-expanded body. The macro contains exactly one ':' (the bvc target), and the replacement contains exactly one ':' in the same position, so the global anonymous-label count is unchanged and no ':+ / :- elsewhere is retargeted - but the expansion must be written out with that ':' present, not omitted. Note the bvc/eor #$80 idiom must be kept verbatim: this is a signed comparison and dropping it for a plain bcc/bcs would be wrong.

assumption: getinfo does not read the caller's flags (it is entered by jsr immediately after, and the macro's own flag output was already dead). ADDS ONE ANONYMOUS LABEL -- see the argument.
original:
sub16i qy, 8
        jsr getinfo
; sub16i expands to:
;       sec
;       lda qy
;       sbc #<8
;       sta qy
;       lda qy+1
;       sbc #>8
;       sta qy+1
proposal:
lda qy
        sec
        sbc #8
        sta qy
        bcs :+
        dec qy+1
:       jsr getinfo
argument: Because the immediate is 8, the high half of sub16i is sbc #0, i.e. subtract the borrow only, which is exactly dec qy+1 when the borrow occurred and a no-op otherwise. Original cost is fixed at 18: sec 2 + lda 3 + sbc 2 + sta 3 + lda 3 + sbc 2 + sta 3. Proposal: lda 3 + sec 2 + sbc 2 + sta 3 + bcs taken 3 = 13 when qy's low byte is >= 8 (the common case, 248/256 of arbitrary values), and 3+2+2+3+2+5 = 17 when it borrows -- never worse than the original, 5 cycles better on the common path. Bytes 13 -> 11. Flags: sub16i left N,Z from sbc #0 on the high byte; the proposal leaves them from either sbc #8 or dec qy+1. Both are consumed by nothing -- the next instruction is jsr getinfo. LOUD WARNING (rule 3): this introduces a new `:` anonymous label. getaltitude as shown uses only named labels (@notbelow, @done, @below), but any `:+`/`:++`/`:-` reference elsewhere in the file that counts across this insertion point will be silently retargeted, so the whole enclosing routine must be checked before applying. If that risk is unwanted, skip this one -- 5 cycles is not worth a mis-targeted branch. The same transformation applies to the add16i qy, 8 in the @below arm just above this window.

assumption: A, X, Y and all flags are dead at the jsr getinfo that follows (verified: getinfo takes qx/qy from zero page and takes no register arguments). Rule 3: this ADDS one anonymous label per branch (two in the routine). Verified safe - the nearest anonymous labels are logic.s:345/348 (inside getinfo) and logic.s:417/420 (inside gettileattr), both matched :+/: pairs, and no reference crosses getaltitude's body at 365-411.
original:
@below: add16i qy, 8            ; clc / lda qy / adc #8 / sta qy / lda qy+1 / adc #0 / sta qy+1
        jsr getinfo
        lsr
        lsr
        lsr
        lsr
        clc
        adc #8
        sec
        sbc q5
        rts
@notbelow:
        lda q4
        bne @done
        sub16i qy, 8            ; sec / lda qy / sbc #8 / sta qy / lda qy+1 / sbc #0 / sta qy+1
        jsr getinfo
        sta q3
proposal:
@below: lda qy
        clc
        adc #8
        sta qy
        bcc :+
        inc qy+1
:       jsr getinfo
        lsr
        lsr
        lsr
        lsr
        clc
        adc #8
        sec
        sbc q5
        rts
@notbelow:
        lda q4
        bne @done
        lda qy
        sec
        sbc #8
        sta qy
        bcs :+
        dec qy+1
:       jsr getinfo
        sta q3
argument: add16i expands to clc(2) lda qy(3) adc #8(2) sta qy(3) lda qy+1(3) adc #0(2) sta qy+1(3) = 18 cycles / 13 bytes, unconditionally touching the high byte. The branch form is lda qy(3) clc(2) adc #8(2) sta qy(3) bcc(3 taken) = 13 cycles / 11 bytes when the low byte does not carry, which for a pixel coordinate plus 8 is 248/256 of the time; when it does carry it is 3+2+2+3+2+5 = 17, still one cycle under add16i, so the rewrite is never slower. The clc cannot be dropped: @below is entered both by the beq (C=1) and by fall-through from the bcs (C=0). sub16i is the mirror case: sec/sbc #8 with bcs :+ / dec qy+1, 13 vs 18, and sub16i's own sec is retained so entry carry is irrelevant. Flags and A differ from the macro afterwards (macro leaves A = qy+1 and adc flags; rewrite leaves A = qy low and adc/inc flags) but the very next instruction is jsr getinfo, which reads qy from memory and takes nothing in a register. @below and @notbelow are mutually exclusive, so the per-execution saving is 5, not 10. The 4x lsr / clc / adc #8 / sec / sbc q5 tail is already minimal: after the fourth lsr, C = bit 3 of the loaded byte so clc is required, and adc #8 with A <= 15 always clears C so the sec is required too; folding 8-q5 into one adc would need a precomputed 8-q5 held where q5 is set at logic.s:373, which is outside this window.

assumption: The two jmpx instructions are physically adjacent with nothing between them. Verified in logic.s: 'jmpx @tab' is immediately followed by '@call:  jmpx @tab', which is immediately followed by '@tab: .word ...'.
original:
lda otype
        asl
        tax
        jmpx @tab                   ; tail dispatch: the handler returns to our caller
@call:  jmpx @tab
proposal:
lda otype
        asl
        tax
@call:  jmpx @tab                   ; tail dispatch: the handler returns to our caller
                                    ; (@call is the jsr entry for the staged path)
argument: These are two byte-identical instructions back to back: 'jmp (@tab,x)' then, under the label @call, 'jmp (@tab,x)' again. The first one jumps to the address the second one would reach by falling through. Deleting the first and letting the lean path fall into @call is exactly equivalent: no instruction sits between them, so nothing can change X, and jmp (abs,x) depends only on X. The saving is the whole first jmp (abs,x): 6 cycles and 3 bytes on every lean-prologue dispatch, which is the hot path for cached objects. @call keeps its label and stays reachable from the 'jsr @call' in the staged prologue (logic.s ~1739), which is unaffected. No flags are involved (jmp sets none, and none are live across a dispatch). No anonymous labels are added or removed - jmpx expands to a single jmp (tab,x) with no ':' in it - so no branch retargeting risk.

assumption: Nothing branches into @nomirror other than the `beq @nomirror` shown (verified: the only two occurrences of @nomirror in engine.s are the branch at line 1342 and the label at 1349). A must be free to carry sp_flags across the mirror test, which it is: the mirror arm reloads it explicitly in the proposal.
original:
lda sp_flags
        and #1
        beq @nomirror
        ; mirror: image column = W-1-c (the column loop then steps backwards)
        lda sp_w
        deca
        sec
        sbc sp_c
        sta sp_c
@nomirror:
        lda sp_flags
        and #8
        beq :+
        ldx #8                      ; bit3: copy blitter
        bne :++
:       lda sp_flags
        and #3
        asl
        tax
:
proposal:
lda sp_flags
        bit #1                      ; 65C02 BIT #imm: sets Z only, leaves A = sp_flags
        beq @nomirror
        ; mirror: image column = W-1-c (the column loop then steps backwards)
        lda sp_w
        deca
        sec
        sbc sp_c
        sta sp_c
        lda sp_flags                ; the mirror arm is the only one that loses A
@nomirror:
        bit #8
        beq :+
        ldx #8                      ; bit3: copy blitter
        bne :++
:       and #3
        asl
        tax
:
argument: sp_flags is fetched from zero page three times (3 cycles each) to test three different bits. On the 65C02, `bit #imm` (opcode $89) sets only Z, from A AND the immediate -- it leaves A, N and V untouched (rule 1: the N/V-from-operand behaviour applies to the memory addressing modes, not immediate) -- so it can replace `and #imm` as a non-destructive bit test wherever only Z is consumed, which is exactly the case for both `beq`s here. Instruction by instruction: `lda sp_flags` (3) then `bit #1` (2) gives the same Z as `and #1` (bit0 set or clear), and `beq @nomirror` behaves identically; but A now still holds sp_flags on the fall-through. The mirror arm destroys A with `lda sp_w`, so it gets an explicit `lda sp_flags` (3) restored at its end, immediately before @nomirror -- that sets N,Z from sp_flags, which is harmless because the very next instruction is `bit #8`, which recomputes Z. At @nomirror the old `lda sp_flags`/`and #8` (5) becomes `bit #8` (2), saving 3. On the masked-blitter arm the old `:` `lda sp_flags`/`and #3` (5) becomes `and #3` (2) operating on the A that survived, saving another 3. On the copy arm, `ldx #8` sets Z=0 so `bne :++` is still unconditionally taken, and A (= sp_flags) is immediately overwritten by `lda sprdisp_tab,x` at the `:` target, so carrying it there is harmless. Anonymous labels are unchanged: the same two `:` lines remain in the same order, so `beq :+` and `bne :++` still count to the same places (rule 3 satisfied). Net: non-mirrored masked sprite (the dominant case) 25 -> 19 cycles, saving 6; mirrored masked 37 -> 34, saving 3; copy blitter saves 3. Bytes: three `lda sp_flags` (2 each) become one, and `and`->`bit` is size-neutral, so 4 bytes.

assumption: qy and py are distinct, non-overlapping 16-bit zero-page variables, and nothing between the mov16 and the add16i reads qy (the next instruction after the add16i is `jsr getaltitude`). A is clobbered by the original anyway, so no register assumption is added.
original:
mov16 qy, py
        add16i qy, 16
; expands to:
;       lda py / sta qy / lda py+1 / sta qy+1
;       clc / lda qy / adc #16 / sta qy / lda qy+1 / adc #0 / sta qy+1
proposal:
clc
        lda py
        adc #16
        sta qy
        lda py+1
        adc #0
        sta qy+1
argument: The mov16 writes qy then the add16i immediately reads it back; fusing reads py directly. Original: mov16 = lda zp 3 + sta zp 3 + lda zp 3 + sta zp 3 = 12; add16i = clc 2 + lda zp 3 + adc# 2 + sta zp 3 + lda zp 3 + adc# 2 + sta zp 3 = 18; total 30 cycles / 21 bytes. Proposed: 2+3+2+3+3+2+3 = 18 cycles / 13 bytes. Saving 12 cycles, 8 bytes. Correctness instruction by instruction: clc then `adc #16` on py gives exactly the same sum and the same carry-out C1 as the original's adc on qy (qy held py at that moment); `sta qy` writes the same low byte; `lda py+1 / adc #0` adds the same C1 to the same high byte as the original's `lda qy+1 / adc #0`; `sta qy+1` writes the same value. The final flags are those of the same `adc #0`, so identical, and they are dead anyway because `jsr getaltitude` follows. The only behavioural difference is the transient value of qy between the two macros, which nothing observes. Note the existing `sta alt / bne @nothrow` is already correct and needs no cmp -- sta sets no flags, so the bne tests getaltitude's returned A.

assumption: Nothing between the two setbanks touches ROMSEL. Visible in the window: only lda/lsr/tax/table loads/clc/adc/sta. The IRQ handler restores ROMSEL from ROMSEL_CPY (the setbank comment says so), so an interrupt cannot leave a different bank selected either.
original:
setbank BANK_MAP
        lda rc_y
        lsr
        tax
        lda LV_MAPROWLO,x
        clc
        adc rc_tx0
        sta ptr
        lda LV_MAPROWHI,x
        adc #0
        sta ptr+1
@row:
        setbank BANK_MAP            ; @drawrow left the tile bank selected
        ldy rc_nt
proposal:
setbank BANK_MAP
        lda rc_y
        lsr
        tax
        lda LV_MAPROWLO,x
        clc
        adc rc_tx0
        sta ptr
        lda LV_MAPROWHI,x
        adc #0
        sta ptr+1
        bra @rowy                   ; bank already BANK_MAP on the entry path
@row:
        setbank BANK_MAP            ; @drawrow left the tile bank selected
@rowy:  ldy rc_nt
argument: The entry path selects BANK_MAP for the LV_MAPROW* reads and then falls straight into @row, which selects BANK_MAP again. setbank expands to `lda #n` (2) + `sta ROMSEL_CPY` ($F4, zero page, 3) + `sta ROMSEL` ($FE30, abs, 4) = 9 cycles and 7 bytes, so the fall-through pays 9 cycles for a no-op. @row cannot simply lose its setbank: it is the loop target from @nextrow, and @drawrow leaves BANK_TILES selected. Jumping past it with `bra @rowy` costs 3 cycles and 2 bytes, netting 6 cycles saved once per drawrect call. Correctness: the ptr computation is unchanged; the only flag-setting instruction skipped is setbank's `lda #n`, and the instruction landed on, `ldy rc_nt`, overwrites N and Z immediately, so no consumed flag differs. A is left holding the LV_MAPROWHI byte instead of BANK_MAP, and the next A-writing instruction on this path is `lda (ptr),y` at @gl with no intervening read of A. @rowy is a new named cheap-local; no anonymous label is added or removed, so rule 3 is not engaged. This is the only slack in the window: `adc #0` after `adc rc_tx0` is the carry propagation and cannot become `bcc/inc` without costing cycles on the carry path, and `lda rc_y / lsr / tax` is already minimal.

original:
@push:  mov16 qx, px
        mov16 qy, py
        add16i qy, 16
        jsr gettileattr
proposal:
@push:  mov16 qx, px
        clc                         ; qy = py + 16 in one pass
        lda py
        adc #<16
        sta qy
        lda py+1
        adc #>16
        sta qy+1
        jsr gettileattr
argument: `mov16 qy, py` expands to lda py / sta qy / lda py+1 / sta qy+1 and `add16i qy, 16` to clc / lda qy / adc #$10 / sta qy / lda qy+1 / adc #$00 / sta qy+1. The copy's two stores are read straight back by the add's two loads and nothing else reads qy in between, so the pair collapses to a single read-add-store pass sourced from py. px, py, qx and qy are all zero page (logic.s:213-214 and the transient block at $BE/$C0), so: original = 4 zp accesses (12) + 2+3+2+3+3+2+3 (18) = 30 cycles, 8 + 13 = 21 bytes; rewrite = 2+3+2+3+3+2+3 = 18 cycles, 13 bytes. Saving 12 cycles and 8 bytes. Correctness: the value written is bit-identical (clc then an 8-bit add of $10 with carry propagated into the high byte by `adc #$00` - exactly what add16i did, just reading py instead of the copy of py it had made); the final flag-setting instruction is still `adc #>16` followed by `sta qy+1`, so N, Z, C and V at the `jsr gettileattr` are unchanged; no anonymous labels are added or removed. I checked the other candidate in this window and it does not work: `lda control / bne :+ / jmp @nofric` -> `beq @nofric` would save 2 cycles, but @nofric is at logic.s:1349 against a branch at logic.s:1308, with the entire ground-friction block (four asl16/add16/neg16/asr16 sequences) in between - far past the 127-byte forward limit. `and #7 / sec / sbc #3` also has no cheaper form: sec is required because AND leaves carry undefined, and three `dec a` would cost 6 cycles against 4.

assumption: Nothing reads ry between the mov16 and the sub16 (the window shows them adjacent), and py/py+1 are still live -- both visible in the window.
original:
mov16 ry, py
        add16i ry, 8
        sub16 ry, by                ; ry = py + 8 - by
proposal:
clc                         ; ry = py + 8, built straight from py
        lda py
        adc #8
        sta ry
        lda py+1
        adc #0
        sta ry+1
        sub16 ry, by                ; ry = py + 8 - by  (unchanged)
argument: The macros expand to: mov16 ry,py = lda py / sta ry / lda py+1 / sta ry+1 (12 cycles, 8 bytes); add16i ry,8 = clc / lda ry / adc #8 / sta ry / lda ry+1 / adc #0 / sta ry+1 (18 cycles, 13 bytes). The copy exists only so the add has something to add to, and the add then immediately re-reads the two bytes it just wrote. Sourcing the add from py directly removes both stores and both reloads: clc(2) lda py(3) adc #8(2) sta ry(3) lda py+1(3) adc #0(2) sta ry+1(3) = 18 cycles, 13 bytes, against 30 cycles and 21 bytes. Saving 12 cycles, 8 bytes. Correctness: the carry chain is identical -- clc before the low add, the low adc's carry feeds the high adc #0, exactly as add16i did after copying. py is read instead of a copy of py that was made one instruction earlier and not touched in between, so the values are the same. sub16 ry, by is left untouched and still reads ry/ry+1, so its 'sta ry' destination semantics are unchanged. Flags: the sequence ends on the same 'sta ry+1' as before, and sub16's leading 'sec' makes carry state on entry irrelevant. Registers: A is clobbered by both forms and the following ble16i starts with 'lda #<(-8)'; X and Y are untouched. No anonymous labels are added or removed (mov16, add16i and sub16 contain none). Rejected as too risky: stashing the low byte of py+8 in X to avoid the ry round-trip in sub16 would save a further 2 cycles but assumes X is dead here, which the window does not establish.

assumption: rx/ry/spx/spy do not alias ox/oy/px/py (they are distinct zero-page reservations). A and all flags are dead at the following lda otype.
original:
dif16 rx, ox, px
        dif16 ry, oy, py
        mov16 spx, ox
        mov16 spy, oy
        lda otype
        asl
        tax
        jsr @call
proposal:
sec
        lda ox
        sta spx
        sbc px
        sta rx
        lda ox+1
        sta spx+1
        sbc px+1
        sta rx+1
        sec
        lda oy
        sta spy
        sbc py
        sta ry
        lda oy+1
        sta spy+1
        sbc py+1
        sta ry+1
        lda otype
        asl
        tax
        jsr @call
argument: dif16 rx,ox,px is sec(2) lda ox(3) sbc px(3) sta rx(3) lda ox+1(3) sbc px+1(3) sta rx+1(3) = 20 cycles / 13 bytes; mov16 spx,ox is lda ox(3) sta spx(3) lda ox+1(3) sta spx+1(3) = 12 / 8. Between them ox and ox+1 are each loaded twice. Interleaving lets one load feed both stores: sta is the only instruction inserted into the subtract and it affects no flags at all, so the sec set before lda ox is still intact at sbc px, and the borrow out of sbc px survives sta rx, lda ox+1 (loads touch N and Z only) and sta spx+1 to reach sbc px+1. That gives 2+3+3+3+3+3+3+3+3 = 26 cycles / 17 bytes per axis versus 32 / 21, i.e. 6 cycles and 4 bytes per axis and 12 cycles / 8 bytes for the pair. The second sec is retained because the first subtract leaves C undefined. The only observable difference at the end of the window is A and the N/Z/C/V state (macro: A = oy+1 and lda flags; rewrite: A = oy+1 - py+1 and sbc flags), and the next instruction is lda otype, which reloads A and overwrites N/Z, with C/V then consumed by nothing before the asl.

assumption: t16 is not read between each mov16 and its following add16i (they are adjacent pairs). No anonymous labels are added or removed.
original:
blt16 px, exitx, @noexit
        mov16 t16, exitx
        add16i t16, 16
        bge16 px, t16, @noexit
        blt16 py, exity, @noexit
        mov16 t16, exity
        add16i t16, 24
        bge16 py, t16, @noexit
        lda #1
        sta exiting
@noexit:
        rts
proposal:
blt16 px, exitx, @noexit
        lda exitx
        clc
        adc #16
        sta t16
        lda exitx+1
        adc #0
        sta t16+1
        bge16 px, t16, @noexit
        blt16 py, exity, @noexit
        lda exity
        clc
        adc #24
        sta t16
        lda exity+1
        adc #0
        sta t16+1
        bge16 py, t16, @noexit
        lda #1
        sta exiting
@noexit:
        rts
argument: Same fusion as logic_1287. mov16 t16,exitx is lda exitx(3) sta t16(3) lda exitx+1(3) sta t16+1(3) = 12 cycles / 8 bytes, and add16i t16,16 immediately reloads what was just stored: clc(2) lda t16(3) adc #16(2) sta t16(3) lda t16+1(3) adc #0(2) sta t16+1(3) = 18 cycles / 13 bytes. Adding during the copy is lda exitx(3) clc(2) adc #16(2) sta t16(3) lda exitx+1(3) adc #0(2) sta t16+1(3) = 18 cycles / 13 bytes, giving the identical 16-bit result exitx + 16 with the carry propagated by the same adc #0. 30 -> 18 is 12 cycles and 8 bytes per pair. The clc is retained: entry carry comes out of blt16's sbc/eor and is not known. Flags and A afterwards differ (macro leaves A = t16+1 after a plain load, rewrite leaves A = t16+1 after adc) but the next instruction is bge16, whose first act is lda px - it consumes neither A nor N/Z/C/V from above. saving_cycles is quoted as 12 for one pair; when the exit test runs to completion (px inside the exit box) both pairs fuse and the window saves 24 cycles / 16 bytes. On the common frame px < exitx and the first blt16 leaves immediately, so neither pair executes and the saving is 0 - this is a rare-path win, which is why I have quoted the per-pair figure rather than the sum.

assumption: Carry need not survive the window. Verified in-file: both exits ('beq @cpos' -> 'lda w16 / cmp #ROWCHARS' and the fall-through 'cmp #$FF') re-derive C with their own cmp before any bcc/bcs, and the negative arm does its own 'clc / adc sp_w'. If you would rather not rely on that, keep the final 'lda w16+1' instead of 'cmp #0' and the saving is 3 cycles / 1 byte.
original:
lda w16+1
        sbc wx+1
        sta w16+1
        cmp #$80
        ror w16+1
        ror w16                     ; arithmetic shift right 1 -> c0 (16 bit)
        lda w16+1
        beq @cpos
        cmp #$FF
        bne @out0
proposal:
lda w16+1
        sbc wx+1
        cmp #$80
        ror a                       ; sign into bit 7, old bit 0 out to C
        sta w16+1
        ror w16                     ; arithmetic shift right 1 -> c0 (16 bit)
        cmp #0                      ; A still holds w16+1: just restore N,Z
        beq @cpos
        cmp #$FF
        bne @out0
argument: After 'sbc wx+1' the new high byte is already in A, so the original spends 3 cycles storing it, 2 comparing, then 5 doing 'ror w16+1' on zero page -- re-fetching and re-storing the byte it just had. Instruction by instruction: 'cmp #$80' does not touch A and sets C = (A >= $80), the sign bit, exactly as before, and it is now done before the store rather than after, which is harmless because sta sets no flags and cmp changes no memory. 'ror a' (2) then produces the same value 'ror w16+1' (5) would have produced -- C into bit 7, A bit 0 out to C -- saving 3. 'sta w16+1' (3) writes it and, crucially, does not disturb C, so the following 'ror w16' still receives the correct bit and the 16-bit arithmetic shift is unchanged. At that point A still equals w16+1 (ror on memory does not touch A), so the 3-cycle 'lda w16+1' is a pure reload; only its N/Z are wanted, and 'cmp #0' supplies them in 2 cycles (N from A-0 is A's bit 7, Z from A == 0). Net 24 -> 20 cycles; bytes 10 -> 9 (ror a is 1 byte, cmp #0 is 2 where lda zp was 2). No anonymous labels are added or removed. No register other than A is touched, and A holds the same value at the end as before. Note the identical-looking pattern at the half-res branch (lda w16+1 / cmp #$80 / ror w16+1 / ror w16) is NOT improvable the same way: there A must be loaded first, so lda+cmp+ror a+sta is 15 cycles, the same as lda+cmp+ror zp+ror zp.

assumption: dpass only ever holds 0 or 1 while the loop body runs (verified: it is set to 1 at entry, decremented at @endpass, and the loop exits on `bmi` as soon as it goes to $FF), and the decimal flag is clear.
original:
lda SPRLIST,x
        cmp #BOXID0
        lda #0
        rol                         ; 1 if this is one, 0 if not
        cmp dpass
        bne @next
proposal:
lda SPRLIST,x
        cmp #BOXID0
        lda dpass
        adc #$FF
        beq @next
argument: The original materialises the carry as 0/1 (lda #0 = 2, rol = 2) purely to compare it against dpass (cmp = 3) and branch on inequality: 9 cycles not taken, 7 bytes. `lda dpass` (3) followed by `adc #$FF` (2) computes dpass + 255 + C, which is zero mod 256 exactly when dpass + C = 1, i.e. exactly when C != dpass for dpass in {0,1}: (0,C=1) -> 256 -> Z=1; (1,C=0) -> 256 -> Z=1; (0,C=0) -> 255 -> Z=0; (1,C=1) -> 257 -> Z=0. So `beq @next` branches on precisely the condition `bne @next` did. 7 cycles not taken, 5 bytes: -2 cycles, -2 bytes, on every sprite of both passes. The carry consumed is the one `cmp #BOXID0` just produced, and `lda` does not disturb it. A afterwards holds 0/1/255 instead of 0/1, but A is dead on both exits: @next begins `lda rp` and the fall-through begins `lda SPRLIST,x`. C afterwards is set in three of the four cases instead of being the compare result, but the fall-through path's next carry consumer is `bcc @write` which is fed by its own `cmp #BOXID0+BOXN`, and @next does an explicit `clc` before its `adc #10`. The dpass in {0,1} restriction is what makes the trick exact - for dpass = 2 the two forms would disagree - and the surrounding code guarantees it.

assumption: @reg is reached only from the two branches shown (verified: it is referenced nowhere else in ob_star), so the fall-through layout can be rearranged.
original:
lsr
        ldx O_EL,y
        beq @reg
        cmp #6
        bcs @reg                    ; sparkle frames stay regular (C = 0 below)
        adc boxbase-1,x
        sta q1
        jsr star_safe
        lda q1
        jmp m_addsprite
@reg:   clc
        adc #34
        jmp m_addsprite
@done:  rts
proposal:
lsr
        ldx O_EL,y
        beq @regc                   ; carry unknown on this path: force it
        cmp #6
        bcs @reg                    ; C = 1 here, so @reg can assume it
        adc boxbase-1,x
        sta q1
        jsr star_safe
        lda q1
        jmp m_addsprite
@regc:  sec
@reg:   adc #33                     ; +33 with C=1 is the old +34 with C=0
        jmp m_addsprite
@done:  rts
argument: The bcs @reg path arrives with C=1 by construction (the branch is taken on carry set), so the clc at @reg is pure waste there; only the beq path has an unknown carry, inherited from the lsr. Splitting the entry gives the beq path sec (2) + adc #33 (2) = 4, exactly what clc (2) + adc #34 (2) cost before, and gives the bcs path adc #33 (2) alone instead of 4. Arithmetic is identical on both paths: A+33+1 = A+34. Strictly no path gets slower, one gets 2 cycles faster, at a cost of one extra byte for the sec. Flags after the adc are the same in both forms (set from the same sum) and are dead anyway, since the next instruction is jmp m_addsprite. X still holds O_EL,y for the boxbase-1,x read on the untouched middle path, and Y is untouched. No anonymous labels are involved -- both labels here are named (@reg, plus the new @regc). The one real cost is readability: the documented constant 34 becomes 33 and only reads correctly next to the sec, so it needs the comment shown.

assumption: Y is dead across jsr @nfull. Verified: @nfull is called from exactly one site (engine.s:2312) and every use of Y anywhere in build_sections loads it first - @cp does ldy #7 at 2204 and @advance does tay at 2444; there is no read of Y that is not preceded by a set in the same routine. X is untouched by the rewrite, so the live SECTAB index survives without the save/restore. Anonymous label count is unchanged (still exactly one ':').
original:
@nfull: stx tmp2                    ; X is the live SECTAB entry index: save it
        ldx barq
        lda ringS
        sec
        sbc mulrowlo,x              ; r = ringS mod 80
        ldx tmp2                    ; restore X (r survives in A)
        cmp #1                      ; C = 0 iff r == 0
        lda #RINGROWS
        bcc :+                      ; r == 0: the last ring row is whole, keep it here
        lda #RINGROWS-1             ; r  > 0: that row straddles, @addr sends it to the mirror
:       sec
        sbc tmp3
        rts
proposal:
@nfull: ldy barq                    ; X is the live SECTAB entry index: index with Y instead
        lda ringS
        sec
        sbc mulrowlo,y              ; r = ringS mod 80
        cmp #1                      ; C = 1 iff r > 0
        lda #RINGROWS-1             ; r  > 0: that row straddles, @addr sends it to the mirror
        bcs :+
        inc a                       ; r == 0: the last ring row is whole, keep it here
:       sec
        sbc tmp3
        rts
argument: Two changes. (1) The whole point of stx tmp2 / ldx tmp2 (3+3 = 6 cycles, 4 bytes) is to free X for mulrowlo,x. mulrowlo,y is an absolute-indexed load at the same 4 cycles (+1 on a page cross, identically for either index register), so indexing with Y leaves X untouched and the save/restore disappears. ldy barq costs exactly what ldx barq cost. Removing ldx tmp2 from between the sbc and the cmp changes nothing the cmp cares about - cmp sets its own N/Z/C from A, which the ldx did not touch. (2) The constant select currently costs 2+2+3 = 7 when r == 0 and 2+2+2+2 = 8 when r > 0; since r = ringS mod 80, r == 0 happens on 1 column in 80, so the expensive arm is the common one. Swapping the polarity to bcs (C = 1 iff r >= 1, from cmp #1) makes the common r > 0 arm the fall-through-and-branch case at 2+2+3 = 7, and the rare r == 0 arm 2+2+2+2 = 8. Using the 65C02 inc a (2 cycles, 1 byte) rather than a second lda # (2 cycles, 2 bytes) for the RINGROWS-1 -> RINGROWS step saves the byte; it sets N/Z from the result, which the following sec / sbc tmp3 overwrites before anything reads them. Net 6 + 1 = 7 cycles on the common path and 4 + 1 = 5 bytes. Note the sec before sbc tmp3 is still required because the bcs path leaves C = 1 but the inc a path leaves it whatever cmp #1 produced.

assumption: A need not hold #>SPRREC at the rts on the curbuf = 0 path. Verified: the direct caller render_frame does `jsr select_backbuf` then `lda wx`, the menu caller goes through m_select_backbuf which ends `jmp pagelogic` (pagelogic loads A itself), so A is dead at both returns. C and V are likewise unused by the callers.
original:
lda #<SPRREC
        sta recp
        lda #>SPRREC
        sta recp+1
        lda curbuf
        beq :+
        lda recp
        clc
        adc #<(MAXREC*10)
        sta recp
        lda recp+1
        adc #>(MAXREC*10)
        sta recp+1
:       rts
proposal:
lda curbuf
        beq :+
        lda #<(SPRREC+MAXREC*10)
        sta recp
        lda #>(SPRREC+MAXREC*10)
        sta recp+1
        rts
:       lda #<SPRREC
        sta recp
        lda #>SPRREC
        sta recp+1
        rts
argument: The routine sets recp = SPRREC and then, for curbuf = 1, adds MAXREC*10 to it at run time - a 16-bit add whose operands are both assembly-time constants. SPRREC is a label and MAXREC*10 a constant, so #<(SPRREC+MAXREC*10) and #>(SPRREC+MAXREC*10) are resolved by ca65 and the whole lda recp / clc / adc / sta / lda recp+1 / adc / sta chain (18 cycles, 13 bytes) becomes two lda/sta pairs. Splitting the two cases before the first store also removes the wasted SPRREC store on the curbuf = 1 path. Cycle count: curbuf = 1 goes from lda#2 + sta3 + lda#2 + sta3 + lda3 + beq2 + lda3 + clc2 + adc2 + sta3 + lda3 + adc2 + sta3 + rts6 = 39 down to lda3 + beq2 + lda#2 + sta3 + lda#2 + sta3 + rts6 = 21, saving 18; curbuf = 0 is 22 either way. Bytes 26 -> 23. Anonymous labels: the block contains exactly one `:` before and after (the earlier `:` in the ACCCON test above is untouched), so no branch is retargeted - the label simply moves from after the last store to before the curbuf = 0 tail, and the `beq :+` that references it is the same instruction. If the moved label is felt to be too much, the strictly-in-place variant (keep the four SPRREC stores and the trailing `: rts` exactly as they are, and replace only the seven-instruction add chain with the two constant lda/sta pairs) still saves 8 cycles and 5 bytes with A identical on both paths and only C,V differing.

assumption: A is dead at @entry2, and N/V are dead there too. In the original A arrives as 0 or $10 (sp_flags & $10) and N=0; in the rewrite A is the full flags byte and N/V are leftovers. Z is 0/1 identically in both, and X (the ROMSEL value) is identical.
original:
lda (ptr),y
        sta sp_flags
        ldx #BANK_SPR
        and #4
        beq :+
        ldx #(BANK_SPR|$80)
:       lda sp_flags
        and #$10
        beq :+
        ldx #BANK_TIL1
:       stx ROMSEL_CPY
proposal:
lda (ptr),y
        sta sp_flags
        ldx #BANK_SPR
        bit #4
        beq :+
        ldx #(BANK_SPR|$80)
:       bit #$10                ; A still holds the flags byte
        beq :+
        ldx #BANK_TIL1
:       stx ROMSEL_CPY
argument: 65C02 bit #imm ($89) is 2 cy / 2 bytes like and #imm but leaves A intact (and, in immediate mode only, touches Z alone - N and V are not written). So the first test no longer destroys the flags byte and the lda sp_flags reload (3 cy, 2 bytes) between the two tests disappears. The intervening ldx sets N,Z but Z is immediately re-established by bit #$10, so both beq decisions are unchanged. Anonymous label count is unchanged (still two).

assumption: A is dead after the sequence (it becomes c0+W-1 instead of c0+W). Flags are unchanged: the window previously ended the pair with dec sp_c1, setting N,Z from the stored value; deca sets N,Z from exactly the same value, and the following stz sp_c0 writes no flags. sp_c1 assumed zero page (if absolute the saving is 4 cy / 1 byte).
original:
adc sp_w
        beq @out0
        bmi @out0
        inc spclip
        sta sp_c1
        dec sp_c1
        stz sp_c0
proposal:
adc sp_w
        beq @out0
        bmi @out0
        inc spclip
        deca
        sta sp_c1
        stz sp_c0
argument:
Decrement in the accumulator instead of read-modify-writing memory: sta zp (3) + dec zp (5) = 8 cy / 4 bytes becomes dec a (2) + sta zp (3) = 5 cy / 3 bytes. inc spclip does not disturb A, so it can stay where it is. The exit flags are bit-for-bit the same as before (N,Z of c0+W-1).
A further 3 cy is available by folding the two branches - deca / bmi @out0 tests A<=0 in one branch and leaves A pre-decremented - but that is only exact if c0+sp_w can never be -128 (i.e. sp_w >= 1, since the comment gives c0 in -128..-1). Not provable from the window, so it is not the proposal.

assumption: X is dead on entry to the window and across both exits (verified in engine.s: the next reference to X on the fall-through path is `ldx #BANK_SPR`, which writes it, and the @titledir path never reads X). A must be dead at @titledir (verified: @titledir starts `lda ptr+1`).
original:
sta ptr
        lda spbank
        cmp #BANK_SPR
        bne @titledir
        lda ptr
        clc
        adc #<SPR_TABLE
        sta ptr
        lda ptr+1
        adc #>SPR_TABLE
        sta ptr+1
proposal:
sta ptr
        ldx spbank
        cpx #BANK_SPR
        bne @titledir
        clc
        adc #<SPR_TABLE
        sta ptr
        lda ptr+1
        adc #>SPR_TABLE
        sta ptr+1
argument: After the three asl/rol pairs A holds the low byte of id*8; `sta ptr` keeps it for the @titledir path, which reads ptr later at @entry2 (ldaz ptr), so the store stays. The only reason `lda ptr` (3 cycles, 2 bytes) exists is that `lda spbank` clobbered A to do the bank test.
