Doing the test in X instead - ldx spbank (3) / cpx #BANK_SPR (2), the same 5 cycles and 4 bytes as lda/cmp - leaves A holding the low byte, so the reload is pure waste. Flags: cpx #BANK_SPR sets N,Z,C from X - imm, and X here holds exactly the value A held in the original, so the bne sees the identical Z. Carry: the following clc is unchanged, so the adc chain is unaffected. On the @titledir path the only difference is that A now holds the offset low byte instead of spbank, and @titledir immediately reloads A with `lda ptr+1`. Net: -3 cycles on the game path (the overwhelmingly common one), 0 on the title path, -2 bytes.

assumption: The preceding line 1047 '@write: ldy #0' is deleted as part of the change; @write must keep its label, moving to the lda SPRLIST,x line. If only the shown window may change (line 1049 onward) the saving is 1 cycle and it costs 1 byte.
original:
@write: ldy #0
        lda SPRLIST,x
        sta (rp),y                  ; copy identity into record, clear rect
        iny
        lda SPRLIST+1,x
        sta spx
        sta (rp),y
        iny
        ...
proposal:
@write: lda SPRLIST,x
        staz rp                     ; copy identity into record, clear rect
        ldy #1
        lda SPRLIST+1,x
        sta spx
        sta (rp),y
        iny
        ...
argument: Only the y=0 store is touched. Original: ldy #0 (2) + sta (rp),y (6) + iny (2) = 10 cycles, 5 bytes, leaving Y=1. Proposed: staz rp, i.e. the 65C02 sta (zp) (5 cycles, 2 bytes) + ldy #1 (2 cycles, 2 bytes) = 7 cycles, 4 bytes, also leaving Y=1. Same byte written to the same address (rp is zero page, engine.s:150). Registers: A is unchanged by both stores and is reloaded immediately by lda SPRLIST+1,x; Y ends at 1 either way, so the four following iny steps still land on offsets 2,3,4. X (the SPRLIST offset) is untouched. Flags: sta/staz set none; ldy #0 and ldy #1 both set N=0 and differ only in Z, and no branch reads the flags between here and the next lda, so the change is invisible. Dropping the ldy #0 at @write is safe because every entry to @write (fall-through, bcc @write at 1036, bne @write at 1041) goes straight into these three instructions with nothing reading Y first. No anonymous labels involved. Net 3 cycles, 1 byte, per sprite record written.

original:
lda (ptr),y
        sta sp_flags
        ldx #BANK_SPR
        and #4                      ; bit2 -> data in ANDY
        beq :+
        ldx #(BANK_SPR|$80)
:       lda sp_flags
        and #$10                    ; bit4 -> data above the tiles in bank 6 (box stars)
proposal:
lda (ptr),y
        sta sp_flags
        ldx #BANK_SPR
        bit #4                      ; bit2 -> data in ANDY (A preserved)
        beq :+
        ldx #(BANK_SPR|$80)
:       and #$10                    ; bit4 -> data above the tiles in bank 6 (box stars)
argument: and #4 destroys A, which is why the flags byte has to be reloaded at the label. The 65C02 bit #imm sets Z from (A AND imm) and leaves A alone - and in immediate mode it does NOT touch N or V (unlike bit zp/abs), so the only flag it writes is the one beq consumes. Both are 2 cycles / 2 bytes, so the swap is free and the lda sp_flags (zero page, engine.s:178 - 3 cycles, 2 bytes) simply disappears. Register state at the label is then A = the flags byte on both arms (the branch-taken arm only does ldx, which does not touch A), exactly what the old lda restored. X is set to BANK_SPR or BANK_SPR|$80 as before. After the and #$10 the code is beq :+ / ldx #BANK_TIL1 / stx ROMSEL_CPY / stx ROMSEL / bra @entry2, and @entry2 starts with ldaz ptr, so A is dead past the and - no need to preserve it there too. Anonymous labels: the ':' line is kept, it simply now carries the and instead of the lda, so the count is unchanged and no :+ / :- elsewhere is retargeted. sta sp_flags is still needed (line 1158 reads it). Net 3 cycles, 2 bytes.

original:
@write: ldy #0
        lda SPRLIST,x
        sta (rp),y                  ; copy identity into record, clear rect
        iny
        lda SPRLIST+1,x
        sta spx
        sta (rp),y
        iny
proposal:
@write: lda SPRLIST,x
        staz rp                     ; sta (rp) - offset 0 needs no index
        ldy #1
        lda SPRLIST+1,x
        sta spx
        sta (rp),y
        iny
argument: Offset 0 of the record does not need Y at all: the 65C02 has (zp) with no index. Original: ldy #0 (2) + lda SPRLIST,x (4) + sta (rp),y (6) + iny (2) = 14 cycles, 8 bytes. Proposal: lda SPRLIST,x (4) + sta (rp) (5) + ldy #1 (2) = 11 cycles, 7 bytes. Saving 3 cycles, 1 byte, on every sprite that is actually written. Correctness: sta (zp) writes the byte at the address in rp, which is (rp),y with y=0; rp is a zero-page pointer already used that way two instructions later. Y is dead on entry to @write (both branches into it - bcc @write and bne @write - fall in with Y either undefined or holding spi), and it is given its value explicitly, so the reordering of ldy relative to the first store is safe. sta affects no flags, and ldy #1 leaves N=0,Z=0 exactly as the iny it replaces did; the next instruction is a load anyway. The label @write must stay on the first instruction, which it does.

original:
@subrow: lda w16
        sec
        sbc #ROWCHARS
        sta w16
        bcs :+
        dec w16+1
:       lda w16+1
        cmp #6
        bcs :+
        lda w16+1
        clc
        adc #$0A
        sta w16+1
:       rts
proposal:
@subrow: lda w16
        sec
        sbc #ROWCHARS
        sta w16
        bcs :+
        dec w16+1
:       lda w16+1
        cmp #6
        bcs :+                      ; not taken: C = 0 for the adc
        adc #$0A
        sta w16+1
:       rts
argument: Two dead instructions on the wrap path. The second lda w16+1 reloads a byte that is already in A - cmp does not disturb the accumulator - so it is 3 cycles and 2 bytes of pure waste. And the clc is redundant for the same reason the sibling routine @addrow just below already exploits (its comment reads 'not taken: C = 1 for the sbc'): falling through bcs :+ means C = 0, exactly what adc #$0A needs. Saving 5 cycles and 3 bytes whenever the row subtraction wraps. Correctness: A holds w16+1 at the adc either way, the sum is identical, sta w16+1 stores the same byte, and rts follows immediately so no flag is consumed. The anonymous label count is untouched - both ':' lines stay, so bcs :+ from the dec and bcs :+ from the cmp still resolve to the same two places.

assumption: A holds the low byte and X the high byte at the `:` label (guaranteed by the sta t16 / stx t16+1 pair that follows it, and by the ldx #0 / ora #0 / bpl :+ / dex sign-extension above), and t16b is dead after this block -- verified: every other user of t16b in logic.s writes it before reading it.
original:
sta t16
        stx t16+1
        ; * 24
        asl16 t16
        asl16 t16
        asl16 t16
        mov16 t16b, t16
        asl16 t16
        add16 t16, t16b             ; 8p + 16p
        add16 vx, t16
...
@air:   mov16 t16, vx
        asl16 t16
        add16 t16, vx
proposal:
sta t16                     ; t16 = p
        stx t16+1
        asl t16                     ; t16 = 2p
        rol t16+1
        clc                         ; A/X still hold p: p + 2p = 3p
        adc t16
        sta t16
        txa
        adc t16+1
        sta t16+1
        asl16 t16                   ; 3p << 3 = 24p
        asl16 t16
        asl16 t16
        add16 vx, t16
...
@air:   lda vx                      ; t16 = 2*vx without the mov16
        asl
        sta t16
        lda vx+1
        rol
        sta t16+1
        add16 t16, vx               ; unchanged
argument: Main block: the original builds 24p as ((p<<3) + (p<<3)<<1) and pays a mov16 for the copy. Cost: sta 3 + stx 3 + 3 x asl16 (asl zp 5 + rol zp 5 = 10 each, 30) + mov16 (4 x 3 = 12) + asl16 10 + add16 (clc 2 + 2 x (lda 3 + adc 3 + sta 3) = 20) = 78. The proposal builds 24p as (3p)<<3 using A and X, which still hold p at that point and are otherwise about to be discarded: sta 3 + stx 3 + asl t16 5 + rol t16+1 5 (t16 = 2p, 16-bit, exact) + clc 2 + adc t16 3 + sta t16 3 + txa 2 + adc t16+1 3 + sta t16+1 3 (t16 = 3p, carry propagated correctly because txa touches only N,Z and leaves C alone) + 3 x asl16 30 = 62. 16 cycles saved; bytes 41 -> 30. Correctness: asl t16 / rol t16+1 does not touch A or X, so A is still the untouched low byte when the clc/adc runs; the low add sets the carry the high add consumes; nothing else reads t16b. Flags leaving the block are N,Z,C from rol t16+1 instead of from adc t16b+1, but the next instruction is add16 vx, t16 which begins with clc, so they are dead. The anonymous label count is unchanged -- the `:` before sta t16 stays where it is and the block adds none. Air path (separate execution path, a further 5 cycles): mov16 t16,vx (12) + asl16 t16 (10) = 22 to form 2*vx; lda vx / asl / sta t16 / lda vx+1 / rol / sta t16+1 is 3+2+3+3+2+3 = 17 for the identical 16-bit result, 12 bytes -> 10. The following add16 t16, vx is unchanged and neg16 starts with sec, so the different residual flags and A value do not matter.

assumption: Layout move: 'bra @vert' is deleted and the one-byte '@out0: rts' is relocated to the gap after 'bra @ck' (engine.s:1265, between it and '@top:'). All five branches to @out0 were re-checked against build/main.lst and stay in range. Mutually exclusive with the engine_1146 proposal.
argument: @cpos and the left-clip arm both converge on @vert; the left arm already ends in 'bra @vert', and the @cpos arm - the common one, taken whenever c0 >= 0, i.e. the sprite is not cut off at the left - only needs its own 'bra @vert' because the single rts byte of @out0 sits between it and @vert. Moving that byte lets @cpos fall through, deleting a taken 'bra' (3 cycles, 2 bytes) from every unclipped sprite. The rts cannot go before @cpos: from build/main.lst @out0 is at 0x759 and the furthest backward branch to it is the 'bcc @out0' at 0x7CD (displacement -118), so pulling @out0 26 bytes earlier would make that -144 and break the assembly. Pushing it later is safe. Placing it in the existing gap after 'bra @ck' (orig 0x7AF): with 3 bytes removed earlier, @out0 lands at 0x7AE and the displacements become bcs at 0x743 -> +105, bne -> +10, bcs -> +4, bmi -> -5, bcc -> -30. All five fit. Correctness otherwise: an rts is an rts wherever it is placed, it is reached only by branch (never by fall-through - the instruction above it is an unconditional 'bra @ck'), no flags or registers are involved, and no anonymous label is added or removed. The remaining 'bra @vert' on the left-clip arm now jumps ~24 bytes instead of 1, still well inside range. Note the rest of the window is already tight: 'adc sp_w / deca' relies on the documented C=0 from the preceding 'bcs @out0' and folding the -1 into a 'cmp #ROWCHARS+1' would still need the decremented value for 'sta sp_c1'.

assumption: X is not live after the fill loop (the following code does stz stars / stz bent / ldy nobj and only reloads X later). The rewrite leaves X=$FF and N=1 instead of X=128 and Z=1; the next instruction is a stz, which reads neither.
original:
ldx #0
        lda #$FF
:       sta LV_GRID,x
        inx
        cpx #128
        bne :-
proposal:
ldx #127
        lda #$FF
:       sta LV_GRID,x
        dex
        bpl :-
argument: Counting down lets the loop terminate on the flags dex already sets, deleting the cpx. 12 cy/iteration becomes 10, over 128 iterations = 256 cycles, plus 2 bytes. dex/bpl runs X = 127..0 inclusive and stops when X wraps to $FF, so all 128 bytes are still written, in the opposite order (the fill value is constant, so order is irrelevant). The single anonymous label is preserved. This is per level_init call, so the absolute win is small, but it is free.

assumption: A is dead at @hl and at @hdone. Verified: @hl (logic.s:1405) begins `mov16 qx, px`, i.e. `lda px`, and @hdone begins `inc anim` with the next A use being `lda firing`. ANONYMOUS LABEL COUNT CHANGES: this removes one `:` line from the region (three become two). `bmi :+` and `bra :++` keep their targets, but any `:-` reference textually AFTER this point that currently binds to the removed label will silently retarget. If that is a risk, keep a bare `:` line where the old one was -- the cycle and byte saving comes from the deleted instructions, not from deleting the label.
original:
@hnext: ; steps -= dir
        lda dpx+1
        bmi :+
        dec dpx
        bra :++
:       inc dpx
:       lda dpx
        beq :+
        jmp @hl
:
        bra @hdone
@wall:  stz vx
        stz vx+1
@hdone:
proposal:
@hnext: ; steps -= dir
        lda dpx+1
        bmi :+
        dec dpx
        bra :++
:       inc dpx
:       beq @hdone      ; Z survives from the inc/dec
        jmp @hl
@wall:  stz vx
        stz vx+1
@hdone:
argument: Two independent deletions. (1) `lda dpx` is redundant: both `dec dpx` and `inc dpx` are read-modify-writes that set N,Z from the result, and the only instruction on the path between them and the test is `bra :++`, which affects no flags. So the Z the `beq` needs is already correct without reloading. dpx is zero page (logic.s:282, dpx = $D5), so this deletes 3 cycles and 2 bytes. (2) `beq :+ / jmp @hl / : / bra @hdone` inverts to `beq @hdone / jmp @hl`: @hdone is only jmp @hl (3 bytes) + stz vx (2, vx is zero page, logic.s:215) + stz vx+1 (2) = 7 bytes past the branch, comfortably in range, so the `bra @hdone` and its label disappear -- 2 more bytes, and 3 cycles on the dpx==0 exit (taken beq 3, versus taken beq 3 + bra 3 plus the deleted lda). Net per pass through @hnext: dpx nonzero 21 -> 18 cycles, dpx zero 22 -> 16. @hnext sits inside the `jmp @hl` step loop, so the 3 cycles are per horizontal step, not per call. Registers: A ends as dpx+1 rather than dpx; both targets overwrite A immediately (see assumption). The `bmi :+` still tests dpx+1's sign from the same `lda dpx+1`, unchanged.

assumption: None beyond the window: every path reaching 'sta dpx+1' does so with A holding the byte being stored, which is exactly what the fall-through and the ':' entry both do.
original:
lda #$FF
:       sta dpx+1
        bne16 dpx, :+
        jmp @hdone
:
proposal:
lda #$FF
:       sta dpx+1
        ora dpx                     ; A is still dpx+1 from the sta above
        bne :+
        jmp @hdone
:
argument: bne16 dpx expands to 'lda dpx / ora dpx+1 / bne label'. Immediately before it, 'sta dpx+1' has just written A into dpx+1, and sta does not alter A -- so A already equals dpx+1 on both entries to that store (fall-through with A = the and #$80 result, which is 0, and the ':' entry with A = $FF). Therefore the macro's 'lda dpx / ora dpx+1' can be replaced by the single 'ora dpx': A becomes dpx | dpx+1, exactly the value whose Z flag the bne tests. Cycles: lda zp (3) + ora zp (3) = 6 becomes ora zp (3), saving 3 cycles and 2 bytes. Flags: ora sets N and Z from the OR result, identical to the macro's final ora; only N is also set, and the only consumer is the immediately following bne, which reads Z. Registers: A is clobbered either way and is reloaded at @hl / the jmp target. Anonymous labels: bne16 contains none of its own and the rewritten 'bne :+' still names the same ':' line after 'jmp @hdone', so the label count in this routine is unchanged. Also examined and rejected: replacing the 'bne16/jmp' long-jump idiom with 'beq16 dpx, @hdone' would save one more cycle but only if @hdone is within branch range, which the window does not show. And the inc/dec-by-one of qx after 'mov16 qx, px' could be folded into an adc/sbc #1 chain on px, but that costs a cycle on the positive path and only pays on the negative one, so it is distribution-dependent and left alone.

assumption: fb+1 is $00 on entry to @left. The routine enforces this: @stop (reached exactly when the subtraction borrows and makes fb+1 = $FF) clears fc, and @left is only entered with fc != 0; the right-hand path re-enters with fb 0..194 and fb+1 cleared by the carry out of its add. The existing comment 'fb+1 is 0 here' asserts the same thing one instruction later.
original:
@left:  lda fb
        sec
        sbc q1
        sta fb
        bcs :+
        dec fb+1
:       bmi16 fb, @stop             ; bit fb+1 / bmi @stop
        lda fb
        bne @coll
@stop:  stz fc
@coll:  add16 rx, fb
argument:
The window tests the 16-bit result of fb = fb - q1 for <= 0, but the borrow out of the sbc has already answered the sign question: with fb+1 = 0 on entry, fb+1 becomes $FF exactly when C is clear, which is exactly when bit fb+1 / bmi @stop fires. So the carry branch can carry both jobs. 'sta fb' sets no flags, so at the ':' label Z is still the sbc's Z -- identical to what 'lda fb' would reload -- and 'bcs' does not disturb it, so 'bne @coll' is exactly the original zero test. The dec of fb+1 must stay (add16 rx,fb and add16 spx,fb below read the high byte), so it keeps its own path, now ending in bra @stop.

Cycles, common path (no borrow, fb != 0): was lda 3 + sec 2 + sbc 3 + sta 3 + bcs taken 3 + bit fb+1 3 + bmi 2 + lda fb 3 + bne taken 3 = 25; now 3+2+3+3+3+3 = 17. Saving 8. Borrow path: 24 -> 21 (bra replaces bit/bmi). fb == 0 path: 24 -> 16. Bytes 19 -> 15.

Registers: A leaves the block holding fb exactly as before, and @coll's add16 begins clc/lda rx, so A is dead either way. X and Y untouched. Anonymous labels: one before, one after -- the count is unchanged.

assumption: The carry, N and V left by the cmp are not consumed before being redefined. Verified: on the taken path @skip does 'ldx bent / lda LV_BNEXT,x / bra @walk' and @walk starts with 'cmp #$FF'; on the fall-through path the next flag consumer is 'bne @apo' fed by 'lda O_TYPE,y', and both successors (@apo and the star branch) redefine C with their own 'cpx #BINMAX'.
original:
lda O_STAMP,y
        cmp frame
        beq @skip
        lda frame
        sta O_STAMP,y
        lda O_TYPE,y
proposal:
lda frame
        cmp O_STAMP,y
        beq @skip
        sta O_STAMP,y
        lda O_TYPE,y
argument: The original loads the stamp, compares it against frame, and then - on the not-equal path - loads frame all over again to store it. Swapping the operands puts the value it is about to store into A for free. Cycle count: original taken path lda abs,y (4) + cmp zp (3) + beq taken (3) = 10; new lda zp (3) + cmp abs,y (4) + beq taken (3) = 10, unchanged. Original fall-through 4 + 3 + 2 (branch not taken) + lda zp (3) = 12 before the sta; new 3 + 4 + 2 = 9. Saves 3 cycles per object that is being stamped for the first time this frame, which is the common case for a freshly walked grid. Bytes 12 -> 10. Correctness: cmp is symmetric for Z, so the branch decision is identical. On the taken path the two cmps produce identical flags anyway (equal operands give Z=1, N=0, C=1 either way) and A holds the same numeric value (frame == O_STAMP,y on that path), and @skip overwrites A with 'lda LV_BNEXT,x' before @walk's 'cmp #$FF' reads it, so the accumulator is not load-bearing there. On the fall-through path C and N now reflect frame-O_STAMP instead of O_STAMP-frame, but neither is read before being redefined (see assumption). The abs,y page-cross penalty is the same for cmp as for lda, so no hidden cycle moves.

assumption: Y=0 is not needed after the compare. Verified: @same/@pos (engine.s:916-918) reload Y with `ldy #1` rather than relying on iny from 0, @next (937) never reads Y, and @done (945) is an rts. The codebase has ldaz/staz/andz macros for the (zp) mode but no cmpz; `cmp (rp)` is the same 65C02 addressing mode those macro bodies emit, so adding a cmpz macro keeps the house style.
original:
lda sprmul5,x
        tax                         ; X = list offset, Y = offset into the record:
        lda SPRLIST,x               ; (rp),y -- NOT (rp,x), which indexes the pointer
        ldy #0                      ; itself and made every compare below read garbage
        cmp (rp),y
        beq @same
proposal:
lda sprmul5,x
        tax
        lda SPRLIST,x
        cmp (rp)                    ; 65C02 (zp): offset 0 needs no index register
        beq @same
argument: `ldy #0`(2 cy, 2 bytes) + `cmp (rp),y`(5 cy, 2 bytes) = 7 cycles / 4 bytes collapses to `cmp (rp)`(5 cy, 2 bytes). The 65C02 (zp) mode is already used two instructions later at engine.s:910 (`ldaz rp`), reading the same byte, so the mode and the address are both proven here. Flags are identical: `cmp (zp)` compares A against the byte at (rp)+0, exactly what `cmp (zp),y` with Y=0 does, setting the same N, Z and C -- and the only consumer is the `beq @same` on the next line. A is unchanged by cmp (it still holds SPRLIST,x, which is what the `cmp #BOXID0` at 908 goes on to test). X is unchanged and stays the list offset for SPRLIST+1..+4 at 919-931. The only register whose value changes is Y, which was left at 0; @pos sets `ldy #1` explicitly instead of `iny`, so nothing downstream depends on the old Y. Runs once per sprite slot per frame.

assumption: Nothing beyond the window. Saving is 4 cycles when r > 0 and 3 when r == 0.
original:
sec
        sbc mulrowlo,x              ; r = ringS mod 80
        ldx tmp2                    ; restore X (r survives in A)
        cmp #1                      ; C = 0 iff r == 0
        lda #RINGROWS
        bcc :+                      ; r == 0: the last ring row is whole, keep it here
        lda #RINGROWS-1             ; r  > 0: that row straddles, @addr sends it to the mirror
:       sec
        sbc tmp3
        rts
proposal:
sec
        sbc mulrowlo,x              ; r = ringS mod 80
        ldx tmp2                    ; restore X (r survives in A)
        eor #$FF                    ; r == 0 -> $FF
        cmp #$FF                    ; C = 1 iff r == 0
        lda #RINGROWS
        sbc tmp3                    ; RINGROWS - tmp3 - 1 + C
:                                   ; keep the label so :+/:- counts are unchanged
        rts
argument: The conditional -1 is folded into the subtraction that follows it. `eor #$FF` (2) complements r, and `cmp #$FF` (2) then sets C = 1 exactly when the complement is $FF, i.e. when r == 0 -- the inverse of what `cmp #1` gives, which is the sense `sbc` needs. `lda #RINGROWS / sbc tmp3` then computes RINGROWS - tmp3 - (1 - C) = RINGROWS - tmp3 when r == 0 and RINGROWS - 1 - tmp3 when r > 0, which is precisely the two cases the original selected by branch, and it replaces the separate `sec` + `sbc tmp3` because the carry it needs is already the one the comparison produced. Cycles from `cmp`/`eor` onward: new = 2 + 2 + 2 + 3 = 9 in both cases; old = 2 + 2 + 3 + 2 + 3 = 12 for r == 0 and 2 + 2 + 2 + 2 + 2 + 3 = 13 for r > 0. Bytes: eor# 2 + cmp# 2 + lda# 2 + sbc zp 2 = 8 against cmp# 2 + lda# 2 + bcc 2 + lda# 2 + sec 1 + sbc zp 2 = 11. `eor` and `cmp` leave X alone, and the `ldx tmp2` that restores the SECTAB index still precedes them (ldx sets N/Z but not C, and neither is live across it here since `eor #$FF` re-derives both from A). ANONYMOUS LABELS: the branch goes away, so the proposal keeps a bare `:` label line at the same place to hold the file's anonymous-label count -- the region just above @nfull uses `bne :--` and `bcc :++`, so a silent shift here is exactly the failure mode to avoid. Marked medium rather than high only because a larger win is available just outside the window: A holds ringS on entry, so `lda mulrowlo,x / cmp ringS / ldx tmp2 / lda #RINGROWS / sbc tmp3` gets the same inverted carry with no eor at all and saves 9-10 cycles, but that depends on ringS >= mulrowlo[barq], which is true (r is a remainder) but is not visible inside the window.

assumption: X is not required to be 0 on entry to the mov16 that follows; the window shows the next use of X is '@l: ldx tmp4', which reloads it.
original:
ldx #0
        stx tmp4                    ; i
        lda recp
        sta rp
        lda recp+1
        sta rp+1
@l:     ldx tmp4
proposal:
stza tmp4                   ; i
        lda recp
        sta rp
        lda recp+1
        sta rp+1
@l:     ldx tmp4
argument: 'ldx #0' (2 cycles, 2 bytes) + 'stx tmp4' (3 cycles, 2 bytes) = 5 cycles, 4 bytes, purely to zero a zp byte. The 65C02 'stz tmp4' (via this codebase's stza macro) does it in 3 cycles, 3 bytes -- 2 cycles and 1 byte saved. Registers: the only reason to keep X = 0 would be a later use, and the window shows X is immediately reloaded at '@l: ldx tmp4' with the same zero, so nothing depends on the register copy. A is not touched by either form. Flags: 'ldx #0' sets Z=1, N=0 and stz sets nothing, so the flag state at 'lda recp' differs -- but 'lda recp' immediately overwrites N and Z, and the first flag consumer after that is 'cpx NSPR / bcs @done', which sets its own. Carry and overflow are untouched by both forms, so the 'bcc :+' further up is unaffected. No anonymous labels are added or removed. Also examined: the 'bcc :+ / lda NSPR / : sta cnt' min() idiom above is already minimal, and '@l: ldx tmp4 / cpx NSPR / cpx cnt' cannot keep i in X across the loop body because the body does 'lda sprmul5,x / tax' and reuses X as the list offset.

assumption: w16's low byte is dead after this read. Confirmed in engine.s: the next reference to w16 is 'sta w16' in the 'lend = lb0 + ext - 1' block eight instructions later, with no label, branch target or jsr in between. w16+1 is still read and is still written correctly.
original:
asl w16
        rol w16+1
        lda w16
        clc
        adc wfine
proposal:
lda w16
        asl                         ; C = old bit 7, exactly what 'asl w16' left
        rol w16+1
        clc
        adc wfine
argument: 'asl w16' (RMW zp, 5) then 'lda w16' (3) reads back a byte the ALU already had. Loading first and shifting in the accumulator gives the same low byte in A (2 cycles) and the same carry into 'rol w16+1'. 13 cycles becomes 10; bytes go from asl w16(2)+rol w16+1(2)+lda w16(2)=6 to lda w16(2)+asl(1)+rol w16+1(2)=5. Correctness: 'rol w16+1' does not touch A, so A still holds the shifted low byte when 'clc / adc wfine' runs; the flags consumed afterwards are the adc's, identical in both. The single behavioural difference is that w16's low byte is left unshifted in memory -- which is why the deadness of w16 low is the stated assumption. w16+1 is written identically and is read two instructions later by 'lda w16+1 / adc #0', so the 16-bit result of the doubling is unaffected.

assumption: vy is a 2-byte zero-page variable (logic.s:215, inside the .zeropage block), so `lda vy+1` is 3 cycles like the `bit vy+1` it replaces.
original:
bmi16 vy, @draw
        beq16 vy, @draw
        lda #1
        sta O_AL,y
proposal:
lda vy+1                    ; was bmi16 vy / beq16 vy: one load does both tests
        bmi @draw
        ora vy
        beq @draw
        lda #1
        sta O_AL,y
argument: bmi16 expands to `bit vy+1 / bmi @draw` and beq16 to `lda vy / ora vy+1 / beq @draw`, so the pair loads vy+1 twice. `lda vy+1` sets N from bit 7 of the high byte exactly as `bit vy+1` does, so the `bmi @draw` test (vy < 0) is unchanged; A then holds vy+1, and `ora vy` leaves vy|vy+1 -- the same value beq16 computes, in the other operand order -- so the `beq @draw` test (vy == 0) is unchanged too. Cycles on the fall-through path (vy > 0, the only path that continues): 3+2+3+2 = 10 against 3+2+3+3+2 = 13. Bytes: 8 against 10. No path gets worse: vy < 0 is 3+3 = 6 either way, and vy == 0 goes from 3+2+3+3+3 = 14 to 3+2+3+3 = 11. Flags on fall-through: the original leaves N,Z from `ora vy+1`, the proposal from `ora vy`, and both operate on the same result value, so they are identical -- and the next instruction is `lda #1` in any case. A holds vy|vy+1 in both versions; X (set to 8 for inrange at 2036) and Y (the object index, used by `sta O_AL,y`) are untouched. Anonymous label count unchanged: neither macro emits one (bmi16 and beq16 have no `:` in their bodies).

assumption: A need not survive the test. Visible in the window: the taken path lands on `@draw: lda O_AL,y` and the fall-through path starts `lda #1`, so A is dead on both.
original:
bmi16 vy, @draw             ; bit vy+1 / bmi @draw
        beq16 vy, @draw             ; lda vy / ora vy+1 / beq @draw
proposal:
lda vy+1
        bmi @draw
        ora vy
        beq @draw
argument: The two macros together mean `branch if vy <= 0`, and they load vy+1 twice. `lda vy+1` sets N from bit 7 exactly as `bit vy+1` did, so `bmi @draw` is unchanged; falling through, A already holds vy+1, so `ora vy` produces the same vy|vy+1 that `lda vy / ora vy+1` produced and `beq @draw` tests the same zero. The order of the two tests is swapped but both branch to the same label, so the combined predicate is identical. Cycles on the fall-through (the path that continues to `lda #1`): original `bit vy+1`(3) + `bmi`(2) + `lda vy`(3) + `ora vy+1`(3) + `beq`(2) = 13; new 3+2+3+2 = 10. The bmi-taken path is 6 either way; the beq-taken path goes 14 -> 11. Bytes 10 -> 8. The only behavioural difference is that `bit` preserved A and `lda` does not, which the assumption covers. No anonymous labels are involved. Note `clc` before `adc #115` further down must stay - the preceding `lsr` leaves carry set from the shifted-out bit and `ldx O_EL,y` does not clear it.

assumption: @f0 is reached only from the single `bcc @f0` above it (true in logic.s: it is the fe < 3 arm of the frame-select ladder). The `bra @sp` needs @sp within reach, which it trivially is -- @sp is about ten bytes further on, immediately after `@f8: lda #8`.
argument: @fr computes A + fc with the carry cleared. For the @f0 arm A is the constant 0, so the result is just fc and the whole add is ceremony: `lda #0` (2) + `bra @fr` (3) + `clc` (2) + `adc fc` (3) + `bra @sp` (3) = 13 cycles and 11 bytes collapse to `lda fc` (3) + `bra @sp` (3) = 6 cycles and 4 bytes. fc is 0 or 1 here (it is set to those constants by the @bset ladder above), but the rewrite does not rely on that -- 0 + fc = fc for any byte value, with no carry out for any fc, which is why the dropped `clc`/`adc` cannot change the result. Flags: the old path left N/Z from `adc` and C = 0; the new one leaves N/Z from `lda fc` (same value, so same N/Z) and C untouched. Neither matters: @sp is `sta q1` (no flags) followed by `lda otype / cmp #5`, which re-establishes N/Z/C, and the later `clc / adc q1` clears the carry explicitly before using it. The @f2, @f4 and the fe >= 9 arms keep the shared @fr tail since their constants are non-zero. No anonymous labels are involved anywhere in this ladder, so nothing renumbers. Replacing the whole cmp-ladder with a table lookup would be cheaper still but needs a new 12-byte table, which is a redesign rather than a re-encoding.

assumption: X is dead here. Checked in engine.s: X was last used for the sprdisp_tab lookup well above, and the next read of X is `ldx #0` at the top of ds_rowloop, so nothing between depends on it.
original:
lda #8
        sta sp_rinc
        lda sp_flags
        and #2
        bne :+
        lda w16+1
        cmp #$80
        ror w16+1
        ror w16
        lsr sp_rinc
:       lda sp_col
proposal:
ldx #8
        lda sp_flags
        and #2
        bne :+
        lda w16+1
        cmp #$80
        ror w16+1
        ror w16
        ldx #4
:       stx sp_rinc
        lda sp_col
argument: sp_rinc is written as 8 and then, on the half-res arm, halved in place. A read-modify-write on zero page costs 5 cycles (`lsr zp`); choosing the value in a register before the single store costs 2 (`ldx #4`). Full-res arm: `ldx #8` (2) + `stx` (3) = 5, exactly what `lda #8` (2) + `sta` (3) cost. Half-res arm: 2 + 2 + 3 = 7 against 2 + 3 + 5 = 10, so 3 cycles. Byte count is identical (6 either way). The `:` label moves up by one instruction so that `stx sp_rinc` is on both paths; that is a relocation of an existing label line, not a new one, so the ca65 anonymous-label count is unchanged and `bne :+` still resolves to the same `:`. Flags: `ldx` sets N and Z, but the only flag consumer in the region is the `bne` that reads the Z from `and #2`, and that happens before the first `ldx #4`; the `ldx #8` at the top is placed before `lda sp_flags`, which reloads A and resets N/Z, so the `and`/`bne` pair is unaffected. STX sets no flags, and the following `lda sp_col / clc / adc w16` establishes its own. The asr16 above (`lda w16+1 / cmp #$80 / ror w16+1 / ror w16`) is the standard signed halve and has no cheaper 65C02 form.

assumption: Requires swapping the tmp block (engine.s:1281-1288, five lines above the window) with the tmp2 block (1289-1296). The two blocks are independent: both only read tmp/tmp2 and they write disjoint destinations.
original:
lda tmp
        and #7
        sta sp_ra0
        lda tmp
        lsr
        lsr
        lsr
        sta sp_r0
        lda tmp2
        and #7
        sta sp_ra1
        lda tmp2
        lsr
        lsr
        lsr
        sta sp_r1
        lda sp_r0
        bne @nopart
proposal:
lda tmp2
        and #7
        sta sp_ra1
        lda tmp2
        lsr
        lsr
        lsr
        sta sp_r1
        lda tmp
        and #7
        sta sp_ra0
        lda tmp
        lsr
        lsr
        lsr
        sta sp_r0                   ; sta sets no flags: Z still from the third lsr
        bne @nopart
argument: sp_r0 is computed, spilled, and then re-read three instructions later purely because the tmp2 block sits in between and needs A. Swapping the two blocks puts the tmp block last, so 'sta sp_r0' is immediately followed by the branch; 'sta' affects no flags, so the 'bne' reads N/Z from the third 'lsr', whose Z is set exactly when tmp>>3 == 0 - the same test 'lda sp_r0 / bne' performed. That deletes 'lda sp_r0' (3 cycles, 2 bytes). Independence: the tmp block reads only tmp and writes sp_ra0/sp_r0; the tmp2 block reads only tmp2 and writes sp_ra1/sp_r1. Neither reads the other's outputs, and nothing between line 1280 and 1297 reads either. The values reaching @nopart and the fall-through are unchanged. X and Y are untouched by both blocks (X is loaded with curbuf on the next line). No anonymous labels are added or removed. Rejected: caching sp_r0 in X instead ('tax' + later 'cpx #0') costs 6 cycles against 5, and X is needed for curbuf immediately afterwards.

assumption: The assembler is in 65C02 mode so `bit #imm` is available (the file already uses bra/stz/inc a). Anonymous label count is unchanged at two.
original:
lda sp_flags
        and #8
        beq :+
        ldx #8                      ; bit3: copy blitter
        bne :++
:       lda sp_flags
        and #3
        asl
        tax
:       lda sprdisp_tab,x
proposal:
lda sp_flags
        bit #8                      ; bit3: copy blitter
        beq :+
        ldx #8
        bne :++
:       and #3                      ; A is still sp_flags: bit #imm does not alter A
        asl
        tax
:       lda sprdisp_tab,x
argument: `and #8` destroys sp_flags in A, which is why the bit3-clear arm has to reload it with a second `lda sp_flags`. `bit #imm` on the 65C02 sets Z from A AND the operand while leaving A untouched, and costs the same 2 cycles / 2 bytes as `and #8`, so the `beq :+` test is bit-for-bit identical and the reload (3 cycles, 2 bytes) can be deleted. bit3-clear path: 17 -> 14 cycles. bit3-set path: unchanged at 12 cycles (the `bne :++` after `ldx #8` is still unconditionally taken because ldx sets Z from 8). Note bit #imm on the 65C02 affects only Z - it does not copy operand bits 6/7 into V/N as the other bit modes do - but only Z is used here, and the subsequent `and #3` re-derives N/Z from the masked value exactly as before. X is written only on the arm that takes it. The number of anonymous labels is two before and after, so no `:+`/`:++` reference is retargeted.

assumption: Y need not hold 0 on any path leaving this compare. Visible evidence: the @same path does lda #2 / sta tmp3 and reaches @pos, which reloads Y with `ldy #1`; the @next path (engine_928) touches only rp/tmp4. What is not visible is the code between @l and this instruction, which must not rely on Y being zeroed here. Also assumes a `cmpz` macro is added alongside the existing ldaz/staz/andz wrappers.
original:
lda SPRLIST,x               ; (rp),y -- NOT (rp,x), which indexes the pointer
        ldy #0                      ; itself and made every compare below read garbage
        cmp (rp),y
proposal:
lda SPRLIST,x
        cmpz rp                     ; cmp (rp) -- 65C02 zero-page indirect
argument: The 65C02 has a (zp) addressing mode with no index, which the file already uses via ldaz/staz/andz (and `ldaz rp` appears five lines below in this very window). cmp (zp) is 5 cycles / 2 bytes; cmp (zp),y is 5 cycles / 2 bytes plus 1 if the indexed address crosses a page. So the compare itself is at worst a wash and at best 1 cycle better, and the `ldy #0` (2 cycles, 2 bytes) that exists only to make Y zero for it disappears outright. Saving 2 cycles / 2 bytes, 3 cycles whenever rp sits in the last byte of a page. Flags: `ldy #0` sets N=0/Z=1 but those are immediately replaced by the compare's own flags, so dropping it changes nothing the following `beq @same` / `cmp #BOXID0` / `bcc @next` sees. A and X are untouched by both forms. No anonymous labels are added or removed.

assumption: A is free here (mov16 clobbers it anyway) and t16 is zero page (t16 = $D1). Nothing reads t16 between the mov16 and the add16.
original:
mov16 t16, vx
        asl16 t16
        add16 t16, vx               ; 3vx
; expands to: lda vx / sta t16 / lda vx+1 / sta t16+1
;             asl t16 / rol t16+1
;             clc / lda t16 / adc vx / ...
proposal:
lda vx
        asl a
        sta t16
        lda vx+1
        rol a
        sta t16+1
        add16 t16, vx               ; 3vx (unchanged)
argument: The original copies vx into t16 and then shifts t16 in memory; doing the shift in A on the way through removes both memory read-modify-writes. Original: mov16 = 3+3+3+3 = 12 (lda vx 3 if zp), asl16 = asl zp 5 + rol zp 5 = 10, so 22 cycles / 12 bytes before the add16. Proposed: lda 3 + asl a 2 + sta zp 3 + lda 3 + rol a 2 + sta zp 3 = 16 cycles / 10 bytes. Saving 6 cycles, 2 bytes, and it is independent of whether vx is zero page or absolute (the two lda costs appear identically on both sides). Correctness: `asl a` produces the same low byte and the same carry-out as `asl t16` would have, and `rol a` on the freshly loaded high byte consumes exactly that carry, just as `rol t16+1` did -- the intervening `sta t16` sets no flags and so cannot disturb C. The result stored to t16/t16+1 is bit-identical. Flags at the end differ (rol/sta vs asl/rol on memory), but the very next macro, add16, begins `clc / lda t16`, which reloads everything, so no flag is consumed. The branch cluster earlier in this window (`lda alt / beq :+ / bmi :+ / jmp @air`) is NOT improvable: both branches target the same label and the third case needs a jmp because @air is evidently out of branch range; reordering beq/bmi only shuffles which case pays 2 vs 3 cycles and depends on a distribution not visible here. Verdict on that part: none.

original:
mov16i bvx, 3584
        lda facing
        beq @bdir
        mov16i bvx, -3584
@bdir:  stz bvy
proposal:
stz bvx
        lda #>3584
        sta bvx+1
        lda facing
        beq @bdir
        lda #>(-3584)
        sta bvx+1
@bdir:  stz bvy
argument: 3584 is $0E00 and -3584 is $F200: both immediates have a zero low byte, so bvx's low half is written with the same value on both paths and only the high half actually differs. That collapses each mov16i (lda #0 / sta bvx / lda #hi / sta bvx+1, 10 cycles, 8 bytes) into stz bvx once (3 cycles, 2 bytes) plus a 5-cycle lda/sta of the high byte on whichever path runs. Cycles: facing != 0 goes 10 + 3 + 2 + 10 = 25 down to 3 + 2 + 3 + 3 + 2 + 2 + 3 = 18; facing == 0 goes 10 + 3 + 3 = 16 down to 3 + 2 + 3 + 3 + 3 = 14. Bytes 20 -> 14. Flag and register state at @bdir is unchanged on both paths: via the taken beq, A = facing = 0 with Z = 1 exactly as before, and via fall-through A = $F2 from lda #>(-3584) exactly as before. Nothing between @bdir and the next `lda #1` reads A or the flags (three stz, which set none). bvx is zero page so stz zp is 3 cycles. No label is added or removed - @bdir is a named local and is still the beq's target.

assumption: w16 is dead on entry to the window: the instruction above it is 'lda w16 / sec / sbc rc_tx0 / sta rc_nt', which consumes the old value. Confirmed at engine.s:413.
original:
sta rc_nt
        lda rc_x
        and #3
        sta rc_sc0
        asl
        asl
        asl
        sta rc_ro0
        lda rc_x
        sta w16
        lda rc_x+1
        sta w16+1
        lda rc_y
        jsr ringaddr
proposal:
sta rc_nt
        lda rc_x
        sta w16                     ; the copy the ring address needs, from the same load
        and #3
        sta rc_sc0
        asl
        asl
        asl
        sta rc_ro0
        lda rc_x+1
        sta w16+1
        lda rc_y
        jsr ringaddr
argument: rc_x is loaded twice, first for 'and #3' and again to seed w16. Hoisting 'sta w16' to immediately after the first load removes the second 'lda rc_x' entirely: 3 cycles and 2 bytes (rc_x is zero page, engine.s:153). Nothing between the two loads writes rc_x -- the intervening stores are to rc_sc0 and rc_ro0 -- so the value stored is identical. 'sta w16' sets no flags, so the 'and #3' that follows sees the same A and the same (irrelevant) incoming flags as before. w16 is scratch and its previous value has already been consumed by the sbc above the window, so writing it early is safe. The rest of the window is unimprovable: the three asl's are a 3-bit shift of a value that must also survive as rc_sc0, and the tail is the argument setup for jsr ringaddr.

assumption: The `lda control / bne @afterctl` one line above the window (logic.s 1517-1518) is retargeted as part of this change, and @ctl is within relative-branch range of it (measured at about 40 bytes, well inside +/-127).
original:
lda control
        bne @afterctl
        lda frame
        sec
        sbc evframe
        sta t16
        lda frame+1
        sbc evframe+1
        bne @setctl
        lda t16
        cmp #25
        bcc @afterctl
@setctl:
        lda #1
        sta control
@afterctl:
        lda control
        bne @ctl
        lda #22
        ldx vx+1
        bmi @spr2
proposal:
lda control
        bne @ctl
        lda frame
        sec
        sbc evframe
        sta t16
        lda frame+1
        sbc evframe+1
        bne @setctl
        lda t16
        cmp #25
        bcc @noctl
@setctl:
        lda #1
        sta control
        bra @ctl
@noctl:
        lda #22
        ldx vx+1
        bmi @spr2
argument: @afterctl re-reads and re-tests `control` even though every path into it already knows the answer, so the `lda control / bne @ctl` pair can be deleted and each predecessor sent straight to its true destination. Path 1, control already non-zero: the test at the top branches to @afterctl only when control != 0, so the re-test always falls to @ctl. Retargeting that `bne` to @ctl saves the whole 6 cycles (lda control 3 + bne taken 3). Both A and the flags are preserved exactly: `lda control` at @afterctl would have loaded the same value the top `lda control` already put in A, with the same N and Z, so @ctl sees an identical machine state. Path 2, control = 0 and the elapsed frame count is under 25: the re-test always falls through to `lda #22`, so `bcc @afterctl` becomes `bcc @noctl` pointing at `lda #22` directly, saving 5 cycles (lda control 3 + bne not taken 2). A and flags are dead there - `lda #22` overwrites A, and the `bmi @spr2` that follows reads the flags of `ldx vx+1`, not of the deleted load. Path 3, @setctl: after `lda #1 / sta control` the re-test always branches, so `bra @ctl` replaces it, saving 3 cycles (6 spent on lda+bne, 3 on the bra). Again A = 1 and N=0/Z=0 from `lda #1` match what `lda control` would have produced, and `sta` sets no flags. Path 1 dominates - `control` is cleared only at @fell (player death) and is otherwise left at 1 - so 6 cycles is the figure to quote, and it is paid every frame of player_update. Net 2 bytes saved (4 removed for lda+bne, 2 added for bra). No anonymous labels are involved: @afterctl, @setctl, @noctl and @ctl are all named local labels, so nothing in the `:+`/`:-` chain shifts. Note @afterctl becomes unreferenced and should be deleted rather than left dangling. The hurt timer immediately above uses the same idiom with @clrhurt/@afterhurt but is not foldable the same way - @afterhurt has a genuine merge of two states.

assumption: X is dead across these six instructions. Verified in engine.s: X is last written at ~line 1120-1127 (the bank number) and consumed immediately by 'stx ROMSEL_CPY / stx ROMSEL' at 1128-1129; there is no further X reference until well past line 1290 (checked by grep for ,x / tax / txa / stx / ldx / inx / dex / cpx over lines 1128-1290). 'jsr sext' preserves X (sext is and/beq/lda/sta/rts).
original:
lda spx
        sec
        sbc (ptr),y
        sta w16
        lda spx+1
        sbc tmp3
        sta w16+1
        lda w16
        sec
        sbc wx
        sta w16
        lda w16+1
        sbc wx+1
        sta w16+1
proposal:
lda spx
        sec
        sbc (ptr),y
        sta w16
        lda spx+1
        sbc tmp3
        tax                         ; high partial stays in X, not w16+1
        lda w16
        sec
        sbc wx
        sta w16
        txa
        sbc wx+1
        sta w16+1
argument: The window does two chained 16-bit subtractions and spills the intermediate high byte to w16+1 only to read it straight back. Replacing 'sta w16+1' (zp, 3 cycles, 2 bytes) with 'tax' (2 cycles, 1 byte) and 'lda w16+1' (3 cycles, 2 bytes) with 'txa' (2 cycles, 1 byte) saves 2 cycles and 2 bytes. Correctness: (a) the intermediate w16+1 is not read by anything between the two instructions - the only instructions in between are lda w16 / sec / sbc wx / sta w16, none of which touch w16+1; (b) the carry produced by 'sbc wx' must survive to 'sbc wx+1', and TXA affects only N and Z, never C, so the borrow chain is intact (this is the one thing that would break with, say, an 'lda' of a scratch byte via a flag-setting path - it does not here); (c) the final value written to w16+1 is identical, and the final flags are those of 'sbc wx+1' in both versions, so the following 'cmp #$80 / ror w16+1 / ror w16' is unaffected; (d) A at the end is the high byte in both versions. X is the only new resource and it is dead here.

original:
pla
        stza w16+1
        asl
        asl
        asl
        asl
        asl
        rol w16+1
        asl
        rol w16+1
        clc
        adc #<SPR_DIGITS
proposal:
pla
        lsr                         ; C = d bit0, A = d >> 1
        sta w16+1
        lda #0
        ror                         ; A = d0 << 7
        lsr w16+1                   ; C = d bit1, w16+1 = d >> 2
        ror                         ; A = d1 << 7 | d0 << 6
        clc
        adc #<SPR_DIGITS
argument:
The existing code multiplies the digit by 64 by shifting A left six times and catching only the last two carries in w16+1, so it costs stz w16+1 (3) + six asl (12) + two rol zp (10) = 25 cycles and 12 bytes. The same product is a 16-bit right shift by two of (d : 0), which is far cheaper because the low half starts as a constant: lsr (2) puts d's bit 0 in C and d>>1 in A, sta w16+1 (3) parks the high half, lda #0 (2) makes the low half -- neither sta nor lda touches C -- ror (2) brings bit 0 into position 7, lsr w16+1 (5) does the second shift of the high half and hands bit 1 to C, and the final ror (2) lands it at position 7 with bit 0 sliding to position 6. 16 cycles, 9 bytes: 9 cycles and 3 bytes saved.

Result: w16+1 = d >> 2, A = (d & 3) << 6, i.e. exactly d * 64. For d <= 15 this is bit-identical to the original; for d >= 16 it is the true product where the original wrapped modulo 1024, so it is strictly no less correct and needs no range assumption.

Flags and registers: the following 'clc / adc #<SPR_DIGITS' sets its own carry, so the carry left by the last ror does not matter, and N/Z are dead. X is the bar column and must survive (the routine's own comment) -- untouched. Y indexes BARCACHE above and is reloaded with #31 below -- untouched. w16+1 ends up holding the high byte just as before, ready for the 'lda w16+1 / adc #>SPR_DIGITS' two instructions later, and the stz is no longer needed because the sta supersedes it.

original: mov16i bvx, 3584        ; lda #<3584 / sta bvx / lda #>3584 / sta bvx+1
proposal:
stz bvx
        lda #>3584
        sta bvx+1
argument: 3584 is $0E00, so the low byte of the immediate is zero and mov16i's first pair is lda #0 (2) / sta bvx (3) = 5 cycles, 4 bytes. The 65C02's stz bvx does the same store in 3 cycles and 2 bytes. Flags: the original's lda #0 sets Z=1,N=0 and is then immediately overwritten by lda #>3584 (Z=0,N=0), and stz sets no flags at all, so the state on arrival at the following `lda facing` is identical in both versions (A = $0E, N=0, Z=0, C and V untouched). bvx is zero page (logic.s .zeropage block) so stz zp is the 3-cycle form. Anonymous label count unchanged. Note this window's other candidates do not survive: the `lda dpx / beq :+ / jmp @hl / : / bra @hdone` tail only trades a cycle between the two paths and would disturb the anonymous labels, and `inc anim` + a later `lda anim` is 8 cycles, exactly what lda/inca/sta would cost with more bytes. See logic_1461 for the larger version of this same fix covering the -3584 store too.

assumption: Depends on a fact one line above the window: logic.s:1469 is `mov16i bvx, 3584`, and <3584 = <(-3584) = $00, so the low byte is already correct. This is a numeric coincidence that a future change to the speed constant would silently break -- only worth taking with a `.assert <(3584) = <(-3584), error` guard beside it. Low confidence for that reason, not because the cycle count is in doubt.
original:
lda facing
        beq @bdir
        mov16i bvx, -3584
@bdir:  stz bvy
proposal:
lda facing
        beq @bdir
        .assert <(3584) = <(-3584), error, "bvx low byte no longer shared"
        lda #>(-3584)               ; low byte already set by the mov16i above
        sta bvx+1
@bdir:  stz bvy
argument: mov16i expands to lda #<imm(2) / sta dst(3) / lda #>imm(2) / sta dst+1(3) = 10 cycles, 8 bytes. 3584 is $0E00 and -3584 is $F200: the low bytes are both $00, so the first two instructions rewrite bvx with the value the preceding mov16i already put there. Dropping them leaves 5 cycles and 4 bytes. Flags: the surviving `lda #$F2` sets N=1, Z=0, exactly as the original's final `lda #>(-3584)` did, and `sta` clears nothing -- the next instruction is `stz bvy`, which reads no flags. Carry is untouched by all of lda/sta/stz. A holds $F2 either way; X and Y are not involved. No anonymous label is added or removed. This runs once per boomerang throw, so the value is in the 4 bytes as much as the 5 cycles.

assumption: PARTADDR's high byte has its low three bits clear (PARTADDR = $3000), so the high half can be OR'd in rather than added. If that is ever untrue, use 'clc / adc #>PARTADDR' instead and the saving becomes 10 cycles / 5 bytes.
original:
lda tmp4
        stz ptr+1
        asl
        rol ptr+1
        asl
        rol ptr+1
        asl
        rol ptr+1
        clc
        adc #<PARTADDR
        sta ptr
        lda ptr+1
        adc #>PARTADDR
        sta ptr+1
proposal:
lda tmp4
        asl
        asl
        asl
        sta ptr                     ; low byte of tmp4*8
        lda tmp4
        lsr
        lsr
        lsr
        lsr
        lsr
        ora #>PARTADDR              ; high byte is tmp4>>5, at most 7
        sta ptr+1
argument: The original shifts a 16-bit value through memory: three 'rol ptr+1' at 5 cycles each dominate, and the whole sequence costs 3+3+3*(2+5)+2+2+3+3+2+3 = 42 cycles / 24 bytes. Computing the two halves independently costs 3+2+2+2+3 = 12 for the low byte and 3+5*2+2+3 = 18 for the high byte: 30 cycles / 18 bytes. Correctness: ptr = tmp4*8 + PARTADDR. The low byte of tmp4*8 is (tmp4<<3) & $FF, which three 'asl' on A give directly; the high byte is (tmp4*8)>>8 = tmp4>>5, which five 'lsr' give. Since tmp4 is a byte, tmp4>>5 <= 7, and $30 has its low three bits clear, so 'ora' and 'add' agree - no carry is needed and the now-dead 'clc' and 'adc #<PARTADDR' (PARTADDR is page aligned, so the low immediate is 0) both disappear. tmp4 is a column index set at line 1903 and is not modified by either version, so reading it twice is safe. 'stz ptr+1' goes because ptr+1 is now written outright; nothing reads ptr or ptr+1 between. Registers: A only, as before. Flags: the original exits with flags from 'adc #>PARTADDR', the rewrite from 'ora' ('sta' sets none) - both dead, since the next instruction is 'lda ptr'. Incidentally the same split-shift idiom is already used verbatim at logic.s:644-655, so it is house style. Even keeping the original structure, the 'clc' alone is provably redundant: ptr+1 starts at 0 and is below $80 before each rol, so the last rol always leaves C = 0.

original:
ldx #0
:       lda t16
        sta LV_MAPROWLO,x
        lda t16+1
        sta LV_MAPROWHI,x
        lda t16
        clc
        adc t16b
        sta t16
        lda t16+1
        adc t16b+1
        sta t16+1
        inx
        bne :-
        jmp pagelogic
proposal:
ldx #0
:       lda t16
        sta LV_MAPROWLO,x
        clc
        adc t16b
        sta t16
        lda t16+1
        sta LV_MAPROWHI,x
        adc t16b+1
        sta t16+1
        inx
        bne :-
        jmp pagelogic
argument: The loop stores t16 then reloads both halves to add t16b. Interleaving lets each half be stored and then added from the copy already in A, deleting two lda zp (2 x 3 cycles, 2 x 2 bytes). Low half: lda t16 (A = lo) / sta LV_MAPROWLO,x (sta affects no flags, so A survives) / clc / adc t16b / sta t16 - the stored table entry is the pre-increment value, as before. High half: lda t16+1 loads the OLD high byte (t16+1 has not been written yet) and stores it to LV_MAPROWHI,x, then adc t16b+1 completes the 16-bit add. The only correctness question is the carry from the low add: adc sets C, and the two instructions between it and the high adc are lda zp and sta abs,x, neither of which touches C (lda writes N and Z only, sta writes nothing), so the carry reaches the high adc intact. N/Z are not consumed anywhere in the body - the only branch is bne off inx. X is untouched by the reordering, and A is dead at the loop bottom. No anonymous labels added or removed (the one ':' and its bne :- are unchanged). Per iteration: 41 -> 35 cycles, and the loop runs 256 times per level init, so ~1536 cycles.

assumption: Applies to the unmirrored expansion of SPRFULL only (mirror = 0); the mirrored expansion is deliberately left alone. 'po' is declared .local at the top of SPRFULL and is defined exactly once in either arrangement.
original:
.if mirror
        lda MASKTAB+$80,x
        and (sp),y
        ora IDENT+$80,x
.else
        lda MASKTAB,x
        and (sp),y
        ora IDENT,x
.endif
        sta (sp),y
        bra ps
po:
.if mirror
        tax
        lda SWAPTAB,x
.endif
        sta (sp),y
ps:     cpy tmp2
proposal:
.if mirror
        lda MASKTAB+$80,x
        and (sp),y
        ora IDENT+$80,x
        sta (sp),y
        bra ps
po:     tax
        lda SWAPTAB,x
        sta (sp),y
.else
        lda MASKTAB,x
        and (sp),y
        ora IDENT,x
po:     sta (sp),y                  ; masked path falls into the shared store
.endif
ps:     cpy tmp2
argument: In the unmirrored expansion the 'po' block is nothing but 'sta (sp),y' - identical to the store the masked path has just reached. So the masked path currently emits its own copy of that store and then a 'bra ps' (3 cycles, 2 bytes) purely to jump over a duplicate of itself. Labelling the shared store 'po' and letting the masked path fall into it removes both: 3 cycles and 4 bytes off every masked byte in an unmirrored partial cell. The opaque path is untouched - 'bmi po' still lands on the same store instruction with A holding the source byte, and still falls through to ps. A, X, Y and the flags at ps are unchanged on both paths (ps starts with 'cpy tmp2', which sets its own flags). The mirrored case must keep the current shape: there 'po' really does have work of its own (tax / lda SWAPTAB,x), and the comment in SPRLINE puts opaque bytes at 45.7% against roughly 30% masked, so the opaque path is the one that should fall through. No anonymous labels are involved - po, ps, pl and pd are all .local named labels.

assumption: X is dead across these four instructions. Verified for this call site: in drawsprite X is last written by the `ldx #BANK_SPR`/`stx ROMSEL` bank select well above @vert and is not read again until `ldx curbuf` far below @ck; `jsr sext` (and #$80 / beq / lda #$FF / sta tmp3 / rts) does not touch X either. This is the one fact outside the window the rewrite needs.
original:
lda spy
        sec
        sbc (ptr),y
        sta w16
        lda spy+1
        sbc tmp3
        sta w16+1
        lda w16
        sec
        sbc wy
        sta w16
proposal:
lda spy
        sec
        sbc (ptr),y
        tax
        lda spy+1
        sbc tmp3
        sta w16+1
        txa
        sec
        sbc wy
        sta w16
argument: w16's low byte is stored and immediately reloaded across three instructions that never read it (`lda spy+1 / sbc tmp3 / sta w16+1`), and it is overwritten again by the final `sta w16`, so the first store is dead. Parking the intermediate in X replaces `sta w16`(3) + `lda w16`(3) with `tax`(2) + `txa`(2): 2 cycles and 4 bytes. Flags: `tax` sets N,Z from A where `sta` set none, but the very next instruction is `lda spy+1`, which sets its own N,Z - and crucially `tax` leaves C untouched, so the borrow from `sbc (ptr),y` still reaches `sbc tmp3` correctly. `txa` likewise sets N,Z, and is followed immediately by `sec`, so nothing downstream sees a changed flag. The `sec` before `sbc wy` is still required: the preceding `sbc tmp3` leaves the borrow of the first 16-bit subtraction in C. The folded alternative (form t+wy first, then subtract from spy) costs the same 42 cycles and needs two extra scratch bytes, so it is not worth it. Anonymous label count unchanged.

assumption: @reg is entered only by the `beq @reg` immediately above it. That is the only reference to it in the window, and grepping ob_tramp in logic.s confirms it is the only one in the routine.
original:
lsr
        lsr                         ; bounce frame 0..2
        ldx O_EL,y
        beq @reg
        clc
        adc #115
        sta q1
        jsr tramp_safe
        lda q1
        jmp m_addsprite
@reg:   clc
        adc #43
        jmp m_addsprite
proposal:
lsr
        lsr                         ; bounce frame 0..2
        clc                         ; hoisted: serves both arms
        ldx O_EL,y
        beq @reg
        adc #115
        sta q1
        jsr tramp_safe
        lda q1
        jmp m_addsprite
@reg:   adc #43
        jmp m_addsprite
argument: Both arms of the branch begin with the same `clc`, and nothing between the branch point and either `adc` can disturb carry, so one clc placed before the test serves both. Instruction by instruction: `lsr` leaves C = the bit shifted out, which is why a clc is needed at all; the hoisted `clc` clears it; `ldx O_EL,y` is an absolute-indexed load that writes only N and Z, not C; `beq @reg` reads the Z that ldx just set and writes nothing. So C = 0 at both `adc #115` and `adc #43`, exactly as before. The Z the branch consumes is still the one from `ldx O_EL,y` - clc does not touch Z, and it is placed before the ldx anyway, so the ordering of the flag producer and its consumer is unchanged. A is untouched by clc and ldx, so the accumulator carrying the 0..2 bounce frame reaches both adds intact. Net: two clc instructions become one - 2 cycles and 1 byte saved on whichever arm is taken, on every execution. No anonymous labels involved (@reg is a cheap-local).

assumption: None beyond the window: @mul is entered only by falling through the `lda sp_c / beq @rows` above it, so a `clc` placed between them runs exactly once per entry.
original:
lda sp_c
        beq @rows
@mul:   lda sp_col
        clc
        adc sp_lines
        sta sp_col
        bcc :+
        inc sp_col+1
:       dec sp_c
        bne @mul
proposal:
lda sp_c
        beq @rows
        clc
@mul:   lda sp_col
        adc sp_lines
        sta sp_col
        bcc :+
        inc sp_col+1
        clc
:       dec sp_c
        bne @mul
argument: Same carry-hoist as engine_1490, applied round a loop. On re-entry to @mul the carry is already 0 whenever `bcc :+` was taken, and `dec sp_c` / `bne` do not touch C, so the per-iteration `clc` is dead work on every iteration that did not carry. Moving it to the carry arm (where `inc sp_col+1` leaves C = 1 and it really is needed) and seeding it once before the loop makes the no-carry iteration lda (3) + adc (3) + sta (3) + bcc taken (3) + dec (5) + bne (3) = 20 cycles instead of 22, and leaves the carry iteration at 26 either way. Placing the seed `clc` after `beq @rows` is safe: the branch has already consumed the Z from `lda sp_c`, and CLC touches no other flag. The loop count is sp_c (the sprite's clipped start column), and sp_lines is the per-column source stride, so the low byte carries only about sp_lines/256 of the time -- the saving lands on nearly every iteration. Costs one byte (one clc removed from the loop, two added). The ca65 anonymous-label count is unchanged: the single `:` line stays, and `bcc :+` still resolves to it. The repeated-addition multiply itself is left alone -- replacing it is a redesign, not a re-encoding.

assumption: sp_c1 >= sp_c0, i.e. the clipped sprite rect has non-negative width. If that ever failed, `sbc sp_c0 / inca` would already be storing a nonsense width byte into the record, so the invariant is required by the surrounding code regardless.
original:
lda sp_c1
        sec
        sbc sp_c0
        inca
        sta (rp),y
        iny
        lda sp_r1
        sec
        sbc sp_r0
        inca
        ldx spclip
proposal:
lda sp_c1
        sec
        sbc sp_c0
        inca
        sta (rp),y
        iny
        lda sp_r1
        sbc sp_r0                   ; C still set by the width sbc above (sp_c1 >= sp_c0)
        inca
        ldx spclip
argument: The second `sec` is redundant if carry survives from the first subtraction. Chain it through: `sbc sp_c0` leaves C = 1 whenever no borrow occurred, which given sp_c1 >= sp_c0 is always; `inca` is 65C02 `inc a`, which sets only N and Z and leaves C untouched; `sta (rp),y` sets no flags; `iny` sets only N and Z; `lda sp_r1` sets only N and Z. So C = 1 reaches `sbc sp_r0` unchanged and the subtraction is identical. Saving is exactly the removed `sec`: 2 cycles, 1 byte, once per sprite record written. Everything else in the window is forced: the leading `clc / adc sp_r0` needs its clc because the preceding `adc #0` of the wcx+1 high-byte propagation leaves carry in an unknown state; `ldx spclip` rather than `lda spclip` is deliberate because A is carrying the height byte through to the `ora #$80` / `sta (rp),y` that follow, and `bit spclip` could not substitute since BIT takes Z from (A AND operand) and A here is the height, not spclip. Confidence is medium only because the sp_c1 >= sp_c0 invariant is not literally proved inside the window.

assumption: None for correctness. The saving applies only on the mirror path (sp_flags bit 0 set).
original:
lda sp_w
        deca
        sec
        sbc sp_c
        sta sp_c
proposal:
clc
        lda sp_w
        sbc sp_c                    ; C=0 subtracts the extra 1: sp_w - sp_c - 1
        sta sp_c
argument: sbc with C=0 subtracts operand+1, so `clc / lda sp_w / sbc sp_c` computes sp_w - sp_c - 1, which is bit-for-bit (sp_w - 1) - sp_c mod 256 -- the same value the `deca / sec / sbc` sequence produces. Cycles: clc(2)+lda zp(3)+sbc zp(3)+sta zp(3) = 11 against lda zp(3)+dec a(2)+sec(2)+sbc zp(3)+sta zp(3) = 13. Bytes: 1+2+2+2 = 7 against 2+1+1+2+2 = 8. Flags: the sbc in both versions performs the identical subtraction, so N, Z, V and C out are identical; the next instruction is `@nomirror: lda sp_flags`, which resets N and Z anyway, and the following `and #8 / beq :+` does not read C. Registers: A is loaded fresh from sp_w and Y (the record index) is untouched. NOTE on the rest of this window: `ldx spclip / beq :+ / ora #$80` must stay. spclip is not a bit-7 flag -- engine.s:1094 zeroes it and 1193/1211/1268/1276 each `inc` it, so it holds 0..4; both `ora spclip` and `bit spclip / bpl` would be wrong. The comment's 'bit 7' refers to the byte being stored into the record, not to spclip.

original:
lda tmp3
        cmp tmp4
        bcs @done                   ; it ends before the source row
        lda tmp4
        sec
        sbc tmp3
        sta tmp4
proposal:
lda tmp4
        sec
        sbc tmp3
        bcc @done                   ; it ends before the source row
        beq @done
        sta tmp4
argument: The original compares tmp3 against tmp4 and then, on the surviving path, performs the very subtraction the compare already implied: lda tmp3(3) cmp tmp4(3) bcs(2) lda tmp4(3) sec(2) sbc tmp3(3) sta tmp4(3) = 19 cycles, 13 bytes. Doing the subtraction first and branching on its flags gives lda tmp4(3) sec(2) sbc tmp3(3) bcc(2) beq(2) sta tmp4(3) = 15 cycles, 11 bytes: -4 cycles, -2 bytes. The three cases map exactly: tmp3 > tmp4 leaves C=0 -> bcc @done (original: bcs taken, since C set on cmp means A >= operand, i.e. tmp3 >= tmp4); tmp3 = tmp4 leaves C=1, Z=1 -> beq @done; tmp3 < tmp4 leaves C=1, Z=0 -> falls through and stores tmp4-tmp3, which is the same non-zero positive value the original stored. Both comparisons are unsigned in both versions, so the signed/unsigned hazard does not arise. tmp3 is not needed in A afterwards: on the fall-through path the next instruction is `lda MIRR_LO`, and @done begins with `pla`, so neither A nor the flags survive. This also removes the need for the `lda tmp3` that immediately follows the three lsr/ror pairs; the shifted result is read straight out of tmp3 as the sbc operand.

assumption: X is dead across this window. Verified in player_update: the last X use before it is `stx t16+1` around line 1337, and the next is `ldx vx+1` around line 1536, which loads X fresh; there is no jsr inside the window.
original:
lda frame
        sec
        sbc evframe
        sta t16
        lda frame+1
        sbc evframe+1
        bne @clrhurt                ; elapsed >= 256 -> clear
        lda t16
        cmp #65
        bcc @afterhurt
proposal:
lda frame
        sec
        sbc evframe
        tax                         ; hold the low byte of the delta in X
        lda frame+1
        sbc evframe+1
        bne @clrhurt                ; elapsed >= 256 -> clear
        cpx #65
        bcc @afterhurt
argument: t16 is used purely as a one-instruction-apart spill of the low byte of the unsigned delta frame - evframe. X can hold it instead. Instruction by instruction: `sta t16` (3 cycles / 2 bytes) becomes `tax` (2 / 1) -- `tax` sets N and Z from A, but the very next instruction is `lda frame+1` which overwrites both, and `tax` does not touch C, so the borrow from `sbc evframe` still reaches `sbc evframe+1` intact (rule 1). The `bne @clrhurt` still reads Z from `sbc evframe+1`, unchanged. `lda t16` (3 / 2) + `cmp #65` (2 / 2) becomes `cpx #65` (2 / 2): `cpx` performs the same unsigned compare and sets the same C for the following `bcc` (rule 4: still unsigned, as the comment requires for the 16-bit frame wrap), and the N/Z it leaves are not consumed. A is left holding the delta's high byte rather than its low byte, but @afterhurt starts `lda control` and @clrhurt starts `stz hurt`, so A is dead either way. Cycles: 3+3+2 = 8 becomes 2+2 = 4 on the fall-through path, saving 4; on the `bne @clrhurt` path only the sta->tax applies, saving 1. Bytes 2+2+2 = 6 becomes 1+2 = 3. The identical five-instruction pattern for `control` immediately below (sta t16 / ... / lda t16 / cmp #25) takes the same rewrite for another 4 cycles, but it lies outside this window.

original:
lda #$40                    ; drop any T1 tick that fired while we were in
        sta VIA_IFR                 ; here: it would step the chain on before the
        lda #0                      ; frame has even started, and the next section's
        sta SECIDX                  ; registers would land a frame early
proposal:
lda #$40                    ; drop any T1 tick that fired while we were in
        sta VIA_IFR                 ; here: it would step the chain on before the
        stz SECIDX                  ; frame has even started, and the next section's
                                    ; registers would land a frame early
argument: SECIDX is declared in the TABLES segment (engine.s:266), so it is absolute: `lda #0` (2) + `sta abs` (4) = 6 cycles / 5 bytes, while `stz abs` is 4 cycles / 3 bytes - hence 2 cycles and 1 byte (the comment block has to shift a line, which is why the byte count is 1 rather than 2). Flags: `lda #0` sets Z=1, N=0 and stz sets none, but the very next instruction in engine.s is `lda DISPSECT`, which rewrites N and Z before anything can read them, so no consumed flag changes. A: `lda #0` leaves A=0 and stz leaves A=$40; again `lda DISPSECT` overwrites A before any read, so A is dead here. Nothing else in the window can be cheapened - `lda #$40 / sta VIA_IFR` must write $40 specifically, and `lda #12 / sta CRTC_IDX` then `lda #13 / sta CRTC_IDX` cannot become `inc CRTC_IDX`, because the 6845 address register at $FE00 is write-only and a read-modify-write would feed it whatever the bus floats. Stronger option, flagged because it depends on two lines just outside the window: engine.s:3063-3064 immediately do `lda DISPSECT / sta SECIDX`, and the only reader of SECIDX anywhere is `ldx SECIDX` at engine.s:2953 at IRQ entry (the NMI handler at 3413 never touches it), so with interrupts masked inside the handler the whole `lda #0 / sta SECIDX` pair is a dead store and deleting it outright saves 6 cycles and 5 bytes. I am proposing only the in-window stz, which is unconditionally safe.

assumption: Y need not be 0 on the @end path. Verified: @end (engine.s:3139) is `stz SFXPTR+1 / lda #$DF / jsr sndwrite / lda #$FF / jsr sndwrite` and never reads Y. sndwrite must already preserve Y, since the existing code relies on that across all three calls.
original:
ldy #0
        lda (SFXPTR),y
        cmp #$FF
        beq @end
        jsr sndwrite
        iny
        lda (SFXPTR),y
        jsr sndwrite
        iny
        lda (SFXPTR),y
        jsr sndwrite
        iny
        lda (SFXPTR),y
        sta SFXDUR
proposal:
lda (SFXPTR)                ; 65C02 (zp): the first byte needs no index
        cmp #$FF
        beq @end
        jsr sndwrite
        ldy #1
        lda (SFXPTR),y
        jsr sndwrite
        iny
        lda (SFXPTR),y
        jsr sndwrite
        iny
        lda (SFXPTR),y
        sta SFXDUR
argument: `ldy #0`(2 cy, 2 bytes) + `lda (SFXPTR),y`(5 cy, 2 bytes) becomes `lda (SFXPTR)`(5 cy, 2 bytes) -- the same 65C02 mode the ldaz macro emits -- so the load costs the same and the ldy disappears. The first `iny`(2 cy, 1 byte) must then become `ldy #1`(2 cy, 2 bytes) to establish the index, which is cycle-neutral and one byte longer, leaving a net 2 cycles and 1 byte. Flags: `lda (zp)` sets N,Z from the loaded byte exactly as `lda (zp),y` with Y=0 did, and the consumer is `cmp #$FF / beq @end` immediately after. A is unchanged in value and is what sndwrite receives. The only behavioural difference is that on the $FF branch Y now holds whatever it held on entry instead of 0, which @end does not read. Runs at most once per sound tick, when SFXDUR expires.

original:
lda #$40
        sta VIA_IFR
        lda #0
        sta SECIDX
        lda DISPSECT
        sta SECIDX
proposal:
lda #$40
        sta VIA_IFR
        stz SECIDX
        lda DISPSECT
        sta SECIDX
argument: SECIDX is declared in the TABLES segment ($0400-$0CFF, engine.s:266), so it is an absolute operand: lda #0 (2 cycles, 2 bytes) + sta abs (4 cycles, 3 bytes) = 6 cycles / 5 bytes, against stz abs = 4 cycles / 3 bytes. Memory effect is identical (SECIDX gets $00, then DISPSECT). Registers: the lda #0 leaves A=0, but the very next instruction is lda DISPSECT, so that A is dead - nothing between the two stores reads it. Flags: lda #0 sets Z=1,N=0 and stz sets none, but the following lda DISPSECT overwrites N and Z before any branch, and the next flag consumer after that is inside jsr scan_keys. Carry is untouched by both forms. The pre-write of 0 is left in place deliberately - it is only two stores apart from the real one and I am not judging whether it is needed. Net 2 cycles, 2 bytes.

assumption: X is not live across this point: it is set to 0 here anyway, and the preceding add16 vx,t16 uses only A.
original:
lda q6
        ldx #0
        ora #0
        bpl :+
        dex
:       sta t16
        stx t16+1
proposal:
ldx #0
        lda q6                      ; N now comes from q6 itself
        bpl :+
        dex
:       sta t16
        stx t16+1
argument:
'ora #0' exists only to restore N after 'ldx #0' clobbered it (ldx #n sets N,Z from the immediate -- rule 1). Loading X first and q6 second makes the branch read the N that the load of q6 produced, so the ora disappears: 2 cycles, 2 bytes, on both the positive and negative paths. Semantics are identical -- t16 = q6, t16+1 = $00/$FF -- and Z/N at ':' are now from q6 rather than from q6 OR 0, which is the same value. Nothing between 'add16 vx, t16' and here reads X, so the reorder is safe. Anonymous label count unchanged.

Not proposed, but noted: the 'ldx #6 / : asr16 t16 / dex / bne :-' loop above costs 121 cycles and unrolls to 90, but that is +30 bytes and would delete an anonymous label for about 31 cycles once per frame -- I do not think it is worth the label churn.

assumption: Entry state at this point, both established by the three instructions immediately above the window at engine.s:800-802 (@dxpos: lda w16 / beq @dyc / cmp #ROWCHARS / bcs @full): A = dx with 1 <= dx <= ROWCHARS-1 = 79 (zero goes to @dyc, >= 80 goes to @full), and C = 0 - the existing code already relies on that carry, as its own comment 'not taken: C = 0 for the adc' says. No anonymous labels are added or removed.
original:
sta rc_w
        lda wcx
        adc #ROWCHARS
        sta rc_x
        lda wcx+1
        adc #0
        sta rc_x+1
        lda rc_x
        sec
        sbc rc_w
        sta rc_x
        bcs @docols
        dec rc_x+1
@docols:
        lda wcy
        sta rc_y
proposal:
sta rc_w
        eor #$FF                    ; A = 255 - rc_w, C still 0 from the cmp above
        adc #ROWCHARS               ; A = ROWCHARS-1-rc_w, C = 1 (rc_w <= 79)
        adc wcx                     ; + wcx + 1 -> wcx + ROWCHARS - rc_w
        sta rc_x
        lda wcx+1
        adc #0
        sta rc_x+1
@docols:
        lda wcy
        sta rc_y
argument: The original does a 16-bit add of ROWCHARS and then a separate 16-bit subtract of rc_w, each with its own high-byte fixup, and re-loads rc_x in between because A was spent on the high byte: sta rc_w(3) lda wcx(3) adc #ROWCHARS(2) sta rc_x(3) lda wcx+1(3) adc #0(2) sta rc_x+1(3) lda rc_x(3) sec(2) sbc rc_w(3) sta rc_x(3) bcs @docols(3) = 33 cycles / 25 bytes, or 35 when the borrow forces dec rc_x+1. Since the result is wcx + (ROWCHARS - rc_w) and A already holds rc_w, the whole thing collapses into one carry chain. eor #$FF gives 255 - rc_w and leaves C untouched at 0; adc #ROWCHARS then computes (255 - rc_w) + 80 + 0 = 335 - rc_w, which for rc_w in 1..79 is 256..334, so A = 79 - rc_w and C = 1 unconditionally; adc wcx then adds that carry back in, giving (79 - rc_w) + wcx + 1 = wcx + 80 - rc_w in A with the true carry out, which adc #0 propagates into the high byte. The result is bit-identical to the original 16-bit computation - checked against rc_w=1/wcx=$0123 -> $0172, rc_w=79/wcx=$00F0 -> $00F1, and rc_w=1/wcx=$00C0 -> $010F, that last one being the case where the low byte carries. The bcs @docols / dec rc_x+1 pair disappears entirely because ROWCHARS - rc_w is in 1..79 and so can never make the 16-bit sum go backwards; @docols is the next line, so nothing needs a branch to reach it. The other entry to @docols is the bra at engine.s:793 on the negative-dx path, which sets rc_x itself and is unaffected. New cost 3+2+2+3+3+3+2+3 = 21 cycles / 16 bytes. The rewrite does lean on 1 <= rc_w <= 79, which is why that is stated as an assumption: outside that range the 8-bit ROWCHARS - rc_w would wrap and the high byte would be off by 256.

assumption: Y is free across @addr. Checked in engine.s: the only code in build_sections that uses Y is @advance, which loads it with `tay` and consumes it as its own loop counter before falling into @wrap; no caller of @addr (@emit, the P2 block, @setq) holds anything in Y across the call.
original:
:       lda w16b
        clc
        adc #<CRTCBASE
        sta tmp
        lda w16b+1
        adc #>CRTCBASE
        sta SECTAB,x
        lda tmp
        sta SECTAB+1,x
        rts
proposal:
:       lda w16b
        clc
        adc #<CRTCBASE
        tay
        lda w16b+1
        adc #>CRTCBASE
        sta SECTAB,x
        tya
        sta SECTAB+1,x
        rts
argument: SECTAB stores the CRTC address high byte first, so the low byte computed first has to be parked somewhere across the high-byte add. It is parked in zero page (`sta tmp` 3, `lda tmp` 3); parking it in Y costs `tay` (2) and `tya` (2) instead -- 4 cycles for 6, and 2 bytes for 4. Neither TAY nor TYA touches the carry, so the `adc #>CRTCBASE` still receives the carry out of the low-byte add exactly as before; that is the whole reason the value had to be saved rather than recomputed. TYA does set N and Z from the transferred byte where `lda tmp` set them from the same byte, so even the flags out are identical; in any case the next instruction is `sta SECTAB+1,x` followed by `rts`, and `rts` reads no flags. X is untouched (it is the live SECTAB entry index). PHA/PLA would be the obvious alternative but costs 7 cycles against the 6 it replaces. The `txa / clc / adc #8 / tax` entry step elsewhere in the routine is genuinely 8 cycles well spent -- eight INX would be 16 -- and its `clc` is needed because the carry arriving from `jsr @addr`'s final `adc` is data-dependent.

original:
lda w16
        clc
        adc rc_w
        sta rc_w
        lda w16+1
        adc #0
        bne @none
        lda rc_w
        beq @none
        lda wcx
proposal:
lda w16
        clc
        adc rc_w
        sta rc_w
        beq @none                   ; Z is still the low sum: sta sets no flags
        lda w16+1
        adc #0                      ; branches do not touch C
        bne @none
        lda wcx
argument: adc rc_w already sets Z from the 8-bit sum, and sta rc_w sets no flags, so the zero test on the low byte is free at that point -- the later lda rc_w (3 cycles, 2 bytes) exists only because the code checks the high byte first and destroys A. Moving the beq up removes that reload. Carry safety: beq is a branch and leaves C untouched, so the adc #0 still consumes the carry out of adc rc_w. The sta is kept ahead of the beq so rc_w is written in exactly the same cases as before, which matters because the rel<0 path falls into @right and @right reads rc_w. Semantics are unchanged: the original rejects on {hi != 0} union {hi == 0 and lo == 0}; the new one rejects on {lo == 0} union {lo != 0 and hi != 0}; both sets are {hi != 0} union {lo == 0}.
